# Architecture decision records

Status: decision log for the specification. It records decisions, not what is built; what is built is measured on
[coverage/README.md](coverage/README.md).

This page records Quader's design decisions, one entry per decision: what forced it, what was
decided, what follows from it, which alternatives were weighed and where the specification states
it in full. The normative text lives on the [specification pages](spec/README.md); an entry here
summarizes and links, it never overrides a spec page. Questions stay on the page that raised them,
with their options, the choice and the rationale, and are only listed here, in the generated index
[Decisions by the development agent](#decisions-by-the-development-agent).

Every question on the spec pages has been decided, most of them by the development agent: for each
one it worked out the options, selected one of them and recorded the reasoning on the question's
page; the status line of a question decided by the owner, a planner or a builder says so. The owner
reviews the development agent's choices at the walkthrough of the first prototype and objects to whatever
he dislikes. Until then every entry outside the owner constraints carries the status *Decided by
the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough*, and development proceeds on it.

**Status values.**

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Accepted (owner constraint) | Fixed by the project owner ([owner constraints](spec/README.md#owner-constraints)). Not reopened by the spec pages or decided by the development agent; a page that finds one costly raises a question for the owner. |
| Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough | The design the spec pages build on: the invariants and every option the development agent selected from the options a question's page documents. Becomes *Accepted* when the owner confirms it at the walkthrough; an objection there leads to a new entry that supersedes it. |
| Accepted | Confirmed by the owner. |
| Superseded by ADR-*n* | Replaced; the entry stays for the record. |

**Rules for this log.** Numbers are assigned in order and never reused or renumbered. A changed
decision gets a new entry that supersedes the old one, and the old entry's status changes. When an
owner constraint changes the premise of an entry rather than a later decision replacing it, the
entry is updated in place, and its Context says when and what was replaced. When a
question is decided on its spec page, the decision either becomes a new entry or updates an entry;
the question's block names that entry or the entry names the question, and the index in
[Decisions by the development agent](#decisions-by-the-development-agent) lists it beside the question.
A question raised later gets its row there from the generator. Alternatives marked as considered here
are the ones the spec pages weighed, plus the obvious designs a reviewer would ask about; the
reasoning for each rejection is one line, the spec page holds the rest.

**Revision of 2026-10-28.** The owner added four constraints that cannot be deselected: high
availability on HA PostgreSQL, HA Valkey with Sentinel and S3
([ADR-092](#adr-092--high-availability-on-ha-postgresql-ha-valkey-with-sentinel-and-s3)),
horizontal scale with random request distribution, split roles and drains without outage
([ADR-093](#adr-093--horizontal-scale-random-distribution-split-roles-drains-without-outage)), a
configurable backup job that writes consistent backups to S3
([ADR-094](#adr-094--a-configurable-backup-job-writes-consistent-backups-to-s3)), and no
ReadWriteMany storage ([ADR-095](#adr-095--no-readwritemany-storage)). The development agent
checked every earlier decision against them:
- **Invariants updated in place.** INV-2, INV-3, INV-11, INV-12 and INV-13 changed under the new
  constraints, so their entries ([ADR-013](#adr-013--one-binary-roles-split-from-the-start-identical-replicas-per-role-inv-2),
  [ADR-014](#adr-014--postgresql-is-the-system-of-record-valkey-holds-only-shared-ephemeral-state-inv-3),
  [ADR-022](#adr-022--pull-through-proxy-semantics-inv-11),
  [ADR-023](#adr-023--high-availability-and-horizontal-scale-on-ha-postgresql-ha-valkey-and-s3-inv-12),
  [ADR-024](#adr-024--the-helm-chart-is-the-supported-deployment-inv-13)) record the revised rule,
  and each Context names what was replaced. The earlier decision "No Redis" is superseded.
- **Revisited questions.** A question whose choice was checked again carries a line "Revisited on
  2026-10-28" on its spec page. That line and the entry that lists the question say whether the
  choice changed.
- **New entries.** The new invariants INV-18 and INV-19 and the design choices of this revision are
  ADR-096 to ADR-123.

## Owner constraints

### ADR-001 · Backend in Go 1.27.3

**Status:** Accepted (owner constraint)

**Context.** The owner fixes the implementation language and version of the server.

**Decision.** The backend is written in Go and built with Go 1.27.3. INV-1 records the check made
on 2026-10-28: the local `go version` and the go.dev download list both showed go1.27.3 as the
current stable release. Patch releases of Go 1.27 are taken when they appear: 1.27.4 on 2026-11-11, because `govulncheck` reported
GO-2026-6859 in `net/http` of 1.27.3 ([INV-1](spec/README.md)).

**Consequences.** Libraries come from the Go ecosystem; the choices are decided in
[Q-ARCH-1](spec/architecture.md#q-arch-1--http-router) to [Q-ARCH-5](spec/architecture.md#q-arch-5--job-queue-implementation). The binary is statically linked without cgo ([R-ARCH-001](spec/architecture.md#r-arch-001--one-binary-identical-replicas-process-roles)).
The toolchain version is pinned in one place that local builds and CI both read; no build file
exists yet, so this is a rule for the first one.

**Alternatives considered.** None; set by the owner.

**Spec:** [owner constraints](spec/README.md#owner-constraints), [ADR-012](#adr-012--one-toolchain-one-image-inv-1), [R-ARCH-001](spec/architecture.md#r-arch-001--one-binary-identical-replicas-process-roles),
[R-ARCH-003](spec/architecture.md#r-arch-003--go-module-and-package-layout).

### ADR-002 · Frontend in Angular 22

**Status:** Accepted (owner constraint)

**Context.** The owner fixes the UI framework and its major version.

**Decision.** The UI is an Angular 22 application. On 2026-10-28 the npm dist-tag `latest` of
`@angular/core` was 22.2.3 (INV-1).

**Consequences.** The UI follows Angular 22's defaults: standalone components, zoneless change
detection, signals ([R-UI-001](spec/api-and-ui.md#r-ui-001--technology-baseline-and-delivery), [R-UI-046](spec/api-and-ui.md#r-ui-046--state-management-with-signals)). UI dependencies should release in step with
Angular majors, which decided [Q-UI-1](spec/api-and-ui.md#q-ui-1--component-library) (Angular Material, the CDK and `@angular/aria`) and [Q-UI-5](spec/api-and-ui.md#q-ui-5--internationalization-mechanism) (`@angular/localize`). A new Angular major is planned work that
upgrades the framework and its companion packages together.

**Alternatives considered.** None; set by the owner.

**Spec:** [owner constraints](spec/README.md#owner-constraints), [ADR-012](#adr-012--one-toolchain-one-image-inv-1), [R-ARCH-004](spec/architecture.md#r-arch-004--angular-workspace-layout),
[R-UI-001](spec/api-and-ui.md#r-ui-001--technology-baseline-and-delivery).

### ADR-003 · PostgreSQL as the database

**Status:** Accepted (owner constraint)

**Context.** The owner fixes the database.

**Decision.** All metadata is stored in PostgreSQL.

**Consequences.** [ADR-014](#adr-014--postgresql-is-the-system-of-record-valkey-holds-only-shared-ephemeral-state-inv-3) (INV-3) makes PostgreSQL the system of record, including every
mutual exclusion whose failure would corrupt data, while HA Valkey holds only shared ephemeral
state ([ADR-092](#adr-092--high-availability-on-ha-postgresql-ha-valkey-with-sentinel-and-s3), [ADR-023](#adr-023--high-availability-and-horizontal-scale-on-ha-postgresql-ha-valkey-and-s3-inv-12)). Decided:
PostgreSQL 16 is the version floor ([Q-HA-2](spec/ha-and-helm.md#q-ha-2--postgresql-version-floor)), and the driver is pgx's native API
([Q-ARCH-2](spec/architecture.md#q-arch-2--postgresql-driver-and-query-layer)). Since the revision of 2026-10-28, a transaction-mode connection pooler is supported for
the main pool from the MVP on, with a direct session host for the leases of `worker` replicas,
`quader migrate` and `quader backup`, and a control endpoint of its own; statement-mode poolers are
not supported ([Q-HA-6](spec/ha-and-helm.md#q-ha-6--transaction-mode-connection-poolers), [Q-HA-20](spec/ha-and-helm.md#q-ha-20--control-connection-behind-a-transaction-mode-pooler), [ADR-101](#adr-101--connection-model-a-transaction-scoped-main-pool-behind-an-optional-pooler-sessions-only-on-workers)).

**Alternatives considered.** None; set by the owner.

**Spec:** [owner constraints](spec/README.md#owner-constraints), [R-HA-013](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-013--supported-postgresql-versions-and-server-settings), [R-HA-014](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-014--database-provisioning-roles-and-privileges).

### ADR-004 · S3 as binary storage

**Status:** Accepted (owner constraint)

**Context.** The owner fixes where package binaries live.

**Decision.** Binaries are stored in S3-compatible object storage.

**Consequences.** [ADR-015](#adr-015--content-addressed-blob-store-on-s3-inv-4) (INV-4) lays the store out by content address. Every supported store
must pass a conformance check ([R-STOR-035](spec/storage.md#r-stor-035--object-store-consistency-assumptions-and-conformance-check)). Decided: the client library is aws-sdk-go-v2 `service/s3`
with a Quader-owned multipart upload ([Q-ARCH-4](spec/architecture.md#q-arch-4--s3-client-library)), and the local development profile and per-change CI
run SeaweedFS, with the MinIO leg on every change and AWS S3 once an AWS account exists (owner decision of 2026-10-29, [ADR-130](#adr-130--the-organisations-ci-and-release-standard); [Q-HA-3](spec/ha-and-helm.md#q-ha-3--s3-component-of-the-local-profile-after-minios-archival)). Backups go to an S3 target of their own,
outside the blob prefix ([ADR-094](#adr-094--a-configurable-backup-job-writes-consistent-backups-to-s3), [ADR-112](#adr-112--the-backup-cronjob-is-off-by-default-and-needs-its-own-target-when-turned-on)), and multi-request uploads keep their
data in S3 multipart uploads rather than on a replica ([ADR-096](#adr-096--no-state-between-requests-on-a-replica-inv-18)).

**Alternatives considered.** None; set by the owner.

**Spec:** [owner constraints](spec/README.md#owner-constraints), [R-STOR-030](spec/storage.md#r-stor-030--object-store-connection-and-bucket-settings), [R-STOR-035](spec/storage.md#r-stor-035--object-store-consistency-assumptions-and-conformance-check).

### ADR-005 · High availability

**Status:** Accepted (owner constraint)

**Context.** Quader sits on the build path of every pipeline that installs or publishes
packages; an outage stops builds.

**Decision.** Quader runs highly available: losing one replica does not interrupt service.

**Consequences.** Replicas of a role are identical and keep no state between requests ([ADR-013](#adr-013--one-binary-roles-split-from-the-start-identical-replicas-per-role-inv-2),
[ADR-096](#adr-096--no-state-between-requests-on-a-replica-inv-18)) and coordinate through PostgreSQL and Valkey ([ADR-023](#adr-023--high-availability-and-horizontal-scale-on-ha-postgresql-ha-valkey-and-s3-inv-12)). On 2026-10-28 the owner made
the constraint concrete and non-negotiable: HA PostgreSQL, HA Valkey with Sentinel and S3
([ADR-092](#adr-092--high-availability-on-ha-postgresql-ha-valkey-with-sentinel-and-s3)), a load beyond one replica with drains at any time ([ADR-093](#adr-093--horizontal-scale-random-distribution-split-roles-drains-without-outage)). Three pages decided the same readiness rule for an object-storage outage:
object storage gates only a replica's first readiness, so running replicas stay ready during a
shared outage ([Q-STOR-1](spec/storage.md#q-stor-1--readiness-tied-to-object-storage-reachability-inv-12), [Q-OPS-2](spec/operations-and-observability.md#q-ops-2--should-object-storage-reachability-gate-readiness), [Q-HA-1](spec/ha-and-helm.md#q-ha-1--readiness-on-object-storage-failure)).

**Alternatives considered.** None; set by the owner.

**Spec:** [owner constraints](spec/README.md#owner-constraints), [R-HA-001](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-001--active-active-replicas-without-a-primary-node), [R-HA-007](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-007--failure-mode-contract).

### ADR-006 · Deployment through a Helm chart

**Status:** Accepted (owner constraint)

**Context.** The owner fixes the deployment mechanism.

**Decision.** Quader is deployed to Kubernetes with a Helm chart.

**Consequences.** [ADR-024](#adr-024--the-helm-chart-is-the-supported-deployment-inv-13) (INV-13) makes the chart the supported deployment and fixes what it
renders; since 2026-10-28 that is one Deployment per role, the backup CronJob and no ReadWriteMany
volume ([ADR-093](#adr-093--horizontal-scale-random-distribution-split-roles-drains-without-outage) to [ADR-095](#adr-095--no-readwritemany-storage)). Decided: the HTTPRoute is MVP and a chart-created Gateway P1 ([Q-HA-7](spec/ha-and-helm.md#q-ha-7--priority-of-gateway-api)), and images and
chart are published to Docker Hub and to the GitHub Pages chart repository (owner decision of 2026-10-29, [ADR-130](#adr-130--the-organisations-ci-and-release-standard); [Q-HA-11](spec/ha-and-helm.md#q-ha-11--publishing-location-of-images-and-chart), which named `ghcr.io` before it).

**Alternatives considered.** None; set by the owner.

**Spec:** [owner constraints](spec/README.md#owner-constraints), [R-HA-028](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-028--chart-scope-rendered-resources-and-naming), [R-HA-031](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-031--values-reference).

### ADR-007 · OIDC login, own tokens, detailed permissions

**Status:** Accepted (owner constraint)

**Context.** The owner requires single sign-on for people, credentials for package clients, and
fine-grained permission management.

**Decision.** Users log in through OpenID Connect; Quader issues tokens; permissions are managed
in detail.

**Consequences.** Spelled out by [ADR-018](#adr-018--humans-authenticate-only-through-an-external-oidc-provider-inv-7) (INV-7, human identity), [ADR-019](#adr-019--quader-issues-opaque-prefixed-tokens-inv-8) (INV-8,
tokens) and [ADR-020](#adr-020--deny-by-default-allow-only-permission-policies-inv-9) (INV-9, authorization).

**Alternatives considered.** None; set by the owner.

**Spec:** [owner constraints](spec/README.md#owner-constraints),
[identity-and-authentication.md](spec/identity-and-authentication.md),
[authorization.md](spec/authorization.md).

### ADR-008 · GitLab CI jobs obtain permissions through OIDC

**Status:** Accepted (owner constraint)

**Context.** CI jobs install dependencies and publish what they build. Long-lived secrets in CI
variables leak and are rarely rotated.

**Decision.** A GitLab CI job obtains Quader permissions through an OIDC procedure. The
permissions are detailed and configurable: read other packages, write the packages the job
produces.

**Consequences.** Spelled out by [ADR-021](#adr-021--gitlab-ci-identity-through-id-token-exchange-inv-10) (INV-10) and the CI entries [ADR-059](#adr-059--ci-tokens-through-a-standard-token-exchange-endpoint) to
[ADR-065](#adr-065--further-ci-issuers-through-the-same-mechanism-p1). "Write the packages the job produces" needs package ownership ([ADR-056](#adr-056--package-ownership-is-decided-by-the-first-publish)).

**Alternatives considered.** None; set by the owner.

**Spec:** [owner constraints](spec/README.md#owner-constraints),
[gitlab-ci-oidc.md](spec/gitlab-ci-oidc.md).

### ADR-009 · Pull-through proxy for external package sources

**Status:** Accepted (owner constraint)

**Context.** Builds depend on public registries; the owner wants them connected through Quader.

**Decision.** External package sources can be connected as pull-through proxies.

**Consequences.** Spelled out by [ADR-022](#adr-022--pull-through-proxy-semantics-inv-11) (INV-11) and [ADR-035](#adr-035--virtual-resolution-in-three-tiers-decided-per-member) to [ADR-039](#adr-039--egress-address-checks-after-dns-resolution-for-every-remote-connection).

**Alternatives considered.** None; set by the owner.

**Spec:** [owner constraints](spec/README.md#owner-constraints),
[repositories-and-proxy.md](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md).

### ADR-010 · Every catalog format, npm and NuGet first

**Status:** Accepted (owner constraint)

**Context.** The owner wants every package format of the [feature catalog](features/formats/README.md)
and welcomes more, with npm and NuGet first.

**Decision.** Quader targets every catalog format. npm and NuGet are the first formats and the
only ones in the MVP.

**Consequences.** [ADR-025](#adr-025--npm-and-nuget-v3-are-the-mvp-formats-inv-14) (INV-14) fixes the MVP clients. The format plug-in contract
([ADR-029](#adr-029--formats-are-compiled-in-plug-ins-behind-a-narrow-host-interface)) keeps later formats from touching the core. Later formats already constrain today's
URL layout: `/v2/` on the client listener is reserved for OCI ([Q-HA-4](spec/ha-and-helm.md#q-ha-4--reserve-v2-on-the-client-listener-for-oci)).

**Alternatives considered.** None; set by the owner.

**Spec:** [owner constraints](spec/README.md#owner-constraints),
[formats/npm.md](spec/formats/npm.md), [formats/nuget.md](spec/formats/nuget.md).

### ADR-011 · Quader is a self-contained, white-label product

**Status:** Accepted (owner constraint)

**Context.** The owner requires Quader to stand as its own product, described in its own terms.

**Decision.** Everything in the repository (documentation, code, configuration, examples, commit
messages) uses Quader's own vocabulary. It names no other repository product as model or origin,
links to no such product's documentation, and reuses none of its endpoint paths, header names,
field or property names, configuration file names, default ports or edition names. Third-party
standards and ecosystems are named and linked, with their native client commands: npm, NuGet,
OCI, Docker, Maven, PyPI, GitLab, GitHub Actions, Kubernetes, Helm, S3, PostgreSQL, the OIDC and
OAuth RFCs. The design questions that asked the owner for an example screenshot
([Q-UI-2](spec/api-and-ui.md#q-ui-2--visual-direction-of-the-shell-example-screenshot-requested), [Q-UI-3](spec/api-and-ui.md#q-ui-3--layout-of-the-package-details-page-example-screenshot-requested), [Q-UI-4](spec/api-and-ui.md#q-ui-4--layout-of-the-policy-editor-and-the-explainer-example-screenshot-requested)) were decided without one; the owner's walkthrough takes its place.
A screenshot the owner brings there adjusts design tokens and spacing, is described in Quader's own
terms, and its origin is not recorded.

**Consequences.** The [feature catalog](features/README.md) uses its own IDs and generic names,
and protocol behavior is specified from the ecosystems' own specifications and client sources,
which the spec pages cite. A check for forbidden references cannot live in the repository: its
pattern list would itself name what it forbids. It has to run from outside the repository, for
example from a CI variable or the review tooling. Not verified: no such check exists in the
repository today.

**Alternatives considered.** None; set by the owner.

**Spec:** not yet listed among the [owner constraints](spec/README.md#owner-constraints) of
spec/README.md, which should add it in its next change; [Q-UI-2](spec/api-and-ui.md#q-ui-2--visual-direction-of-the-shell-example-screenshot-requested).

### ADR-092 · High availability on HA PostgreSQL, HA Valkey with Sentinel and S3

**Status:** Accepted (owner constraint)

**Context.** On 2026-10-28 the owner stated that high availability of Quader on HA PostgreSQL, HA
Valkey including Sentinel, and S3 is a core requirement that cannot be deselected. It makes
[ADR-005](#adr-005--high-availability) concrete and adds Valkey to the services that [ADR-003](#adr-003--postgresql-as-the-database) and [ADR-004](#adr-004--s3-as-binary-storage) fixed.

**Decision.** Quader runs highly available on HA PostgreSQL, HA Valkey with Sentinel and
S3-compatible object storage. The requirement cannot be deselected: no supported production
configuration leaves out one of the three or runs PostgreSQL or Valkey as a single instance.

**Consequences.**
- **Topology.** INV-12 names it: HA PostgreSQL (for example CloudNativePG, Patroni or a managed
  service), Valkey with one primary, at least one replica and at least three Sentinels, and S3.
  Quader finds the Valkey primary through Sentinel and follows failovers. Single instances serve
  development only, and the local profile itself runs PostgreSQL with a standby and Valkey with a
  replica and three Sentinels ([ADR-023](#adr-023--high-availability-and-horizontal-scale-on-ha-postgresql-ha-valkey-and-s3-inv-12), [R-HA-051](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-051--local-development-profile)).
- **What Valkey may hold.** INV-3 limits Valkey to shared ephemeral state whose loss costs
  performance, never correctness or data ([ADR-014](#adr-014--postgresql-is-the-system-of-record-valkey-holds-only-shared-ephemeral-state-inv-3), [ADR-098](#adr-098--valkey-holds-coordination-and-the-negative-cache-nothing-served-and-nothing-that-grants)). The earlier decision "No Redis"
  is superseded.
- **Degradation.** A Valkey outage degrades Quader and is alerted on, but makes no replica unready
  ([ADR-100](#adr-100--valkey-degrades-quader-but-never-gates-readiness-except-for-configuration-errors)). The client and the supported server versions are [ADR-099](#adr-099--valkey-client-valkey-go-against-valkey-90-and-later-sentinel-in-production).
- **Chart.** The chart consumes the three services and bundles no production instance of any
  ([ADR-024](#adr-024--the-helm-chart-is-the-supported-deployment-inv-13)).

**Alternatives considered.** None; set by the owner.

**Spec:** [owner constraints](spec/README.md#owner-constraints), [INV-3, INV-12](spec/README.md#design-invariants),
[R-ARCH-030](spec/architecture.md#r-arch-030--valkey-usage-map), [R-ARCH-031](spec/architecture.md#r-arch-031--valkey-client-sentinel-discovery-tls-acl-and-degradation), [R-HA-056](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-056--valkey-with-sentinel-connection-and-supported-topologies), [R-HA-057](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-057--valkey-failover-outage-and-degraded-mode).

### ADR-093 · Horizontal scale: random distribution, split roles, drains without outage

**Status:** Accepted (owner constraint)

**Context.** On 2026-10-28 the owner stated the load model: n workers answer requests that a
Kubernetes Service distributes at random, and the expected load exceeds what one worker can carry.

**Decision.** Quader runs as n replicas that answer randomly distributed requests behind a
Kubernetes Service. The service is cut for load sharing from the start. A node drain causes no
outage at any time when the setup is sized for it. There may be more than one type of worker, and
the service may be split.

**Consequences.**
- **Roles from the start.** `web` and `worker` run as separate Deployments; `all` exists only for a
  binary started outside the chart in development ([ADR-013](#adr-013--one-binary-roles-split-from-the-start-identical-replicas-per-role-inv-2), [ADR-104](#adr-104--subsystems-per-role-web-serves-worker-owns-background-work-and-leases)). Further splits into pools
  are values, not code ([R-HA-062](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-062--further-splits-of-a-role-into-several-deployments), P1).
- **No affinity.** No request may depend on state that an earlier request left on one replica
  (INV-18, [ADR-096](#adr-096--no-state-between-requests-on-a-replica-inv-18)).
- **Connections.** PostgreSQL connections must not grow without bound with the replica count
  ([ADR-101](#adr-101--connection-model-a-transaction-scoped-main-pool-behind-an-optional-pooler-sessions-only-on-workers)).
- **Budgets, not per-replica values.** A limit an operator sets holds for the installation: rate
  limits ([ADR-102](#adr-102--cluster-wide-rate-limits-in-valkey-with-a-per-replica-fallback)) and the upstream fetch budget ([ADR-022](#adr-022--pull-through-proxy-semantics-inv-11)).
- **Drains.** The shutdown protocol ([ADR-103](#adr-103--shutdown-protocol-drain-delay-transfers-cut-at-the-deadline-resumed-on-any-replica)) and the capacity rule with its defaults ([ADR-105](#adr-105--drain-capacity-one-replica-more-than-the-peak-needs-per-role))
  define what "sized for it" means ([R-HA-059](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-059--node-drain-without-outage)).
- **Caches on n replicas.** They stay correct through the change log in PostgreSQL ([ADR-031](#adr-031--caches-validate-themselves-notifications-only-evict-early),
  [ADR-057](#adr-057--a-compiled-grant-index-per-replica-consistent-through-an-epoch-failing-closed), [ADR-114](#adr-114--authentication-caches-answer-only-while-the-change-log-is-fresh)).

**Alternatives considered.** None; set by the owner.

**Spec:** [owner constraints](spec/README.md#owner-constraints), [INV-2, INV-12, INV-18](spec/README.md#design-invariants),
[R-ARCH-001](spec/architecture.md#r-arch-001--one-binary-identical-replicas-process-roles), [R-ARCH-024](spec/architecture.md#r-arch-024--process-lifecycle-start-up-readiness-graceful-shutdown), [R-HA-002](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-002--role-split-into-api-packages-and-worker-deployments), [R-HA-059](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-059--node-drain-without-outage), [R-HA-062](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-062--further-splits-of-a-role-into-several-deployments).

### ADR-094 · A configurable backup job writes consistent backups to S3

**Status:** Accepted (owner constraint)

**Context.** Point-in-time recovery of the database and versioning of the bucket protect the two
stores separately, through the platform. On 2026-10-28 the owner asked for a backup job like
GitLab's: configurable, and producing a consistent backup of the service in S3 whenever it runs.

**Decision.** A configurable backup job creates a consistent backup of the service when it runs
and stores it in S3.

**Consequences.**
- **INV-19.** The job is `quader backup create`: a transactionally consistent snapshot of Quader's
  PostgreSQL data together with every blob it references, written to a configurable S3 target. The
  chart schedules it as a CronJob, and `quader backup restore` restores into an empty installation
  ([ADR-097](#adr-097--consistent-backups-to-s3-restored-into-an-empty-installation-inv-19)).
- **MVP.** Backup creation and restore are MVP, although the catalog ranks them P1 and P2. The
  revocation journal and the platform layer moved to MVP with them ([Q-HA-9](spec/ha-and-helm.md#q-ha-9--making-revocations-survive-a-database-restore-h-37), [Q-HA-19](spec/ha-and-helm.md#q-ha-19--priority-of-the-platform-backup-layer-and-the-point-in-time-restore),
  [ADR-078](#adr-078--restores-keep-metadata-and-blobs-consistent-by-ordering-not-by-coordination)).
- **Design.** Format and garbage-collection protection, runs, credentials, encryption, restore and
  the CronJob default are [ADR-106](#adr-106--backup-format-a-quader-native-snapshot-export-a-shared-blob-pool-and-a-garbage-collection-hold) to [ADR-112](#adr-112--the-backup-cronjob-is-off-by-default-and-needs-its-own-target-when-turned-on). Valkey is not part of a backup (INV-3).

**Alternatives considered.** None; set by the owner.

**Spec:** [owner constraints](spec/README.md#owner-constraints), [INV-19](spec/README.md#design-invariants),
[backup-and-restore.md](spec/backup-and-restore.md), [R-HA-060](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-060--backup-cronjob-and-restore-job).

### ADR-095 · No ReadWriteMany storage

**Status:** Accepted (owner constraint)

**Context.** On 2026-10-28 the owner stated that the clusters Quader targets offer no storage class
whose volumes several pods can attach at once.

**Decision.** No ReadWriteMany storage class can be assumed, so no volume may be attached to
several pods. A worker type that needs a ReadWriteOnce volume is acceptable, but not desired.

**Consequences.**
- **Nothing to share.** No pod mounts a volume that another pod writes, and nothing a service needs
  lives on a Quader volume: PostgreSQL holds metadata, S3 holds blobs, backups and the revocation
  journal, Valkey holds ephemeral state ([R-HA-061](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-061--volumes-nothing-shared-nothing-persistent)).
- **Scratch only.** Spool and temporary space are `emptyDir` or a generic ephemeral volume
  (ReadWriteOnce, deleted with its pod). The chart renders no PersistentVolumeClaim, no StatefulSet
  and no `volumeClaimTemplates`, its schema admits only `ReadWriteOnce` and `ReadWriteOncePod`, and
  CI checks the rendered output (INV-13, [ADR-024](#adr-024--the-helm-chart-is-the-supported-deployment-inv-13)). No role needs a persistent volume today.
- **No hand-over through a disk.** A cut remote fetch starts over on another replica
  ([Q-REPO-7](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-7--remote-fetches-on-a-replica-that-is-shutting-down)), a cut download resumes from S3 with `Range` ([ADR-103](#adr-103--shutdown-protocol-drain-delay-transfers-cut-at-the-deadline-resumed-on-any-replica)), and a
  multi-request upload keeps its bytes in an S3 multipart upload ([ADR-096](#adr-096--no-state-between-requests-on-a-replica-inv-18)).
- **Outside the chart.** The ReadWriteOnce claims of the PostgreSQL instances belong to their
  operator.

**Alternatives considered.** None; set by the owner.

**Spec:** [owner constraints](spec/README.md#owner-constraints), [INV-13](spec/README.md#design-invariants),
[R-HA-035](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-035--spool-and-temporary-volumes), [R-HA-061](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-061--volumes-nothing-shared-nothing-persistent).

### ADR-124 · Releases stay on major version 0

**Status:** Accepted (owner constraint); changed by the owner on 2026-10-31

**Context.** On 2026-10-29 the owner set the release numbering: development starts with `v0.1.0`,
and there is no major release until the owner explicitly decides otherwise. On 2026-10-31 the owner
decided that no fixed version number is expected for the beta.

**Decision.** Quader releases stay on major version 0 until the owner says otherwise. Semantic Release
cuts every release from the conventional commits on `main`
([ADR-130](#adr-130--the-organisations-ci-and-release-standard)); no project phase, milestone or the
beta has a version number expected beforehand. A phase of [docs/projektplan/](projektplan/BETA.md)
closes with the release cut from the commits that close it, and BETA.md's Version column records that
release once it is published. The beta release is the release cut from the commits that close phase 8.
The Helm chart follows the same numbering.

**Consequences.** Semantic Versioning would allow any change within 0.x; Quader does not use that
latitude. The promises of [R-ARCH-025](spec/architecture.md#r-arch-025--versioning-and-compatibility-policy)
apply between 0.x minors as they would within a major: direct upgrade to any later minor, rolling
upgrade without downtime from N-1 to N, deprecated configuration aliases for at least two minors. A
breaking change in 0.x is announced in the release notes together with its migration path. The
roadmap and the project plans name releases by the phase or milestone they close, never by an
expected number.

**Changed on 2026-10-31.** The owner decided that no fixed version number is expected for the beta.
Until then this entry said that every completed phase is released as the next minor version, with
`v0.7.0` for the beta, and the plans expected the beta candidate as `v0.7.0`, the beta as `v0.8.0` and
the releases after it from `v0.9.0` on. Semantic Release had meanwhile cut `v0.2.0`, `v0.3.0` and
`v0.4.0` (2026-10-29 and 2026-10-30) while phase 3 was still open, so a phase is not one minor version.

**Alternatives considered.** None; set by the owner.

**Spec:** [owner constraints](spec/README.md#owner-constraints), [R-ARCH-025](spec/architecture.md#r-arch-025--versioning-and-compatibility-policy),
[roadmap](coverage/roadmap.md#milestones-at-a-glance).

### ADR-153 · Quader is cut into task areas: roles of one binary, network seams only at trust or load boundaries

**Status:** Accepted (owner decision of 2026-11-04); changed by the owner the same day: no fetch service; the cut itself is [ADR-155](#adr-155--three-roles-api-packages-and-worker-variants-are-pools)

**Context.** Until now Quader ran two pod types, `web` and `worker`
([ADR-013](#adr-013--one-binary-roles-split-from-the-start-identical-replicas-per-role-inv-2),
[ADR-104](#adr-104--subsystems-per-role-web-serves-worker-owns-background-work-and-leases)). Both were
decisions of the development agent awaiting the owner's review; the owner's own constraint
([ADR-093](#adr-093--horizontal-scale-random-distribution-split-roles-drains-without-outage)) allows more
than one type of worker and a split service, and further splits existed only as pools of the same two
roles (R-HA-062, P1, not built). On 2026-11-04, before phase 6b would have put the background mirror
sync on `worker` as well, the owner asked for options to cut Quader into microservices so that it scales
better, and chose among four:

| Option | What it is | Scaling gain | Cost | Risk to existing guarantees |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (a) More roles, one binary | Roles by load profile (UI and management, package protocols, workers per queue), each its own Deployment, autoscaler, disruption budget and network policy; one database | Independent scaling and drains; a package surge cannot starve the UI, the advisory sync cannot starve maintenance | Small: roles are data (`SubsystemsFor`, the wiring areas), the chart and path routing | None |
| **(b) (a) plus network seams at trust or load boundaries** | As (a), and an internal upstream fetch service, the only pod type that contacts upstream registries (dropped, see below) | (a), and the egress address rules of R-REPO-038 and the upstream credentials held by one pod type, client-first priority decided in one service, the detached fetch of a draining `web` replica gone | Medium: one internal API over mutual TLS, a further hop on a cache miss | Low |
| (c) Control and data plane with separate data access | The data plane reads PostgreSQL read replicas, writes go through the control plane's API | Less load on the primary | Large | High: the authentication caches refuse on a stale change log ([ADR-114](#adr-114--authentication-caches-answer-only-while-the-change-log-is-fresh)), a lagging replica serves revoked access or refuses |
| (d) Domain microservices with their own databases | Identity, authorization, repository configuration, a service per format, blobs, vulnerabilities, audit; APIs and events between them | Independent releases; no throughput gain for the measured bottlenecks | Very large | High: the publish commit holds item, claims and audit event in one transaction; R-ARCH-027's one statement per download becomes several network hops; one image (ADR-012) ends |

**Decision.** Option (b). Quader stays one binary and one image; a task area is a role, a set of wiring
areas enabled as data, and runs as its own Deployment. Where a role needs a further variant of the same
subsystems (paths, queues) it is a pool of that role (R-HA-062). A network seam between roles is added
only where a trust or load boundary requires it. The Bastion (M13) is the existing seam of this kind at
the exposure boundary; no further seam is decided. Seams are guarded by ingress rules on the receiving
pods ([ADR-154](#adr-154--network-policies-are-ingress-rules-between-the-charts-pods-each-with-its-port)).

**Changed on 2026-11-04.** This entry first named an upstream fetch service as the first seam: the only
role that contacts upstream registries. Checked against the owner's constraints, its gains did not hold,
and the owner dropped it the same day:
- egress isolation: under ADR-154 no pod's egress is restricted, and the address policy of R-REPO-038 is
  code that holds the same in every role;
- upstream credentials in one role: every role builds the key ring (`AreaKeyRing` in
  `internal/app/steps.go`) and reads the same database, so a compromised serving pod holds more than the
  upstream passwords anyway;
- client-first priority in one place: the fetch service would need several replicas too, and the
  priority across replicas is the same distributed problem (Q-ARCH-286 solves it without a seam);
- the detached fetch of a draining replica: it moves to the fetch pod and adds a stream that can break
  between two roles.
Its costs stood: a further TLS hop on every miss, an internal API kept compatible across rolling
upgrades (R-ARCH-025) with mutual TLS identities that rotate without restart, a cut through the proxy
engine's flight, fill hooks and ingest, and a new path on which every miss fails. One exit to the
internet, where an operator wants it, is the outbound proxy of R-REPO-037.

**Consequences.** ADR-013 and ADR-104 are revised by the cut decision that follows this one; R-ARCH-001,
R-HA-002 and R-HA-062 are rewritten with it. PostgreSQL stays the system of record of every role, and the
transactions that hold security guarantees stay in one database. The measured bottlenecks (the CPU
profile of the npm load in [BETA.md](projektplan/BETA.md) phase 7, the statement count of F-41) are work
per request and stay with the roles that serve them.

**Revisit condition.** The PostgreSQL primary is measured as the bottleneck (write load or connection
budget), or separate teams own formats: then a cut with data of its own, option (d) for that area, is
weighed again. A fetch service is weighed again when a security rule requires the upstream credentials
to leave the pods that read the database, or a single exit is required that the outbound proxy of
R-REPO-037 cannot provide.

**Alternatives considered.** (a), (c) and (d) above.

**Spec:** [owner constraints](spec/README.md#owner-constraints),
[R-ARCH-001](spec/architecture.md#r-arch-001--one-binary-identical-replicas-process-roles),
[R-HA-002](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-002--role-split-into-api-packages-and-worker-deployments),
[R-HA-062](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-062--further-splits-of-a-role-into-several-deployments).

### ADR-154 · Network policies are ingress rules between the chart's pods, each with its port

**Status:** Accepted (owner constraint of 2026-11-04); governs both charts, `quader` and `quader-bastion`, by the owner's
decision of 2026-11-05

**Context.** The chart renders ingress-only policies for `web` and `worker`
([R-HA-042](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-042--network-policies)); the specification also planned an optional
egress policy (off by default, Q-HA-10, gap H-41). With the cut into task areas
([ADR-153](#adr-153--quader-is-cut-into-task-areas-roles-of-one-binary-network-seams-only-at-trust-or-load-boundaries))
more pod types talk to each other, so the owner set the rule for every policy.

**Decision.** Quader writes only ingress rules, only for the pods the Helm chart deploys and between them,
and every rule names its specific port. The chart renders no egress rule and no policy for pods it does
not deploy. The rule governs both charts, `quader` and `quader-bastion` (owner, 2026-11-05).

**Consequences.** The egress part of R-HA-042, its values (`networkPolicy.egress`), Q-HA-10 and H-41 are
rewritten with the specification of the cut; separating egress is Quader's address policy (R-REPO-038)
and, beyond it, the cluster operator's own policy. Each seam between task areas is an ingress rule of
the receiving role that admits the sending roles on the seam's port.

**Changed on 2026-11-05.** The chart `quader-bastion` rendered an egress policy, on by default (R-BAS-047
before 2026-11-05: DNS, the main installation's address, Valkey, the cache bucket and the span collector,
nothing else). The owner extended the rule to both charts and removed it: R-BAS-047 is ingress rules only,
the values `networkPolicy.egress` and their render guards are gone, and Q-BAS-55 is superseded in part.
Containing the outbound connections of a taken-over Bastion pod is the cluster operator's own policy, recorded
as the gap [H-522](security/bastion.md#h-522--the-chart-restricts-no-egress-of-the-bastion-pods); the Bastion
still holds no credential for PostgreSQL, the object store or upstream registries (R-BAS-030).

**Alternatives considered.** None; set by the owner. For the chart `quader-bastion` the owner weighed and
rejected keeping its egress policy as an exception, and keeping it off by default as an opt-in.

**Spec:** [owner constraints](spec/README.md#owner-constraints),
[R-HA-042](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-042--network-policies),
[R-BAS-047](spec/bastion.md#r-bas-047--network-policy).

### ADR-155 · Three roles: api, packages and worker; variants are pools

**Status:** Accepted (owner decision of 2026-11-04); the role `fetch` dropped by the owner the same day

**Context.** [ADR-153](#adr-153--quader-is-cut-into-task-areas-roles-of-one-binary-network-seams-only-at-trust-or-load-boundaries)
cuts Quader into roles of one binary. Which roles exist was
the next decision. What the code already has: the route families `ui`, `api`, `ci_exchange`, `packages` and `files`
([R-EP-005](spec/endpoints.md#r-ep-005--surface-per-endpoint); `internal/config/endpoints.go`); an endpoint without `ui` evaluates no session cookie
(R-EP-010); roles are sets of wiring areas chosen as data (`SubsystemsFor` in `internal/app/roles.go`); the job queue
has named queues with their own slots (`default`, `maintenance`, `index`, `delivery`), and the advisory sync shares
`maintenance` with garbage collection and cleanup.

| Option | Roles | What it separates | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| (A) Minimal | `web` as today, `fetch`, `worker` with queue pools | Upstream contact and background queues; UI and package traffic keep sharing pods, load and secrets | Small |
| **(B) By trust** | `api` (`ui`, `api`, `ci_exchange`), `packages` (`packages`, `files`), `fetch`, `worker` with queue pools | Humans, sessions, the OIDC client secret and break-glass in `api`; machine traffic with tokens only and no session evaluation in `packages`; the lease pool and session connections in `worker` | Medium |
| (C) Fine | As (B), and a role per format and per queue | As (B), with more Deployments whose subsystems are identical | Medium to large |

**Decision.** Option (B). A role is a set of subsystems and secrets of its own; a variant of a role by path prefix or
queue is a pool of that role (R-HA-062), rendered from values without code.

| Role | Serves | Holds | Admitted by its ingress rules (ADR-154) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `api` | route families `ui`, `api`, `ci_exchange` | sessions, the OIDC client secret, the break-glass password | 8080 from the edge, 8081 from monitoring |
| `packages` | route families `packages`, `files`; tokens only; the fills of client misses | no session store, no login secret | 8080 from the edge, 8081 from monitoring |
| `worker` | the job queue, leases, the scheduler, the mirror's passes and the advisory sync; pools by queue (`maintenance`, `index`, `vuln`, `mirror`) | the lease pool | 8081 from monitoring |

`bastion` and `backup` stay as they are. A pool per format (`/api/npm/`, `/api/nuget/`) or per queue is option (C)'s
split, available as values under this decision.

**Consequences.** ADR-013 and ADR-104 are revised by the specification of phase 6a, together with INV-2, R-ARCH-001,
R-HA-002, R-HA-062 and R-HA-042. Routing splits one host by path prefix between `api` and `packages` (R-HA-037 routes a
host whole today). Not verified when this was decided, and checked by the specification: that the UI never calls a
`packages` or `files` route with a session cookie; if it does, that call is served through `api`. The specification of
phase 6a checked it: the UI's uploads and folders are `PUT /files/…` and its Download buttons navigate to `/files/` and package
URLs, all with the session cookie; they move to session-only content routes of `api`
([Q-UI-106](spec/api-and-ui.md#q-ui-106--how-the-uis-downloads-and-uploads-reach-api-after-the-cut)). Each role that
fills or probes an upstream contacts it itself, as before: `packages` for client misses and shadowing probes, `api`
for upstream tests, `worker` for the mirror's passes and the advisory sync.

**Changed on 2026-11-04.** The owner chose option (B) with a fourth role `fetch`, the only role that contacts upstream
registries, and dropped it the same day after its gains were checked (ADR-153, "Changed on 2026-11-04"). Options (A)
and (C) named it as well; without it, (A) is `web` and `worker` with queue pools.

**Revisit condition.** Two formats need different subsystems or secrets (then a format becomes a role), or a queue's
work needs a secret the others must not hold.

**Alternatives considered.** (A) and (C) above.

**Spec:** [R-EP-005](spec/endpoints.md#r-ep-005--surface-per-endpoint),
[R-ARCH-001](spec/architecture.md#r-arch-001--one-binary-identical-replicas-process-roles),
[R-HA-062](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-062--further-splits-of-a-role-into-several-deployments).

### ADR-156 · Projects own their repositories, members hold roles, names are scoped to the project

**Status:** Accepted (owner decision of 2026-11-06); the details it left open decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough. Amended on 2026-11-20 by [ADR-209](#adr-209--the-built-in-project-upstream-holds-the-products-well-known-repositories-and-a-virtual-repository-may-list-them): a built-in project `upstream` holds the product's well-known repositories, and a virtual repository may list them beside its own project's

**Context.** Projects came into the beta as a frame for delegated administration
([R-AUTHZ-026](spec/authorization.md#r-authz-026--projects-for-delegated-administration), 2026-11-02): a repository belonged
to at most one project, project administrators with two switches administered it, and the names of a project's
repositories, policies and service accounts carried the project key as a prefix, with overlap rules between keys and names
(Q-AUTHZ-176). In his review of 2026-11-06 the owner expected repositories always to belong to a project and users to be in
a few projects and to choose among them. Quader is pre-alpha: no installation and no client has to keep working
([CLAUDE.md](../CLAUDE.md), [Q-ARCH-340](spec/architecture.md#q-arch-340--no-backward-compatibility-until-the-first-stable-release)).

**Decision.**
- Every repository belongs to exactly one project, without a built-in project, and none is shared: a virtual repository
  lists only repositories of its project, a remote of a public registry exists in each project that needs it
  ([Q-AUTHZ-206](spec/authorization.md#q-authz-206--every-repository-belongs-to-exactly-one-project)).
- A repository is addressed inside its project, and its key is unique within it: `/api/<format>/<projectKey>/<repoKey>/…`,
  `/files/<projectKey>/<repoKey>/…`, `/api/v1/projects/<projectKey>/repositories/<repoKey>…` ([Q-REPO-212](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-212--a-repository-is-addressed-inside-its-project-and-no-repository-is-shared)).
- Users and groups are members of a project with one of four roles: Reader (`read`), Developer (also `annotate`,
  `deploy`), Maintainer (every action), Owner (every action and the administration of the project on its own); the
  switches go. `admin` creates and deletes projects and names the first Owner; `admin` and `auditor` see every project
  ([Q-AUTHZ-207](spec/authorization.md#q-authz-207--a-user-or-group-is-a-member-of-a-project-with-a-role-and-the-role-grants-the-projects-repositories), [Q-AUTHZ-208](spec/authorization.md#q-authz-208--four-project-roles-reader-developer-maintainer-owner)).
- A project's policies and service accounts are named within the project, without a prefix; administrators keep
  service accounts and policies of no project ([Q-AUTHZ-209](spec/authorization.md#q-authz-209--a-projects-policies-and-service-accounts-are-named-within-the-project-administrators-keep-instance-wide-ones)).
- The details the owner left open, decided by the development agent: a project's CI mappings are named within it too
  ([Q-AUTHZ-214](spec/authorization.md#q-authz-214--a-projects-ci-mappings-are-named-within-the-project-like-its-policies-and-service-accounts)); a role reaches the member's session and personal tokens within their scope, the Owner's
  administration needs a session or an `admin: true` token, and service accounts are no members ([Q-AUTHZ-215](spec/authorization.md#q-authz-215--a-members-role-acts-through-its-session-and-personal-tokens-within-their-scope-and-service-accounts-are-not-members));
  selectors name the project in instance contexts and a bare key inside a project ([Q-AUTHZ-216](spec/authorization.md#q-authz-216--repository-selectors-name-the-project-in-instance-contexts-and-a-bare-key-inside-a-project)); only an
  administrator removes or demotes the last Owner ([Q-AUTHZ-217](spec/authorization.md#q-authz-217--the-last-owner-of-a-project-is-removed-or-demoted-only-by-an-administrator-of-quader)); a move to another project is an operation of
  its own, refused while the source project names the repository ([Q-REPO-217](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-217--a-repository-moves-to-another-project-through-an-operation-of-its-own-and-only-while-nothing-of-its-project-names-it)); the label binding of host roots
  goes ([Q-EP-76](spec/endpoints.md#q-ep-76--a-host-root-binds-a-repository-by-project-and-key-and-the-label-binding-goes)).

**Consequences.** Every route, client guide, selector, exposure rule, host-root binding, CI mapping and principal reference
that names a repository, a project's service account or a project's CI mapping changes; INV-5 and INV-6 are revised
([ADR-016](#adr-016--repository-model-local-remote-virtual-inv-5), [ADR-017](#adr-017--url-layout-on-two-listeners-inv-6)).
The prefix rules, their overlap checks and their gaps go. A repository named outside its project, in a log, a metric, an
audit event or a job target, is the qualified `<projectKey>/<repoKey>`. The schema is changed in place, without a
migration path. The format contract (R-ARCH-008) changes with it: a format names a repository by its qualified
`qname.Repo` (`RepoRef.Name`), the read scope, the link builder, the refusals and the request carry that name
(`ReadScope.MayRead` and `Shape`, `LinkBuilder.File` and `Registry`, `Refusal.Name` and `CacheView`, `Request.Addressed()`),
and `catalog.ValidID` is replaced by `qname.ValidFormat`: a changed meaning and a removal, so `formats.ContractVersion`
rises from 1 to 2 under the rule of R-ARCH-025, every format is moved in the same change and
`internal/formats/testdata/contract.txt` is regenerated. The declaration of the API names the project from the path and the least role, so the shared step narrows
to the project itself ([ADR-146](#adr-146--an-operation-admits-project-administrators-through-a-declaration-of-its-own),
superseded in part). Built.

**Alternatives considered.** A built-in project for repositories without one (Q-AUTHZ-206 (a)); a global key with the
project key as a required prefix, or the project as a column only (Q-REPO-212 (b), (c)); membership derived from policies,
or every project visible to everybody (Q-AUTHZ-207 (b), (c)); three or five roles (Q-AUTHZ-208 (a), (c)); keeping the
prefix for policies and service accounts (Q-AUTHZ-209 (b)).

**Revisit condition:** the model is the owner's; each detail of the development agent names its own condition on its page.

**Spec:** [R-AUTHZ-026](spec/authorization.md#r-authz-026--projects-for-delegated-administration),
[R-AUTHZ-004](spec/authorization.md#r-authz-004--repository-selectors),
[R-REPO-002](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md#r-repo-002--repository-keys-and-client-addresses),
[R-REPO-060](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md#r-repo-060--move-a-repository-to-another-project),
[R-AUTH-020](spec/identity-and-authentication.md#r-auth-020--service-accounts),
[R-CI-009](spec/gitlab-ci-oidc.md#r-ci-009--identity-mapping-model-and-evaluation-order),
[R-EP-006](spec/endpoints.md#r-ep-006--host-root-binding-the-reserved-mechanism), [INV-5 and INV-6](spec/README.md#design-invariants).

### ADR-199 · The product is renamed from trove to Quader, with the token prefix `qdr_` and a new mark

**Status:** Accepted (owner decision of 2026-11-17); the token prefix `qdr_` chosen by the development agent, open to the
owner's objection

**Context.** On 2026-11-17 the owner renamed the product from trove to Quader and gave it a new mark. The name trove and the
token prefix `trv_` came from the rename of 2026-10-28 ([ADR-019](#adr-019--quader-issues-opaque-prefixed-tokens-inv-8)).
Quader is pre-alpha: no installation and no client has to keep working ([CLAUDE.md](../CLAUDE.md),
[Q-ARCH-340](spec/architecture.md#q-arch-340--no-backward-compatibility-until-the-first-stable-release)).

**Decision.**
- The product is Quader: "Quader" in running text, `quader` in identifiers.
- The internet-facing cache keeps its name: the Quader Bastion, `quader-bastion`
  ([ADR-142](#adr-142--the-quader-bastion-an-internet-facing-read-only-cache-instance-in-the-beta)).
- The derived names: the Go module and the repository `github.com/guided-traffic/quader`; the binary `quader` and its
  configuration file `/etc/quader/quader.yaml`; the environment variables `QUADER_*` and the metrics `quader_*`; the image
  `guidedtraffic/quader`; the charts `quader` and `quader-bastion`.
- The token and cookie prefix is `qdr_`: the tokens `qdr_pat_`, `qdr_sat_`, `qdr_cit_`, `qdr_bst_` and `qdr_rgt_`, the
  cookies `__Host-qdr_session`, `__Host-qdr_csrf` and `__Host-qdr_oidc_binding`. It is as long as `trv_`, so an opaque
  token stays 57 characters long. Chosen by the development agent; the owner may object.
- The mark: Quader is a wall of three courses with one stone coloured; the Bastion is a tower of three courses
  (battlements, an overhanging crown, a shaft) with the middle merlon coloured. Both are drawn on a grid of 64 with a
  margin of 4, a stone height of 16, a joint of 4 and a corner radius of 1.5. The stones are `#28272d` on light and
  `#ececef` on dark; the coloured stone is sandstone, `#b4690e` on light and `#e9a13b` on dark.
- Nothing of the old name is accepted any more: no alias, no `trv_` token or cookie, no `TROVE_*` variable, no old chart,
  image or metric name, no migration path.

**Consequences.** A token or a session issued under `trv_` is refused, so an installation is set up again under the new
chart, release and image names, with new tokens. The test vectors and the scanner pattern that carry the prefix are
recomputed ([R-AUTH-022](spec/identity-and-authentication.md#r-auth-022--token-types-and-format)). The rule of
[R-ARCH-025](spec/architecture.md#r-arch-025--versioning-and-compatibility-policy) that a prefix never changes meaning
holds for the new prefixes; the old ones are gone, not given another meaning. The wall replaces the lanes of
[Q-UI-145](spec/api-and-ui.md#q-ui-145--the-logos-wordmark-as-paths-from-inter-bold-and-a-reduced-mark-as-the-favicon),
and the wordmark reads "Quader"; the [design language](developer/design-language.md) documents the mark and its
generator. Not verified: whether "Quader" is free as a trademark and as a domain.

**Alternatives considered.** For the prefix: `quader_` (explains itself in a leak report, but three characters longer, so
every token, its length check and its test vectors change length) and keeping `trv_` (nothing to recompute, but every
leaked token would name the old product). For the name and the mark: none; set by the owner.

**Revisit condition:** the owner objects to `qdr_`.

**Spec:** [INV-8](spec/README.md#design-invariants),
[R-AUTH-022](spec/identity-and-authentication.md#r-auth-022--token-types-and-format),
[Q-AUTH-2](spec/identity-and-authentication.md#q-auth-2--session-cookie-name),
[R-ARCH-025](spec/architecture.md#r-arch-025--versioning-and-compatibility-policy), [spec/bastion.md](spec/bastion.md).

### ADR-200 · A list's filters open in a drawer, the app's one pattern for content over the page

**Status:** Accepted (owner decision of 2026-11-18) for the drawer; its build decided by the development agent, owner review at
the walkthrough

**Context.** In the walk of 2026-11-18 (W-6) the owner called the filter panel beside a list "extremely ugly" and asked for a drawer.
One component carried the filters of every list, and it stood beside the list where the list kept 71 rem and between its button and
the list where it did not
([Q-UI-327](spec/api-and-ui.md#q-ui-327--the-filter-panel-sits-beside-a-list-only-where-the-list-keeps-71-rem-and-a-tables-columns-share-its-rows-width-without-the-scrollbar)):
two layouts, and a list rebuilt narrower whenever the panel opened. The app had no drawer for content; the navigation's drawer at
narrow widths belongs to the shell.

**Decision.**
- Content over the page is a drawer that slides in from the right: `<quader-drawer>`
  ([drawer.ts](../web/src/app/shared/ui/drawer.ts)), the CDK dialog the app's dialogs already use (Q-UI-126), placed at the window's
  right edge with its full height, 24 rem wide. It is a modal dialog named by its heading; the focus moves in and is trapped;
  Escape, its close button and a click beside it close it; the focus returns to the opener; the page behind it does not scroll.
- A list's filters are such a drawer, `<quader-filter-panel>`: one behaviour at every width. The list keeps its width and its
  columns. The search by name is outside the drawer, in the list's head, and the filters that are set show beside **Filters** as
  chips ([R-UI-100](spec/api-and-ui.md#r-ui-100--the-head-of-every-list-the-search-by-name-filters-and-the-filters-that-are-set),
  [R-UI-101](spec/api-and-ui.md#r-ui-101--the-filters-open-in-a-drawer-over-the-page)).

**Consequences.** Every list screen with filters changed at once, and the layout grid of Q-UI-327 is gone. What filters a list is
read in its chips while the drawer is closed, not in an open panel. A further screen that needs content over the page (the
details of one row, a picker) uses the same component and does not build its own overlay.

**Alternatives considered.** The navigation's drawer reused (from the left, the shell's, without a dialog role or focus trap); the
panel beside the list kept (the owner's verdict); a drawer of the app's own without the CDK (the focus trap, the inert page behind
it and the scroll block written again).

**Revisit condition:** a list's filters need more than 24 rem, or a second kind of content over the page does not fit a drawer.

**Spec:** [Q-UI-420](spec/api-and-ui.md#q-ui-420--the-filters-of-a-list-open-in-a-drawer-from-the-right-over-the-page) to
[Q-UI-423](spec/api-and-ui.md#q-ui-423--the-drawers-filters-stand-open-apply-closes-it-and-closing-without-apply-keeps-what-the-list-shows).
### ADR-202 · The client setup and the guide are one page of a repository

**Status:** Accepted (owner decision of 2026-11-18, the walk through the frontend, W-2: "context instead of choices"). The address,
the layout and the change of the API are decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** Quader had two pages for one job. The guides (`/guides`) asked for four things in boxed groups of radio buttons
(package type, client, repository, repository class) before a boxed contents list and dense prose; the client setup (`/setup`)
showed the snippets for a repository named in its query. The owner found the guides "so ugly and overloaded that nobody wants to
work with them", and took the client address out of the list of repositories because an address without its guide has no context
(W-4).

**Decision.** One page, **Set up client**, belongs to a repository: `/projects/{project}/repositories/{key}/setup`. It asks for
nothing the repository decides: the format, the class and the repository are its header, the client is one control where the format
has several. The job comes first (the address, the token, then the snippets of Configure, Install and, for who may publish,
Publish) and the explanation after it: what a repository of the class is, then the format's sections folded under their headings.
The navigation entry **Guides** shows the formats as tiles; a tile leads to the format's repositories, and the guide of a class
without a repository is the same page at `/guides/{format}/{class}`. `/setup` is removed. The guide's answer carries its snippets
beside its sections, and the format contract no longer names a setup section per guide section
([R-API-070](spec/api-and-ui.md#r-api-070--a-guide-carries-its-snippets-beside-its-sections)).

**Consequences.** Every **Set up client** has one target, and one look per place (a default button on a page, a quiet row action in a table row, Q-UI-487). The address of a repository is shown with the snippets that
use it. The token is created on the page and read into the variable, so the reader does not leave the task. A guide is reached
through a repository, so a reader without one takes one more step (the format's page, then a class). The guide of a reader who may
not publish leaves publishing out. Kit check 8 now requires the configure and install templates of every client of a format with
a guide instead of a section that attaches them.

**Alternatives considered.** Restyling the guides page and keeping its four choices (the owner: not chosen); moving the guides
into the manual (the owner: not chosen; the text would lose this installation's addresses); keeping two pages linked to each
other (the state the owner rejected).

**Spec:** [R-UI-120](spec/api-and-ui.md#r-ui-120--set-up-client-is-one-page-of-a-repository) to
[R-UI-127](spec/api-and-ui.md#r-ui-127--the-format-tiles-are-one-component), R-UI-016, R-UI-049, R-API-053, R-API-070; decided:
Q-UI-480 to Q-UI-488, Q-API-310.

### ADR-203 · Browse goes; a repository's files live on its page

**Status:** Accepted (owner decision of 2026-11-18, walk objection W-8); the details decided by the development agent — owner review
at the walkthrough

**Context.** Until 2026-11-18 a project had two ways to the same content. **Browse** (`/projects/<project>/browse/<repo>/<path>`)
showed a tree of the project's repositories, folders and files beside a details pane, and it was the only place with upload, new
folder and delete. The page of a repository ([R-UI-052](spec/api-and-ui.md#r-ui-052--repository-content-page)) listed the files of a
generic repository too and offered none of these, not even to the project's Owner. In his walk of 2026-11-18 the owner chose one way to
the files, from the repository; keeping both, and keeping Browse for Owners and administrators only, were not chosen.

**Decision.**
- The navigation entry **Browse**, its routes and its screen are removed. Nothing redirects from the old addresses (no backward
  compatibility before the first stable release, [Q-ARCH-340](spec/architecture.md#q-arch-340--no-backward-compatibility-until-the-first-stable-release)).
- A folder or a file is the page of its repository at `/projects/<project>/repositories/<key>/files/<path…>`
  ([Q-UI-510](spec/api-and-ui.md#q-ui-510--a-folder-and-a-file-are-the-repositorys-page-at-files-and-their-path)); the root of a
  generic repository's files is the repository's own address. A package format keeps its packages as the page and shows its raw
  files on demand ([Q-UI-511](spec/api-and-ui.md#q-ui-511--a-package-formats-raw-files-are-a-page-behind-files-in-the-header-menu)).
- The operations move there, each for the caller who may use it at that path: upload, new folder and delete
  ([R-UI-010 to R-UI-012](spec/api-and-ui.md#r-ui-010--files-of-a-repository),
  [Q-UI-512](spec/api-and-ui.md#q-ui-512--the-operations-stand-where-they-act-and-only-for-who-may-use-them)). The plain reader
  sees the list, a folder, a file, Download and the copy buttons.
- Copy, move and the trash can are not built, because their operations are not ([R-STOR-019, R-STOR-022, R-STOR-023](spec/storage.md#r-stor-019--copy-and-move),
  milestones M7 and M8 of the [FULL plan](projektplan/FULL.md)). Their place on the repository's page is decided now: a copy or a move
  chooses its target repository from a list and its folder by browsing it in the dialog
  ([Q-UI-515](spec/api-and-ui.md#q-ui-515--a-copy-or-a-move-chooses-its-target-repository-from-a-list-and-its-folder-by-browsing-it));
  a repository's trash can is a page of the repository, the installation's an administrator's page
  ([Q-UI-516](spec/api-and-ui.md#q-ui-516--the-trash-can-of-a-repository-is-a-page-of-the-repository-the-installations-is-the-administrators)).

**Consequences.** The tree across the repositories of a project is gone: a reader who wants another repository goes back to the
project's list, and a copy or a move into another repository needs the target picker of Q-UI-515 instead of a drag inside a tree.
Every link that led into Browse leads to the repository's page or to the file's page
([Q-UI-519](spec/api-and-ui.md#q-ui-519--every-link-into-browse-leads-to-the-repositorys-page-or-to-the-files-page)). The `@angular/aria`
tree is still used by the Documentation tab of an Ansible collection, so it stays a dependency. No API changes: the page reads the
items, children and stats operations and writes through the content route and the items delete of
[R-API-025](spec/api-and-ui.md#r-api-025--items-and-raw-file-transfer).

**Alternatives considered.** Keeping both screens (two ways to one job, and the operations on the one nobody expects); keeping
Browse for Owners and administrators only (the same split, moved to fewer people). Both were the owner's options and not chosen.

**Revisit condition:** users who work across many repositories at once ask for a tree again, or the copy and move of R-STOR-019 are
built and the picker of Q-UI-515 proves too slow for a deep target.

**Spec:** [R-UI-010 to R-UI-014](spec/api-and-ui.md#r-ui-010--files-of-a-repository),
[R-UI-052](spec/api-and-ui.md#r-ui-052--repository-content-page), [Q-UI-510 to Q-UI-521](spec/api-and-ui.md#decisions).

### ADR-204 · An administrator restricts visibility levels to administrators

**Status:** Accepted (owner requirement of 2026-11-18, walk objection W-11); the rules decided by the development agent — owner
review at the walkthrough

**Context.** Since T-18 a project's level is an administrator's and a repository's levels are its Owner's, up to the project's level
([Q-AUTHZ-267](spec/authorization.md#q-authz-267--an-administrator-sets-the-level-of-a-project-its-owner-sets-the-levels-of-its-repositories-within-it)).
An administrator could not keep a level from the Owners: an Owner of a public project opened any of its repositories to the
internet. In his walk of 2026-11-18 the owner asked, with the general settings of his GitLab as the reference, for two settings in
the administration area: the default project visibility (which existed, in a closed section, as "Default visibility level") and
restricted visibility levels.

**Decision.**
- The installation's visibility settings gain `restrictedLevels`, a set of levels only an administrator may choose
  ([R-AUTHZ-037](spec/authorization.md#r-authz-037--restricted-visibility-levels),
  [R-API-075](spec/api-and-ui.md#r-api-075--the-restricted-levels-in-the-visibility-settings)). An administrator is whoever holds
  `security-settings:write` for the request, the permission that changes the restriction
  ([Q-AUTHZ-283](spec/authorization.md#q-authz-283--an-administrator-is-whoever-holds-security-settingswrite-for-the-request)).
- Everyone else is refused a restricted level it chooses for a project or a part of a repository, with 403
  `visibility_level_restricted`, after the rules that bind everyone
  ([R-AUTHZ-038](spec/authorization.md#r-authz-038--the-order-in-which-a-level-is-refused)). A level an object has is kept and may be
  lowered, never chosen anew; a create that names no level falls to the highest level the caller may choose; the default is
  never restricted; a cascade, a move or a replay is no choice (Q-AUTHZ-284 to Q-AUTHZ-288).
- Every signed-in caller reads the levels it may choose (`GET /api/v1/visibility-choices`,
  [R-API-076](spec/api-and-ui.md#r-api-076--the-levels-a-caller-may-choose)), and every form that chooses a level shows a level
  the caller cannot choose disabled with the reason the server would answer
  ([R-UI-141](spec/api-and-ui.md#r-ui-141--a-level-the-caller-cannot-choose-is-disabled-where-a-level-is-chosen)).
- **Admin area › Settings › General › Visibility** opens with the page and holds **Default project visibility** and **Restricted
  visibility levels**, one checkbox per level, with one save
  ([R-UI-140](spec/api-and-ui.md#r-ui-140--the-restricted-visibility-levels-in-the-general-settings)).

**Consequences.** Opening content to the organization or to the internet can be kept to the administrators without taking the level
of repositories away from their Owners: they still narrow and open within what is not restricted. Restricting a level closes
nothing that is open; an administrator who wants that lowers the projects, whose cascade lowers their repositories. The creation
form keeps its one level group; an Owner whose project's level is restricted gets the next lower level without being asked. Today
only `admin` holds `projects:write`, so for projects the rule binds only a token of an administrator scoped without
`security-settings:write`.

**Alternatives considered.** A restriction that lowers the objects that have the level (closes content behind the setting's back);
an exemption by the object's capability (`repositories:write-config` would bypass a restriction meant for it); refusing a create
whose project level is restricted (the plain path would fail). Each is a decision block on
[authorization.md](spec/authorization.md#decisions).

**Revisit condition:** the owner wants a restriction that also closes what is open, or projects are created by their teams and
`projects:write` reaches callers without `security-settings:write`.

**Spec:** [R-AUTHZ-037, R-AUTHZ-038](spec/authorization.md#r-authz-037--restricted-visibility-levels), Q-AUTHZ-283 to Q-AUTHZ-289;
[R-API-075, R-API-076](spec/api-and-ui.md#r-api-075--the-restricted-levels-in-the-visibility-settings), Q-API-330 to Q-API-332;
[R-UI-140, R-UI-141](spec/api-and-ui.md#r-ui-140--the-restricted-visibility-levels-in-the-general-settings), Q-UI-540 to Q-UI-543.

### ADR-205 · The format contract declares what a fetch of a version is, and a size may be partial or not known; the contract is at version 5

**Status:** Accepted (owner decision of 2026-11-19, walk objection W-24: a remote lists what was fetched, every cell is true, for every
format); the contract change decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough

**Context.** The owner saw a remote OCI tag listed with **0 B**, **Last fetched** "Never" and no downloads. The package view counted a
version's downloads on its lead item, which a remote OCI tag has none of, a Debian version has one of several, and a pull by digest never
touches; the size of an index was the sum of its children held when the index was written; and the streamed first answer of every remote
miss was not counted. The owner decided that what is settled at OCI holds for every format, built and future.

**Decision.**
- `formats.Descriptor` gains `VersionFetch` (`FetchLeadFile`, `FetchAnyFile`, `FetchDocument`; the zero value `FetchUndeclared`):
  which downloads are fetches of a version ([R-API-079](spec/api-and-ui.md#r-api-079--what-a-fetch-of-a-version-is-in-every-format-and-class)).
  `Validate` refuses a format with a package view that declares none; `formats/all` pins each format's rule in a test.
- `formats.ViewSizer.ViewSizes` returns a `ViewSize` (`Bytes`, `Partial`, `Unknown`) instead of a number
  ([R-API-080](spec/api-and-ui.md#r-api-080--a-size-that-is-not-known-is-not-a-number)); the kit's check 11 refuses a number for a size
  that is not known.
- `formats.ItemStore` gains `RecordDownload`: a format that answers the bytes of an item from a store of its own (a remote OCI tag from its
  metadata entry) counts the download on that item (R-STOR-015, Q-OCI-222).
- A changed method and a required field move every format: `ContractVersion` is 5 (R-ARCH-025).

**Consequences.** The package view counts a version's downloads by its format's rule in the statements that read the rows; a future format
declares its rule before it registers. The API's `sizeBytes` is nullable and gains `sizePartial` (Q-API-341). No table is added: the item
statistics hold every download, and the view `package_version_listing` gains the content digest of a version without a lead file
(migration 00079).

**Alternatives considered.** An optional view method that returns the fetch items (forgotten by a new format, a second pass for the list's
counts); the core's own rule over the linked files (counts the provenance bundle and the `.nuspec`, misses a pull by digest); a statistics
row per version written on the serve path (Q-API-295, Q-API-340).

**Revisit condition:** a format whose fetch is none of the three rules.

**Spec:** [architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-008, R-ARCH-025; [api-and-ui.md](spec/api-and-ui.md) R-API-065, R-API-079 to R-API-081,
Q-API-295, Q-API-340 to Q-API-343; [formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md) Q-OCI-221, Q-OCI-222; [repositories-and-proxy.md](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md)
Q-REPO-330, Q-REPO-331.

### ADR-206 · Download limits: budgets per caller and repository, technical tokens on three levels, Audit and Enforce

**Status:** Accepted (owner decisions of 2026-11-19, walk item W-26: seventeen decisions in his working paper); the mechanisms decided
by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough

**Context.** The owner asked to set, for single users, technical tokens, groups and anonymous addresses, how many requests and how many
bytes from the cache and from the upstream a caller may take per second and per hour, and for administrators and project Owners to
see every caller's downloads at a glance. Until now the package protocols had three rate-limit classes keyed by the token ID, none on
the registry's `/v2/` (finding F-155), and nothing counted bytes or callers. What is decided for OCI holds for every format.

**Decision.**
- Every request on a protocol path fits two budgets in the same figures: its subject's at the place whose rule applies, and the
  remote's ceiling for its class of callers ([usage-and-limits.md](spec/usage-and-limits.md) R-LIM-001 to R-LIM-016). A subject is a
  user (sessions and personal tokens together), a technical token, a CI project or an anonymous address (IPv4, IPv6 `/64`).
- Profiles name every figure; rules give a profile to a single caller, an address range, a group or a kind at the instance, a project
  or a repository; resolution takes the place first, then the caller; consumption under a repository's rule counts against that rule.
  A project Owner narrows, and goes above the instance only up to a maximum the administrator gives the project.
- Counters live in Valkey (with `INCRBY` and sorted sets added to the ACL); one round trip per protocol request, one more for a
  download or a miss; the usage store is buffered per replica and written to PostgreSQL every ten seconds (R-LIM-017, R-LIM-027).
- At the limit: 429 for requests; slowing down for bytes per second; 429 before a download for hourly and daily bytes; what is
  cached is still served when the upstream budget is used up (R-REPO-025 step 9a); a block after too many refused requests.
- One instance switch, Enforce (the default) or Audit. In Audit nothing on a protocol path is refused or slowed, the package
  classes of R-API-016 included (the owner, 2026-11-19, Q-LIM-4 (b)); `package_read` and `package_anonymous` are removed and
  `package_write`, keyed by the subject, holds in Enforce only. The default is Enforce because Audit has no request limit
  (the development agent, on the owner's leave of 2026-11-19; R-LIM-026, R-API-016).
- A service account belongs to the instance, a project or a repository; a repository's account holds its actions at the account;
  each account has named technical tokens, each a budget subject that rotation keeps
  ([identity-and-authentication.md](spec/identity-and-authentication.md) R-AUTH-045, R-AUTH-046,
  [authorization.md](spec/authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-039).
- The format contract is at version 6: `Host.Serve` may refuse a download before its status line, and a route's kind decides what
  is counted, checked and paced; a kit check and a pinned table hold every format to it (R-LIM-036).

**Consequences.** INV-9 gains the actions of a repository's service account as a grant source. The `/files/` paths move from the
management API's classes to the protocol paths. The service-account token operations become the technical-token operations; stored
SATs are not converted (pre-alpha). The usage of anonymous callers, with their addresses, is kept 30 days and seen by
administrators, auditors and the Owner of the project. The admin area gains **Usage** and **Download limits**; a project's and a
repository's settings gain a closed section **Download limits**; the profile gains **Usage**.

**Alternatives considered.** One budget per caller for the installation with repositories only narrowing, an ordered list of group
rules, counting and showing before limiting, a technical token as a project account's token narrowed to a repository (the
development agent's proposals the owner chose against); counters in PostgreSQL as for storage quotas (Q-LIM-10); every 404 as a
refused request (Q-LIM-7); policies for a repository's account (Q-AUTHZ-296).

**Revisit condition:** Valkey incidents let budgets be exceeded visibly; a format whose route kinds do not say what is content; an
installation switched to Audit is abused through a public remote (H-1015 of [security/usage-and-limits.md](security/usage-and-limits.md)).

**Spec:** [usage-and-limits.md](spec/usage-and-limits.md) R-LIM-001 to R-LIM-039, Q-LIM-1 to Q-LIM-27;
[api-and-ui.md](spec/api-and-ui.md) R-API-016, R-API-082, R-UI-177 to R-UI-186, Q-API-344, Q-API-345, Q-UI-730 to Q-UI-736;
[identity-and-authentication.md](spec/identity-and-authentication.md) R-AUTH-045, R-AUTH-046, Q-AUTH-415 to Q-AUTH-417;
[authorization.md](spec/authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-039, R-AUTHZ-040, Q-AUTHZ-296 to Q-AUTHZ-298;
[repositories-and-proxy.md](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-025 step 9a; [architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-031,
R-ARCH-034.

### ADR-207 · A probe starts the download of its version in the background; the format contract is at version 7

**Status:** Accepted (owner decisions of 2026-11-19, walk item W-25: the trigger, the platforms of an index, the bound by the download
limits, every format); the mechanisms decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough

**Context.** The owner asked that a request which only probes an image, without starting its download, make Quader start the download
in the background. INV-11 and R-REPO-024 said a remote fetches nothing ahead of time in mode `pullThrough`. The owner decided that a
request naming exactly one version or file without fetching its content starts the download of that version's content in every format,
that an OCI index downloads the platforms of a list per repository (`linux/amd64, linux/arm64` by default, the list the mirror reads),
