and that the download limits bound it; the charge was fixed beforehand in R-LIM-037.

**Decision.**
- INV-11 and R-REPO-024 are rewritten: a remote fetches ahead only the content of a version a client probed, charged to that client,
  unless `remote.downloadOnProbe` is off, and in mode `mirror` what its passes discover
  ([repositories-and-proxy.md](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-065, Q-REPO-360).
- The decision is taken on the probe's request after its answer, in a fixed order: the switch and the repository's state, the patterns
  and claims, the caller's populate permission, what is stored, the queue, step 9a for the caller (Q-REPO-362, Q-REPO-364).
- The download is the job `remote-background-download` of the worker, exclusive per version, through the gate and engine of a mirror
  pass; bounded by 1,000 files and `limits.maxArtifactBytes` per version and `limits.maxConcurrentFetches` per repository (Q-REPO-361,
  Q-REPO-363). The charge travels with the job as a ticket and is resumed on the worker ([usage-and-limits.md](spec/usage-and-limits.md)
  Q-LIM-54). The repository's patterns now hold for every background fill (Q-REPO-365).
- `oci.mirror.platforms` becomes `oci.platforms` with the default `["linux/amd64", "linux/arm64"]`
  ([formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md) Q-OCI-223).
- The format contract is at version 7: `Descriptor.Probes` (or `NoProbe` with the reason) is required of a format with the class remote,
  `RemoteAdapter.ProbeContent` names a probed version's content, and `RemoteFetcher.Probed` is how a handler tells the host of a probe it
  answered; `formats/all` pins every format's probes ([architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-008, R-ARCH-025).
- A probe through a virtual repository is the probe of the member that serves the version, found by the tiers of R-REPO-019 without an
  upstream; the member's settings decide and the charge is the probe's, as Q-LIM-2 places every figure (Q-REPO-367). `Probed` takes a
  request of either class and a probe route may serve the class virtual; the contract stays at 7, since both were added before version 7
  was released.
- A remote OCI tag is listed once a background download stored its content (R-API-081, migration 00083).

**Consequences.** A `docker pull` that asks the tag's manifest first races its own background download; the flights of R-REPO-026
collapse the two and the client's fetch pre-empts a background request. An upstream that counts manifest requests counts the background
download's (H-1017). A NuGet probe through a virtual repository with several remote members may start at a member that lacks the
version (H-1019). No new table: the job and the usage store carry what a
user sees.

**Alternatives considered.** A detached fetch on the probe's replica (lost on a drain, invisible); marking the version for the next mirror
pass (mirror mode only); deciding before the answer (delays every probe); a switch of the instance instead of the repository; every
platform of an index, or none (the owner's options b and c).

**Revisit condition:** probes counted as `busy` or `queue_full` under normal load; operators turning the switch off for every Docker Hub
remote; the storage quota of R-STOR-029.

**Spec:** [repositories-and-proxy.md](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-024, R-REPO-065, Q-REPO-360 to Q-REPO-367, H-1017 to H-1019;
[spec/README.md](spec/README.md) INV-11; [usage-and-limits.md](spec/usage-and-limits.md) R-LIM-037, Q-LIM-54; [architecture.md](spec/architecture.md)
R-ARCH-008, R-ARCH-025; [api-and-ui.md](spec/api-and-ui.md) R-API-081, R-UI-082, Q-UI-766 to Q-UI-768; [formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md)
Q-OCI-223, Q-OCI-224; [formats/npm.md](spec/formats/npm.md) Q-NPM-89; [formats/nuget.md](spec/formats/nuget.md) Q-NUGET-124;
[formats/ansible.md](spec/formats/ansible.md) Q-ANS-80; [formats/debian.md](spec/formats/debian.md) Q-DEB-122.

### ADR-208 · A setup snippet names the parts that are the reader's, and a template declares its examples

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough. Part of the redesign of **Set up client** the owner chose on
2026-11-20 (W-27, [Q-UI-800](spec/api-and-ui.md#q-ui-800--set-up-client-takes-variant-a-snippets-are-windows-the-page-has-pictures-and-less-text)).

**Context.** The page marks what the reader must replace (`<package>`, an example such as `myapp:1.0`) and where the token goes. A screen that
guessed these by pattern would mark the tags of a `nuget.config` (`<configuration>` reads like `<package>`), miss every example that has no
brackets (`./acme-tools-1.0.0.tar.gz`), and need a list per format. The OCI pull said `<package>` where the push said `myapp:1.0`: two words for
one image.

**Decision.**
- `ClientSnippet` carries `marks`: each part of its content that is the reader's, by its literal text, with the kind `token` (the reference to
  the credential in the spelling the credential mode wrote, or the placeholder the browser fills) or `value` (a placeholder of the core:
  `<package>`, `<version>`, `<project>`, `<repository>`; or an example of the template) ([api-and-ui.md](spec/api-and-ui.md) R-API-030,
  [Q-UI-802](spec/api-and-ui.md#q-ui-802--the-server-names-the-readers-parts-of-a-snippet-and-an-image-has-one-word)).
- `formats.SetupTemplate` gains two fields, an addition that keeps `ContractVersion` at 7: `Examples`, the literal values of the template the
  reader replaces, and `PackageExample`, what an install template shows in place of `<package>` when the request names no package. Kit check 8
  refuses an example the template does not write and a package example off an install template that places the package. OCI names `myapp:1.0`
  for both, so the pull and the push say the same thing; NuGet names its package files, Ansible its archive, Debian its `.deb`, generic `<path>`
  and `<file>`.
- `language` lists `powershell` and `cmd` as themselves; Q-API-191 mapped them to `shell` for a freeze that does not apply before the first stable
  release ([Q-UI-801](spec/api-and-ui.md#q-ui-801--a-snippets-window-is-an-editor-for-a-file-and-a-terminal-for-a-command-coloured-by-its-language)).

**Consequences.** A format that adds an example declares it once, beside the text; the UI knows no format. A format that writes an example
without declaring it leaves it unmarked, which a reader of its renders sees.

**Alternatives considered.** Patterns in the UI (wrong for XML, blind to examples); ranges instead of texts (wrong as soon as the browser writes
a token into the snippet); a template function that writes and marks an example (no list to keep, but a second way to place the package and a
change of the template language every format reads).

**Revisit condition:** an example that also stands in the snippet where it is not the reader's (a mark in the wrong place).

**Spec:** [api-and-ui.md](spec/api-and-ui.md) R-API-030, Q-UI-801, Q-UI-802; [architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-009 (the written
contract of `SetupTemplate`), R-ARCH-010 check 8.

### ADR-209 · The built-in project `upstream` holds the product's well-known repositories, and a virtual repository may list them

**Status:** Accepted (owner decisions of 2026-11-20); the details decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.
Amends [ADR-156](#adr-156--projects-own-their-repositories-members-hold-roles-names-are-scoped-to-the-project) narrowly.

**Context.** Every repository belongs to exactly one project and none was shared (ADR-156), so every project that needed a public
registry kept a remote repository of its own: its own configuration, its own credential, its own share of the registry's pull limit.
The owner wanted the well-known registries preconfigured once, in a well-known project, and configurable in the admin area.

**Decision** (the owner's, [repositories-and-proxy.md](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md)
[Q-REPO-370](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-370--a-built-in-project-upstream-holds-the-products-well-known-repositories) to
[Q-REPO-372](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-372--a-reference-protects-nothing-a-member-that-is-not-there-stays-as-a-placeholder)):
- Every installation has the project `upstream`. It holds only the repositories the product defines: one remote repository per upstream
  preset of the format catalog, keyed by the preset's `id`, and the system repositories of the product's own work. Nobody creates,
  moves, renames or deletes a repository in it, and the project cannot be deleted. Every repository still belongs to exactly one project
  ([Q-AUTHZ-206](spec/authorization.md#q-authz-206--every-repository-belongs-to-exactly-one-project), amended).
- Every one is off until an administrator switches it on, on a page of its own in the admin area, which also sets each one's visibility,
  switches all on (`internal`, never `public`) and sets the visibility of all. An administrator may change a repository's address (an
  escape hatch, marked as differing and resettable) and store an account for it.
- A virtual repository lists repositories of its own project and of `upstream`, and of no other. A reference protects nothing: a member
  that is not there stays as a placeholder and takes effect again when it is.
- Beside the address and the account, an administrator sets only the six settings that narrow what a well-known repository serves
  ([Q-REPO-378](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-378--besides-the-state-the-level-the-address-and-the-account-an-administrator-sets-the-narrowing-settings),
  "Option B"); the Debian and Ubuntu repositories carry their archive keys
  ([Q-REPO-379](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-379--the-debian-and-ubuntu-well-known-repositories-carry-their-archive-keys),
  "ja, Schlüssel mitbringen").

The details, decided by the development agent: the project row comes from migration 00086 and the repositories from a reconcile in
`quader migrate` (Q-REPO-374); off is `disabled` with a row of `upstream_repository` that says why (Q-REPO-375); a retired preset leaves
a tombstone (Q-REPO-376); a release follows the product's address unless overridden and drops an account whose hosts it moves
(Q-REPO-377); members are written `upstream/<key>` (Q-REPO-381); a placeholder's state is in the settings and in the 404 (Q-REPO-382);
the project has no members, policies or accounts and is administered with `repositories:write-config` (Q-AUTHZ-300, Q-AUTHZ-303); it is
stored `public` and seen through its repositories (Q-AUTHZ-301); the operations of the admin page are their own (Q-API-360).

**Consequences.** INV-5 is revised: no repository is shared but those of `upstream`. The member tables' same-project guard admits the
built-in project. Quick setup lists the central repository instead of creating a remote (Q-REPO-385). A team's limits decide at its
virtual repository, the central repository's ceilings bound everyone (Q-LIM-62), and its usage through a central member stays visible
to its Owner (Q-LIM-63). Switching a central repository on widens every virtual repository that lists it at once; the dependency-confusion
protections hold for it as for every remote. The format catalog, part of the frozen format contract, gains `UpstreamPreset.Settings` (the
format members a preset carries, Q-REPO-379) and `ReservedPresetIDs` (the ids no preset takes, Q-REPO-387): an addition that keeps
`ContractVersion` at 7 (R-ARCH-025). The format contract also gains `VirtualPlan.NotFound` and `VirtualPlan.Unknown`, the sentence of a
placeholder for a format that walks a plan's members itself (Q-REPO-400), an addition as well. The names, the states and the declarations live in the leaf package `internal/wellknown`. Not part of it: binding a host to a repository at its root (R-EP-006, unchanged), an address
without the project segment, and the installation's own registries as presets (T-21b).

**Alternatives considered.** Each project keeps its own remotes (Q-REPO-370 (a)); well-known repositories at the API's root without a
project (Q-REPO-370 (c)); a virtual repository listing any project's repositories (Q-REPO-371 (c)); removing a member when its repository
goes, or keeping the repository on while it is listed (Q-REPO-372 (a), (c)).

**Revisit condition:** the model is the owner's; each detail of the development agent names its own condition on its page.

**Spec:** [repositories-and-proxy.md](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-066 to R-REPO-074, R-REPO-015, R-REPO-017, R-REPO-019,
R-REPO-062; [authorization.md](spec/authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-041, Q-AUTHZ-206; [api-and-ui.md](spec/api-and-ui.md) R-API-083,
R-UI-187 to R-UI-191; [usage-and-limits.md](spec/usage-and-limits.md) Q-LIM-62, Q-LIM-63; [INV-5](spec/README.md#design-invariants).

### ADR-211 · `scanner-trivy` is a system repository of `upstream` that only the image scanning reads

**Status:** Accepted (owner decision of 2026-11-20, his confirmation of the development agent's reading the same day); the details
decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** The image scanning fetched the analyser's vulnerability database straight from `mirror.gcr.io`. The owner did not want the
scanning to make every installation open a general registry, and wanted no second way that falls back to the public source.

**Decision** (the owner's, [Q-REPO-373](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-373--scanner-trivy-holds-the-analysers-database-always-private-and-only-for-the-scanner)):
one repository of `upstream`, `scanner-trivy`, holds the database and lets nothing else of its registry through; it is always private
and only for the scanner, and an administrator cannot change that; it is switched on with the image scanning and by nothing else; its
address and an account stay an administrator's, as for every well-known repository ("scanner-trivy, genau wie von dir beschrieben").
The development agent's details ([Q-REPO-380](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-380--scanner-trivy-answers-no-client-and-is-in-use-while-the-image-scanning-reads-through-it)):
no protocol request reaches it, administrators' included; system work resolves the tag through it in process; it has no state of its own,
and whether it is in use is read from the scanning's configuration.

**Consequences.** The scanning's setting names the repository the database comes from, `upstream/scanner-trivy` by default
([vulnerability-scanning.md](spec/vulnerability-scanning.md)); the general `ghcr` stays off unless an administrator wants it.

**Alternatives considered.** The database through the general registry repository (Q-REPO-373 (a)); the worker fetching it directly, as
before (Q-REPO-373 (c)); a private repository like any other, which a global policy could open (Q-REPO-380 (b)).

**Revisit condition:** the scanner role of H-812 needs the database over HTTP.

**Spec:** [repositories-and-proxy.md](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-070.

### ADR-212 · The image analysis runs in a role `scanner` that holds no secret

**Status:** Accepted (owner decision of 2026-11-20: "Perfekt, machen wir wie du analysiert hast", after he asked for a look at how a
comparable registry's scanner adapter does it); the mechanisms decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough

**Context.** The image scanning ran the analyser as a child process of a worker job, with an empty environment, on a layout the worker built
from the object store after its own checks of every layer (Q-VULN-140). The analyser is a large parser of hostile input, and it shared the
worker pod's file system, mounted secrets, network and memory limit: an escape reached the database's, the object store's and Valkey's
credentials and the key ring (H-812), and a hostile image could end the worker pod (H-818). The design read for comparison runs its
analyser in a service of its own without the registry's database or storage credentials, called with the registry's address, a credential,
the repository and the digest, and pulls the image itself; it queues the work and keeps the reports in a shared store, through which the
credential travels in clear and reaches a debug log, and its analyser inherits the service's environment and downloads its database from the
internet.

**Decision.**
- A role `scanner` of the same binary and image, a Deployment of its own, with no secret of PostgreSQL, the object store or Valkey and no
  key of the key ring ([architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-036, [ha-and-helm.md](spec/ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-065).
- The worker keeps the job: its lease, its time slice, its attempts and the deferrals. It calls the scanner with one HTTPS request per
  manifest, naming the repository, the image, the digest and a scan token, and receives the package list as the answer
  ([vulnerability-scanning.md](spec/vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-041, Q-VULN-161, Q-VULN-162).
- The scanner pulls the image through Quader's own registry, on a scan listener of `packages` that accepts scan tokens only, checks and bounds
  every byte as the worker did, runs the analyser, and answers ([R-VULN-042](spec/vulnerability-scanning.md#r-vuln-042--the-scanners-pull-through-the-registry),
  [architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-037).
- The detection stays in the worker, on a document the worker writes anew from the answer (R-VULN-043, Q-VULN-164).
- What is not taken from the comparable design: a shared store for the queue and the reports, a credential in a message, an analyser that
  inherits the service's environment, a database download by the analyser. Quader's scanner holds no state between calls.
- The links are mutual TLS against the installation's CA (R-ARCH-038), behind ingress rules on their ports (ADR-154, R-HA-042); since
  ADR-215 each end presents its own kind's pair and checks the other's name.

**Consequences.** H-812 and H-818 are closed: an escape from the analyser reaches the scanner's own material (the image of the call, its
scan token, the TLS pair and the CA), and a hostile image ends a scanner's analysis and spends an attempt, never a worker. The chart renders
a fourth Deployment and two internal Services; the worker's spool shrinks back to 5 Gi and the scanner's is checked against its slots
(Q-HA-318). The first network seam between Quader's roles exists (ADR-153 allows it at a trust boundary). What stays open is recorded on
[security/image-scanning.md](security/image-scanning.md): no egress rule for the scanner (H-1036), the scanner's own pair in reach of its analyser
(H-1035, narrowed by ADR-215), analyses that share a pod with more than one slot (H-1037), the detection's analyser in the worker (H-1038).

**Alternatives considered.** A sandbox for the analyser inside the worker pod (needs privileges the pod does not have); a Kubernetes Job per
scan (needs a role that creates pods); the worker pushing the image's bytes to the scanner (the owner chose the pull); accept-and-poll with
reports kept in a shared store (Q-VULN-161).

**Revisit condition:** analyses that regularly outlast the scanner's drain window; a second caller of the scanner; a measured analyser that
needs more than the pod's 2 GiB for ordinary images.

**Spec:** [vulnerability-scanning.md](spec/vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-033 to R-VULN-036, R-VULN-041 to R-VULN-043, R-VULN-046,
Q-VULN-161 to Q-VULN-170; [architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-001, R-ARCH-036 to R-ARCH-038, Q-ARCH-527 to Q-ARCH-531;
[ha-and-helm.md](spec/ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-002, R-HA-042, R-HA-063, R-HA-065 to R-HA-067, Q-HA-316 to Q-HA-322;
[operations-and-observability.md](spec/operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-003, Q-OPS-215; [spec/README.md](spec/README.md) INV-2.

### ADR-213 · A scan token is a registry token a worker issues for one manifest, used only on the scan listener

**Status:** Accepted in its frame (owner decision of 2026-11-20: a registry token, pull only, that one repository, valid for minutes); the
mechanisms decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough. The system subject is named `vuln-scanner-trivy` since
[ADR-223](#adr-223--a-unit-that-runs-a-tool-carries-the-tools-name) (2026-11-21); the text below keeps the name of its day.

**Context.** The scanner must read the image it analyses and nothing else, and it may hold no key with which it could make a credential
itself. Quader's registry tokens (R-OCI-005) are self-contained, signed with a key derived from the key ring, and verified without a query;
each is bound to a Quader token and an endpoint.

**Decision.**
- The worker signs the token in process with the registry token's key, for each call; no token service, no Quader token, no principal row
  ([formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md) R-OCI-037, Q-OCI-226).
- Its claims name the system subject `image-scanner`, a scan ID, the endpoint `scan`, one grant entry of the repository and the image with
  `pull`, and the manifest's digest; it reaches that manifest by its digest and the blobs of its name, nothing else (Q-OCI-227).
- It lives `vulnerabilities.images.pull_timeout`, 10 minutes by default (Q-OCI-229), is accepted only on the scan listener of `packages`, and
  is decided by one fixed rule: read the repository it names while it is not disabled, never fill (Q-OCI-228).
- Its request is no delivery: no block gate, no download, no probe; it is system work, recorded under the repository and limited by nothing
  (Q-OCI-230, [usage-and-limits.md](spec/usage-and-limits.md) Q-LIM-66).
- It never reaches a log, a row, a job or an error text, and is not revoked one by one: it runs out.

**Consequences.** The grammar of a registry token gains a second kind; the enforcement point of the registry gains a digest pin; the decision
point gains a subject kind `system` (a rule of [authorization.md](spec/authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-015's evaluation). A compromised scanner
holds the tokens of the calls it receives, each good for one image for minutes (H-1041).

**Alternatives considered.** A built-in service account with a stored technical token (a long-lived secret in the worker); a grant of the
whole image name (every tag of the name); a token per blob issued on the scanner's request (the scanner would call the worker).

**Revisit condition:** a second system reader of the registry; pulls of the largest admitted image that do not fit the default lifetime.

**Spec:** [formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md) R-OCI-005, R-OCI-037, Q-OCI-226 to Q-OCI-230; [usage-and-limits.md](spec/usage-and-limits.md)
R-LIM-001, Q-LIM-66; [architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-037; [authorization.md](spec/authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-002, R-AUTHZ-008,
R-AUTHZ-015 (the subject kind `system` and its fixed rule); [endpoints.md](spec/endpoints.md) R-EP-001, R-EP-002, R-EP-010 (the endpoint
`scan`); [storage.md](spec/storage.md) R-STOR-015 and [api-and-ui.md](spec/api-and-ui.md) R-API-079 (no download);
[identity-and-authentication.md](spec/identity-and-authentication.md) R-AUTH-038 (no throttle on the scan listener).

### ADR-214 · The analyser's database lies in a repository of Quader

**Status:** Accepted (owner decisions of 2026-11-20: Quader is the cache of the analyser's database; one repository of the project `upstream`
holds it, `scanner-trivy`, always private, only for the scanner; switched on with the image scanning and by nothing else; no second way that
falls back to the public source; an installation without the internet names a local OCI repository of its own; its upstream address and an
account stay an administrator's, "scanner-trivy, genau wie von dir beschrieben"); the mechanisms decided by the development agent — owner
review at the walkthrough

**Context.** A task copied the database every six hours from the publisher into a private slot of the object store with a small OCI client of
its own, and air-gapped installations uploaded a file into a generic repository (Q-VULN-139). The owner: "Ich fände es doof, wenn Trivy …
dazu führt, dass jeder auch das zentrale ghcr nutzen muss", and the repository is called `scanner-trivy`, not `trivy-db`.

**Decision.**
- `vulnerabilities.images.database.repository` names the repository, `upstream/scanner-trivy` by default, and `database.image` the image,
  `aquasec/trivy-db` (its name at `mirror.gcr.io`, the address of `upstream/scanner-trivy`); the tag is the schema version the release
  reads (`2`), no setting (Q-VULN-171). A registry that publishes the database under another name is used through a remote of the
  installation's own project, named in both settings (R-VULN-044).
- The task resolves the tag through the repository in process, as the background download of R-REPO-065 runs a fill on the worker: the remote
  engine as system work, the format's gate and the engine's integrity check, charged to `system` and limited by nothing; a local repository is
  read through the item store (Q-VULN-172).
- The database in use is the source state's digest; the layer stays an item of its repository, and a worker reads it from there and keeps
  its unpacked copy by digest as before (Q-VULN-173).
- A run that cannot use the repository fails with a code that says why, shown on the sources screen with a link to the repository; nothing
  falls back (Q-VULN-174, R-VULN-045, Q-UI-850).
- Removed with no path from the state before: the table `vuln_image_db`, `vulnerabilities.sources.trivy` and its modes, the task's own OCI
  client, the file in a generic repository; the table goes with migration 00089 (00088 is the malware scanning's).

**Consequences.** The repository's upstream address and account, an administrator's for every well-known repository, decide the database
(H-813 restated). The database's bytes are counted in the usage store under the repository. The cache cleanup keeps the layer in use and
removes the older ones (R-REPO-070). The definition of `upstream/scanner-trivy` (its project, its fixed level, its include rule, that it
answers no client and has no state of its own) is [ADR-211](#adr-211--scanner-trivy-is-a-system-repository-of-upstream-that-only-the-image-scanning-reads)'s.

**Alternatives considered.** Keeping the private slot beside the repository (the owner removed it); pulling through Quader's registry like
the scanner (a listener hop and a token for work in the process that has the engine); a setting for the tag.

**Revisit condition:** the pinned analyser reads a second schema version; a repository's cleanup removes the layer often enough to show as
skipped scans.

**Spec:** [vulnerability-scanning.md](spec/vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-025, R-VULN-026, R-VULN-035, R-VULN-044, R-VULN-045,
Q-VULN-139, Q-VULN-171 to Q-VULN-176; [repositories-and-proxy.md](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-070; [storage.md](spec/storage.md)
R-STOR-045; [authorization.md](spec/authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-002, R-AUTHZ-008 (`system:image-database`); [api-and-ui.md](spec/api-and-ui.md)
R-UI-188, Q-UI-850.

### ADR-215 · Every kind of pod has a TLS pair and a name of its own, which the chart issues

**Status:** Accepted (owner decision of 2026-11-20: "Option c", on his question "Option A, macht es vielleicht Sinn das jeder Pod-kind sein
eigenes Cert erhält?"); the mechanisms decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough. The kind `scanner` is named
`vuln-scanner-trivy` since [ADR-223](#adr-223--a-unit-that-runs-a-tool-carries-the-tools-name) (2026-11-21); the text below keeps the
name of its day.

**Context.** Every pod of the chart served and presented the one pair of `tls.secretName`, which the operator issued with every Service name
of the installation. The scanner role of ADR-212 brought the first links between Quader's pods and showed what the one pair costs: the
scanner, whose analyser parses hostile images, held the pair the edge trusts for `api` and `packages` (H-1035); the links admitted any
certificate of the CA, and an operator's CA issues many (the owner's: 76, 28 of them with client authentication); and the owner's
certificate allowed server authentication only, so the scanner stayed not ready.

**Decision.**
- Four kinds of pod hold a pair: `api`, `packages`, `worker` and `scanner`. Pools and endpoint pools carry their role's; the Jobs and the backup
  pods none. Each pair names `<fullname>-<kind>.<namespace>.svc` and `<fullname>-ops.<namespace>.svc`; the pairs of `worker` and `scanner`
  allow client authentication ([ha-and-helm.md](spec/ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-063, Q-HA-346).
- With `tls.certManager.issuerRef` the chart renders a cert-manager Certificate per kind; without it, `tls.existingSecrets` names an existing Secret per kind, never
  one for two kinds. `tls.secretName`, `tls.ops` and `scanner.tls` are gone (Q-HA-347).
- A pod mounts its own kind's Secret only, with `ca.crt` where a link verifies with it; each Secret rotates on its own, without a restart.
- Each end of a link checks the other's name, listed exactly in its certificate ([architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-038,
  Q-ARCH-552; [vulnerability-scanning.md](spec/vulnerability-scanning.md) Q-VULN-185); the edge verifies each backend under its kind's name
  (Q-HA-348); the scrape under the operations name (Q-HA-349).
- The role `all` keeps one pair and may leave the names empty; the integration harness issues a pair per role (Q-ARCH-553).

**Consequences.** A taken-over analyser holds the scanner's pair, which passes nowhere the scanner does not pass already (H-1035). cert-manager
becomes the standard path of an installation with TLS. The chart knows every name and usage, so an operator writes neither; one who names
Secrets writes four. The operations name is shared by every pair (H-1071), the names are only as strong as the issuer's policy of who may
request them (H-1072), and a CA rollover reaches each kind with its own renewal (H-1073). An installation that ran the one pair changes its
values; nothing migrates it (pre-alpha).

**Alternatives considered.** One pair for all as built; a pair for the scanner only, the rest sharing (Q-HA-345); a pair per Deployment
(Q-HA-346); a name shared by `api` and `packages` toward the edge (Q-HA-348).

**Revisit condition:** a kind that runs code or holds secrets its siblings do not (a pool apart); an issuer policy that binds names to
namespaces, which would let the chart rely on it.

**Spec:** [ha-and-helm.md](spec/ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-031, R-HA-037, R-HA-063, R-HA-065 to R-HA-067, Q-HA-345 to Q-HA-349;
[architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-038, Q-ARCH-552, Q-ARCH-553; [vulnerability-scanning.md](spec/vulnerability-scanning.md)
R-VULN-041, R-VULN-042, Q-VULN-185; [endpoints.md](spec/endpoints.md) R-EP-008.

### ADR-220 · Every downloaded artifact is scanned for malware, and one switch lets only checked artifacts through

**Status:** Accepted (owner decisions of 2026-11-20, Q-MAL-1 to Q-MAL-5, Q-MAL-9, Q-MAL-11 to Q-MAL-15: "Alle Artefakte müssen
Viren-geprüft werden. Es muss im Admin-Bereich einen Schalter geben, der es ermöglicht, dass nur geprüfte Artefakte gedownloaded werden
können."); the mechanisms decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough

**Context.** The vulnerability scanning matches stored versions by name and never reads a blob (R-VULN-001); only container images are
analysed for what they hold. Nothing checked the bytes of an npm tarball, a `.deb` or a generic file against known malware.

**Decision.**
- The unit of a scan and of a verdict is the blob, by SHA-256, for the whole installation; a verdict follows the bytes into every repository
  that holds them ([malware-scanning.md](spec/malware-scanning.md) R-MAL-001, R-MAL-002).
- A commit makes the blob due and wakes a job of the worker on a queue of its own; discovery finds what came before; a download that waits
  under the switch raises the blob to the front (R-MAL-004, R-MAL-014).
- One gate in the two places every stored download passes refuses an infected blob always, and under the switch also a pending one after a
  wait of at most 25 s (`503` with `Retry-After`), an unscannable and a failed one (`403`), in each format's shape (R-MAL-013, R-MAL-016).
- The switch **Only checked artifacts can be downloaded** is one setting of the installation in the database, the administrator's, off by
  default; a repository may only make itself stricter (R-MAL-019, R-MAL-020).
- An infected blob is kept and refused; the instance auditor releases it per digest, with a reason, in the security dashboard
  (R-MAL-021, R-MAL-025).
- Rescans: content downloaded lately within a day of a new database, everything on a cycle of 30 days (R-MAL-009).
- A refusal ends resolution in every virtual repository, the OCI walk included; a find reaches the Bastions through the feed (R-MAL-018).

**Consequences.** The download statement joins two tables more; a new format is scanned and gated with no code of its own and adds one kit
case. Under the switch a remote fill is stored before it is served, and the first byte comes after the scan. What signatures do not find
stays unfound (H-1100); the gaps of the gate are on [security/malware-scanning.md](security/malware-scanning.md).

**Alternatives considered.** A verdict per item or per version; a scan on the upload path; a refusal at once or a wait without a bound; a
switch only per repository; deletion of infected content; a report mode.

**Revisit condition:** a measured scan time that keeps small downloads waiting past 25 s; false positives frequent enough that releases
become routine.

**Spec:** [malware-scanning.md](spec/malware-scanning.md) R-MAL-001 to R-MAL-031, Q-MAL-1 to Q-MAL-36; [formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md)
R-OCI-027, Q-OCI-240; [repositories-and-proxy.md](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-004, R-REPO-019, R-REPO-061, R-REPO-069;
[bastion.md](spec/bastion.md) R-BAS-015, Q-BAS-164; [api-and-ui.md](spec/api-and-ui.md) Q-API-370, Q-UI-870 to Q-UI-872.

### ADR-221 · The malware scanner is a kind of the role `scanner`, with `clamd` beside it, and reads one blob by its digest

**Status:** Accepted (owner decisions of 2026-11-20, Q-MAL-6, Q-MAL-7, Q-MAL-10); the mechanisms decided by the development agent — owner
review at the walkthrough. The kind `malware` is named `clamav`, and the Deployment `<fullname>-malware-scanner-clamav`, since
[ADR-223](#adr-223--a-unit-that-runs-a-tool-carries-the-tools-name) (2026-11-21); the text below keeps the names of its day.

**Context.** ADR-212 named "a second caller of the scanner" and ADR-213 "a second system reader of the registry" as their revisit
conditions; the malware scanning is both. Quader's image is static and distroless; `clamd` is a dynamically linked GPL program that holds
its signature database in memory and answers many scans.

**Decision.**
- A Deployment of its own of the role `scanner`, of the kind `malware` (`process.scanner_kind`), with a container `clamd` of ClamAV's
  official `_base` image beside it, pinned by digest, over a Unix socket of the pod; no secret of the installation in either container
  ([architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-036, [ha-and-helm.md](spec/ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-068).
- The worker calls it per blob over mutual TLS with a blob token: a scan token of the kind `blob` that names one digest and one repository
  that holds it, read only, for minutes, accepted on one route of the scan listener that names no format (R-MAL-005, R-MAL-006).
- The scanner unpacks what ClamAV cannot read (`ar`, zstd, containers above `max_file_size`) under bounds and hands the rest whole
  (R-MAL-007, R-MAL-008).
- The scanner loads the database in use from a route of the scan listener that admits its certificate name, before it is ready.

**Consequences.** The image scanning's role and links are reused; a fourth image is pinned; about 5 GiB of memory limits by default. A
taken-over `clamd` reaches the artifacts its pod scans at the same time (H-1105).

**Alternatives considered.** `clamd` beside the image analysis; `clamscan` per call; `libclamav` through cgo; each format's route with a
token; the worker pushing bytes; a role `malware-scanner`.

**Revisit condition:** ClamAV reads `ar` and zstd itself; a measured `clamd` that needs more than 2 GiB.

**Spec:** [malware-scanning.md](spec/malware-scanning.md) R-MAL-005 to R-MAL-008, Q-MAL-6, Q-MAL-7, Q-MAL-10, Q-MAL-25 to Q-MAL-27, Q-MAL-33;
[architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-036, R-ARCH-037, Q-ARCH-560; [endpoints.md](spec/endpoints.md) R-EP-010, Q-EP-95;
[authorization.md](spec/authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-002, Q-AUTHZ-340; [ha-and-helm.md](spec/ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-068, Q-HA-360, Q-HA-361;
[usage-and-limits.md](spec/usage-and-limits.md) Q-LIM-80.

### ADR-222 · `freshclam` fetches the ClamAV database, and Quader keeps it in `upstream/scanner-clamav`

**Status:** Accepted (owner decision of 2026-11-20, Q-MAL-8, in the frame of ADR-214: Quader is the cache of its scanners' databases); the
mechanisms decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough

**Context.** ClamAV's database is plain files, not an OCI artifact, and ClamAV's network supports `freshclam` and `cvdupdate` only:
scripted clients "are explicitly denied" and other methods "may be rate limited, or blocked" (ClamAV's FAQ, read 2026-11-20).

**Decision.**
- A container `freshclam` of the pinned image beside each worker that claims `malware`, a daemon seeded from the version in use, with no
  credential ([ha-and-helm.md](spec/ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-069).
- The task `malware-sync-db` stores each new version in `upstream/scanner-clamav`, a system repository of `upstream`, generic, local and
  private, which answers no client; the version in use is a row; versions older than 48 hours that are not in use go
  ([malware-scanning.md](spec/malware-scanning.md) R-MAL-010, R-MAL-011, [repositories-and-proxy.md](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md)
  R-REPO-075).
- Without internet, the setting names a local generic repository of the installation, filled with `cvdupdate`'s files (R-MAL-012).

**Consequences.** The first local repository in `upstream`, and a declaration that names its class (Q-REPO-411). `freshclam` reaches
ClamAV's network outside the repositories' egress rules (H-1106). Quader's own client makes no request to ClamAV's network.

**Alternatives considered.** A generic remote of ClamAV's network; `cvdupdate` as a CronJob writing into Quader; the official image with the
database through an OCI repository.

**Revisit condition:** ClamAV publishes its database as an OCI artifact, or names a supported client Quader could be.

**Spec:** [malware-scanning.md](spec/malware-scanning.md) R-MAL-010 to R-MAL-012, Q-MAL-8, Q-MAL-28; [repositories-and-proxy.md](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md)
R-REPO-066, R-REPO-075, Q-REPO-410, Q-REPO-411; [ha-and-helm.md](spec/ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-069, Q-HA-362.

### ADR-223 · A unit that runs a tool carries the tool's name

**Status:** Accepted (owner decision of 2026-11-21: "Also immer so benennen, dass man sieht um welches Tool es sich handelt und das man
später evtl mal mehrere Tools nebeneinander laufen lassen kann."); the boundary decided by the development agent — owner review at the
walkthrough. Supersedes the names of the kinds `scanner` and `malware-scanner` in [ADR-215](#adr-215--every-kind-of-pod-has-a-tls-pair-and-a-name-of-its-own-which-the-chart-issues)
and [ADR-221](#adr-221--the-malware-scanner-is-a-kind-of-the-role-scanner-with-clamd-beside-it-and-reads-one-blob-by-its-digest), and the
values `image` and `malware` of `process.scanner_kind`, and the system subjects of [ADR-213](#adr-213--a-scan-token-is-a-registry-token-a-worker-issues-for-one-manifest-used-only-on-the-scan-listener)
and ADR-221. The boundary was moved by the owner later the same day ("Vom Builder gemeldet, nicht geändert: direkt nacharbeiten. Das ist
alles wichtig und muss umgesetzt werden.", [ha-and-helm.md](spec/ha-and-helm.md#q-ha-373--every-name-an-operator-or-an-auditor-reads-of-a-scanner-unit-carries-its-tool) Q-HA-373): the system subjects, the readiness checks, the link labels and
the log components carry the unit's name too.

**Context.** The owner looked at his cluster: "Die Deployments quader-scanner und quader-malware-scanner sind mir nicht differenziert genug.
quader-scanner ist trivy? Dann quader-vuln-scanner-trivy. quader-malware-scanner hätte ich auch lieber quader-malware-scanner-calmav
genannt." ("calmav" is a typo of his; the tool is ClamAV.) Both Deployments run the role `scanner`; the name of neither said which tool it
wraps, and neither left room for a second tool of the same purpose.

**Decision.**
- A kind of pod that exists to run one third-party tool, and everything named after it, is named `<purpose>-scanner-<tool>`:
  `vuln-scanner-trivy` and `malware-scanner-clamav`, with their Deployments, Services, disruption budgets, autoscalers, policies,
  Certificates and Secrets, component labels, certificate names and keys of `tls.existingSecrets`
  ([ha-and-helm.md](spec/ha-and-helm.md) Q-HA-372).
- The chart's value blocks are `vulnScannerTrivy` and `malwareScannerClamav`, one per unit; `process.scanner_kind` takes `trivy` or
  `clamav`, default `trivy` ([architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) Q-ARCH-561).
- Every name an operator or an auditor reads of a unit carries it too (the owner's decision, Q-HA-373): the label `listener` of its link
  and its listener, the log field `component` of its process, the system subject of its reads (`system:vuln-scanner-trivy`,
  `system:malware-scanner-clamav`, also the usage records' credential) and its readiness check in camel case, `vulnScannerTrivy` and
  `malwareScannerClamav`, in its own process and in the one that calls it ([operations-and-observability.md](spec/operations-and-observability.md#q-ops-221--a-scanner-units-readiness-check-is-its-name-in-camel-case-the-same-in-the-process-that-calls-it) Q-OPS-221,
  [Q-OPS-222](spec/operations-and-observability.md#q-ops-222--the-loader-of-the-signature-database-logs-as-its-unit)).
- What is the same whichever tool does the work keeps its purpose's name: the role `scanner`, the jobs, queues and tasks, the configuration
  keys `vulnerabilities.images.scanner.*` and `malware.scanner.*`, the metric names, the error codes and the subjects of the worker's own
  tasks.

**Consequences.** A second tool for a purpose is a unit beside the first. An installation upgraded from the old names loses the old
objects and gets new ones; the Secrets cert-manager wrote for the old kinds stay behind. The Service `<fullname>-malware-scanner-clamav`
is a DNS label only for a `<fullname>` of at most 40 characters; the chart refuses a longer one and no longer cuts `<fullname>`
([ha-and-helm.md](spec/ha-and-helm.md#q-ha-374--the-chart-refuses-a-fullname-too-long-for-the-names-it-builds-and-never-cuts-it) Q-HA-374). Dashboards, alert rules and log queries that select the old link labels, check names, components or
credentials are changed by hand. The rule stands in the repository's `CLAUDE.md`.

**Alternatives considered.** The tool's name on everything a scanner touches; the tool's name on the Deployment only; the values of
`process.scanner_kind` kept as purposes, or without a default.

**Revisit condition:** a second tool for one purpose, which needs the worker's link per purpose to become a list.

**Spec:** [ha-and-helm.md](spec/ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-002, R-HA-028, R-HA-029, R-HA-063, R-HA-065 to R-HA-068, Q-HA-372 to Q-HA-374;
[architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-001, R-ARCH-036, R-ARCH-038, Q-ARCH-561; [operations-and-observability.md](spec/operations-and-observability.md)
R-OPS-001, R-OPS-008, Q-OPS-221, Q-OPS-222; [authorization.md](spec/authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-002; [usage-and-limits.md](spec/usage-and-limits.md)
R-LIM-001; [formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md) R-OCI-037; [malware-scanning.md](spec/malware-scanning.md) R-MAL-006.

### ADR-224 · A scanner reports itself through the scan listener, and `packages` keeps its row

**Status:** Accepted (owner decision of 2026-11-21: "Also immer so benennen, dass man sieht um welches Tool es sich handelt und das man
später evtl mal mehrere Tools nebeneinander laufen lassen kann." and, to the report that no screen named a scanner pod or its tool: "Vom
Builder gemeldet, nicht geändert: direkt nacharbeiten. Das ist alles wichtig und muss umgesetzt werden."); the mechanism decided by the
development agent — owner review at the walkthrough. Supersedes
[Q-OPS-215](spec/operations-and-observability.md#q-ops-215--the-scanner-has-no-row-in-the-replica-registry-and-shows-through-its-metrics-and-the-workers-codes).

**Context.** A scanner holds no secret of the installation
([ADR-212](#adr-212--the-image-analysis-runs-in-a-role-scanner-that-holds-no-secret)) and so no row of the replica registry. The System page
showed no scanner, **Settings › Malware scanning** two counts, the image scanning's page nothing.

**Decision.**
- Each replica of the role `scanner` reports itself every `system.heartbeat_interval` with `PUT /scan/v1/replicas/{uid}` to the scan
  listener of `packages` it already reaches with its kind's certificate, and signs off with `DELETE` at its clean shutdown
  ([operations-and-observability.md](spec/operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-048, Q-OPS-223).
- `packages` takes the kind from the verified client certificate (`vulnerabilities.images.registry.client_name` is `trivy`,
  `malware.scan_listener.client_name` `clamav`), checks the report's size and shape, and writes a row of `scanner_replica`, a table apart
  from the registry, on PostgreSQL's clock; a kind holds at most 64 live rows; the rows go by the registry's rule.
- `GET /api/v1/system/scanners` (`settings:read`) lists the kinds and the rows (Q-API-381); one shared table shows them on the System page,
  under the summary of the malware settings and in the section **Image scanners** of the advisory sources (Q-UI-897).

**Consequences.** Every scanner pod is seen, ready or not, with its tool's version; the scanner gains no credential and no route of
another kind. A taken-over scanner can make an administrator read made-up rows of its own kind (H-1161). Without TLS no scanner is listed.

**Alternatives considered.** The worker records the replicas its calls reach; the worker probes every pod through a headless Service; the
scanner writes the registry with a credential.

**Revisit condition:** a second tool for one purpose, which adds a kind and its certificate's name; a need to tie a row to its pod beyond
the kind's certificate.

**Spec:** [operations-and-observability.md](spec/operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-003, R-OPS-048, Q-OPS-215, Q-OPS-223;
[api-and-ui.md](spec/api-and-ui.md) R-UI-038, Q-API-381, Q-UI-897; [architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-036, R-ARCH-037;
[ha-and-helm.md](spec/ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-002, R-HA-065, R-HA-066, R-HA-068; [malware-scanning.md](spec/malware-scanning.md) R-MAL-023;
[vulnerability-scanning.md](spec/vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-022.

### ADR-225 · The ClamAV updater is a Deployment of its own, and ClamAV's definitions are a repository format

**Status:** Accepted (owner decision of 2026-11-21: "Gliedere Freshclam aus, es wird als seperates deployment ins helm integriert. Default
reicht uns 1 replica. Diese Instanz fetched die online-ressource, und wir kommen regelmäßig bei unserer freshclam vorbei und besorgen uns
ggf. das aktuelle update. Außerdem möchte ich, dass wir das freshclam artefakt als spezifisches ClamAV-Repo in Upstream einbindbar machen.");
the mechanisms decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough; who reads the definitions when they are switched on was
decided by the owner the same day (Q-REPO-415: Public by default, the levels below it a detail, client certificates in addition). Supersedes the container `freshclam` of the worker and the repository `upstream/scanner-clamav` of
[ADR-222](#adr-222--freshclam-fetches-the-clamav-database-and-quader-keeps-it-in-upstreamscanner-clamav), whose frame stands: the tool
the ClamAV project supports fetches, and Quader keeps each set. Reads [ADR-223](#adr-223--a-unit-that-runs-a-tool-carries-the-tools-name)'s
pattern as `<purpose>-<function>-<tool>`.

**Context.** `freshclam` ran in every worker pod that claimed `malware`, in the network position of the pod that holds the installation's
credentials, one fetcher per worker replica. ClamAV's guidance is one private mirror per network for more than ten hosts, and a company
runs many ClamAV installations of its own.

**Decision.**
- `freshclam` runs in the Deployment `malware-updater-freshclam`, one replica, `Recreate`, exempt from the rule of two, beside a `quader`
  container of the role `scanner` and the kind `freshclam` that seeds its directory from the set in use and lists it over mutual TLS
  ([ha-and-helm.md](spec/ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-069, [malware-scanning.md](spec/malware-scanning.md) R-MAL-032,
  [architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) Q-ARCH-562). It fetches whole signed containers (`ScriptedUpdates no`), from ClamAV's network or an
  internal mirror an installation names.
- The worker's task asks the updater every 30 minutes, fetches only what is new, verifies each container's signature against ClamAV's key
  before it stores it, and records the set in use (R-MAL-010, R-MAL-033).
- The definitions are the repository `upstream/clamav` of the format `clamav`, system only: one package per database, every piece of
  metadata of a version shown, the set in use and the previous one kept and the rest removed, their metadata kept for the rescan cycle
  ([formats/clamav.md](spec/formats/clamav.md), R-MAL-034, [repositories-and-proxy.md](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-075).
- An administrator switches **ClamAV definition updates** on among the upstream registries; the endpoint
  `/api/clamav/upstream/clamav` then serves the set in use to every stock `freshclam` with `PrivateMirror`, answers never `403` or `429`, and
  is public by the recommendation put to the owner.
- The format contract gains `catalog.Facts.SystemOnly` (a fact; the contract's version does not change).

**Consequences.** The worker no longer reaches ClamAV's network; one pod does, which an egress policy admits by label. A taken-over updater
can hold back new sets but cannot get a container stored that ClamAV did not sign. The chart refuses a `<fullname>` above 37 characters.
The owner's installation retires `scanner-clamav` at its next `quader migrate`, and its updater fetches the first set whole.

**Alternatives considered.** The updater pushing into Quader; a shared volume; patches and a `.cld`; a role `updater`; a web server image;
a key `scanner-clamav`; a preset repository; serving patch files for `DatabaseMirror`; third-party signature sets as sources.

**Revisit condition:** a `429` or a `403` from ClamAV's network to the one updater; a database ClamAV publishes without the legacy signature;
a third tool unit that is no scanner.

**Spec:** [malware-scanning.md](spec/malware-scanning.md) R-MAL-010 to R-MAL-012, R-MAL-032 to R-MAL-034, Q-MAL-93 to Q-MAL-101;
[formats/clamav.md](spec/formats/clamav.md) R-CLAMAV-001 to R-CLAMAV-010, Q-CLAMAV-1 to Q-CLAMAV-14;
[repositories-and-proxy.md](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-073, R-REPO-075, Q-REPO-413 to Q-REPO-416;
[ha-and-helm.md](spec/ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-069, Q-HA-375 to Q-HA-377; [api-and-ui.md](spec/api-and-ui.md) R-API-083, R-UI-187, R-UI-188,
R-UI-194, Q-API-382, Q-UI-903 to Q-UI-905; [endpoints.md](spec/endpoints.md) R-EP-008, R-EP-010, Q-EP-96;
[operations-and-observability.md](spec/operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-010, R-OPS-048, Q-OPS-224;
[architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-036, Q-ARCH-562.

### ADR-226 · Quader detects, reads and verifies the signatures of every format, and shows them at the artifact

**Status:** Accepted (owner decisions of 2026-11-21, Q-SIG-1, Q-SIG-5 to Q-SIG-9, Q-SIG-12, Q-SIG-14 to Q-SIG-16: "Quader muss in Zukunft auch
das feststellen, auslesen und verifizieren von Signaturen auf (wenn möglich) allen Artefaktarten unterstützen."); the mechanisms decided by the
development agent — owner review at the walkthrough. Stage 1 of three; stage 2 (Quader signs) and stage 3 (a gate per repository) get their
own specification.

**Context.** Debian was the only format whose signatures Quader verified (a remote's releases against `deb.upstreamKeys`). OCI stored
referrers and showed signature tags as versions; npm's local publish dropped the attestations and the keys and attestations endpoints answered
404; NuGet kept the signature inside the package unread; Ansible passed `signatures[]` through; a generic `.asc` was an ordinary file. No table
held a fact "signed by" at an artifact, and the format contract had no place for one.

**Decision.**
- Three steps, stored at the signed content: detect at every place the format defines, read what the signature carries, verify that it
  matches the content and that an anchor knows the signer; the original object is kept ([signatures.md](spec/signatures.md) R-SIG-001,
  R-SIG-003, R-SIG-005, R-SIG-006).
- The integrity verdict once per signature object and subject for the installation; attachments per repository; trust per scope, the
  installation's or a project's; an anchor change recomputes trust and reads no artifact (R-SIG-003, R-SIG-004, R-SIG-008, R-SIG-012).
- A background job of the worker at ingest with libraries in process (sigstore-go, notation-core-go with tspclient-go, digitorus/pkcs7 with digitorus/timestamp,
  go-crypto), measured at 4.76 MiB more binary; no tool and no Deployment (R-SIG-011, R-SIG-014).
- A signature is valid if it was valid when made; a log entry or a trusted timestamp proves the time, else Quader's receipt; no revocation
  lists; an administrator blocks a signer (R-SIG-007, R-SIG-020).
- Four visible states; the badge stands for the publisher's signature and provenance; a registry's signature is "Origin confirmed by
  registry" in the details; stage 1 shows and alarms and refuses nothing (R-SIG-009, R-SIG-038).
- A remote fetches its content's signatures in the background, bounded; mirror passes take them (R-SIG-025, R-SIG-026).
- The origin of an upload, for a CI job its verified claims, is recorded at the item (R-SIG-010).

**Consequences.** Six formats gain a detector each, npm two endpoints, OCI a cascade and attachment tags that are no versions; the worker reads
hostile signature containers (H-1166); Docker Hub sees up to four pulls more per signed image fetched (R-SIG-026).

**Alternatives considered.** Verification at display; a unit without secrets per tool; pass-through only for remotes; strict expiry as the
clients; revocation lists; a gate in stage 1.

**Revisit condition:** a library flaw that a bound cannot contain (then the scanners' pattern); a measured cost of the trust recomputation that
keeps readers on stale rows for long.

**Spec:** [signatures.md](spec/signatures.md) R-SIG-001 to R-SIG-043, Q-SIG-1 to Q-SIG-46; [formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md) R-OCI-016,
R-OCI-026; [formats/npm.md](spec/formats/npm.md) R-NPM-001, R-NPM-027; [formats/nuget.md](spec/formats/nuget.md) R-NUGET-005;
[formats/ansible.md](spec/formats/ansible.md) R-ANS-013, Q-ANS-14; [formats/generic.md](spec/formats/generic.md) R-GENERIC-002;
[formats/debian.md](spec/formats/debian.md) R-DEB-023; [repositories-and-proxy.md](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-004;
[api-and-ui.md](spec/api-and-ui.md) R-UI-002, R-UI-158; [README.md](spec/README.md) INV-4.

### ADR-227 · Trust anchors of four kinds in three scopes, and the administrator decides whether project Owners add their own

**Status:** Accepted (owner decisions of 2026-11-21, Q-SIG-2 to Q-SIG-4 and the reading r4 of Q-SIG-16: "Ein Admin muss also gültige
unternehmens CAs einstellen können … Er muss einstellen können, ob Projekt-Owner weitere CAs für ihr Projekt konfigurieren können (default
nein)."); the mechanisms decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** "Company CAs" cover two of the four families of trust (certificate chains and, through an own Sigstore, Sigstore identities);
Debian, Ansible and generic `.asc` files need OpenPGP keys, npm's registry and cosign's key pairs raw public keys.

**Decision.**
- Four kinds under one setting **Trust anchors**: CA certificate (code signing or timestamping, an optional subject restriction), OpenPGP key,
  public key, Sigstore identity against the public or an own trust root ([signatures.md](spec/signatures.md) R-SIG-015).
- Scopes: shipped (the public Sigstore root, npm's keys, Debian's and Ubuntu's keyrings, nuget.org's certificates and its timestamping roots;
  each can be switched off; the public root and npm's keys refreshed through TUF), from the Helm values (read-only, applied by `quader
  migrate`), the administrator's, and a project's (R-SIG-016 to R-SIG-018).
- One switch of the installation, off by default: when on, a project's Owner adds anchors that hold only in the project's scope; the
  administrator sees and removes them; off again they stay stored and stop applying (R-SIG-019).
- `security-settings:write` writes anchors, blocks and the switch; `settings:read` reads them (R-SIG-021).

**Consequences.** "Verified · public" means a signer Quader ships and keeps current; "Verified · internal" an anchor of the company or the
project. A project Owner's anchor is shown to every reader of the project's repositories (H-1167). Without internet the public root ages with
the release (H-1170).

**Alternatives considered.** CA certificates only; anchors only in Helm or only in the UI; a list of public code-signing CAs; a capability of
its own.

**Revisit condition:** more than a handful of identities against one own Sigstore root (a root object of its own); a public CA list a source
keeps current.

**Spec:** [signatures.md](spec/signatures.md) R-SIG-015 to R-SIG-021, Q-SIG-2 to Q-SIG-4, Q-SIG-27, Q-SIG-29 to Q-SIG-31, Q-SIG-39;
[authorization.md](spec/authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-010, R-AUTHZ-037.

### ADR-228 · The format contract declares every format's signatures, and a signature is never a version

**Status:** Accepted (owner decisions of 2026-11-21, the readings r5 and r6 of Q-SIG-16: "Das muss bei zukünftigen Registries automatisch mit
berücksichtigt werden." and "von der Darstellung her, soll eine Signatur aber nicht alleine stehen sondern klar einem Image zugeordnet
werden"); the mechanisms decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** No standard covers every format, so "automatically for future registries" cannot be a format-neutral detector. OCI's referrers
tag and cosign's tags were versions of their image.

**Decision.**
- The contract gains `Format.Signatures() SignatureAdapter`: a declaration (the kinds, where they live, what they cover, how a client gets
  them, or none with the reason) and a detector over what a commit stores; `Base` returns nil and `Register` refuses nil, so a format without
  the declaration does not start; `ContractVersion` rises to 8 ([signatures.md](spec/signatures.md) R-SIG-022). The block joins R-ARCH-008
  with the code.
- Kit check 18 holds the declaration, one detected case per kind, and that no signature becomes a version.
- OCI's `sha256-<hex>` tags and their `.sig`, `.att`, `.sbom` forms are attachment tags without a version; they and referrers stay on the
  wire unchanged and follow their image on delete, the trash, eviction, retention, copy and mirror (R-SIG-024, R-SIG-025).

**Consequences.** Every format changes in one change; a new format adds one kit case. Version lists, counts, search, download counts and the
image scanning see an image without its attachments.

**Alternatives considered.** An optional interface; versions with a flag every list filters; recognising attachment tags by content only.

**Revisit condition:** a release tag of the form `sha256-<64 hex>` in real use.

**Built** (stage 1, package 1): the contract at version 8 with every format's declaration and detector, kit check 18, the store and the
hooks that record candidates and origins (Q-SIG-47 to Q-SIG-52), and the OCI attachment tags without a version row.

**Spec:** [signatures.md](spec/signatures.md) R-SIG-022 to R-SIG-025, Q-SIG-32, Q-SIG-43, Q-SIG-47; [formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md) R-OCI-016,
R-OCI-018, R-OCI-026; [architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-008, R-ARCH-010.

### ADR-229 · The scanner unit detects as well, and the analyser comes from its own image

**Status:** Accepted (owner decisions of 2026-11-21, after he saw no Trivy container in the scanner pod and asked why the worker runs the
analyser too and why the scanner's answer counts as untrusted: "Option B, nach der umbenennung. Trivy dann aus den anderen Images
entfernen.", and for where the scanner's analyser comes from: "Option b"); the mechanisms decided by the development agent — owner review at
the walkthrough. Supersedes the detection in the worker of [ADR-212](#adr-212--the-image-analysis-runs-in-a-role-scanner-that-holds-no-secret),
whose frame stands: the analysis runs in a role without secrets, called by the worker job.

**Context.** The unit `vuln-scanner-trivy` analysed an image; the worker ran the same analyser a second time for the detection, against the
database it kept, after writing the scanner's answer anew under limits because the answer counts as untrusted. The analyser, a static binary
of 163 MB, lay in the one image that `api`, `packages`, `worker` and both scanner units run (239 MB in all).

**Decision.**
- The scanner unit does both steps: `POST /scan/v1/detections` carries the stored analysis, names the database and the analyser version, and
  answers the analyser's report; the analysis stays once per manifest digest and analyser version, so a new database reads no layer
  ([vulnerability-scanning.md](spec/vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-048). The worker runs no tool, keeps the analysis as answered after a
  bounded check (R-VULN-043), and reads the report in Go under limits. The rewrite and its fidelity test go.
- Each scanner pod keeps the database read-only: a second container of the Quader image, of the kind `trivy-db`, reads it through a route of
  the scan listener with the pod's certificate, as the malware scanner reads its signatures, and writes it into a volume that the scanner's
  container mounts read-only (R-VULN-049, [architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) Q-ARCH-564). No scanner fetches it from the internet.
- The analyser comes from its own official image, pinned by digest (`TRIVY_IMAGE`), which an init container copies into a volume the scanner
  mounts read-only; the chart's `trivy.image` holds the same value under a chart test, one Renovate group moves both, and the digests of the
  release archive go ([ha-and-helm.md](spec/ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-070). The release image carries no analyser.
- The scanner's process is not dumpable; detections share the analyses' slots; after a new database the images without a detection go first.
- The role `all` builds no image scanner; the test profiles run the image scanning only where a test reads it.

**Consequences.** H-1038 closes: no analyser parses an image's values in a pod with secrets. A second tool with a database of its own would
be a unit beside the first and nothing in the worker. The release image shrinks by 163 MB, and every kind leg that does not scan images
loads that much less. A node pulls a third party's image when a scanner pod starts (H-1182), each scanner pod holds about 1.7 GiB of database
and reads 142.6 MB per new one, and a scanner pod whose own process is taken over answers the detections it serves (H-1181).

**Alternatives considered.** The detection in the worker with the analyser in the common image (option A put to the owner); a second image
with the analyser built per release; the database in the scanner's own spool; a hash of the database per detection; Landlock; an image
volume; the analyser version as a release constant; the version from the scanners' reports.

**Revisit condition:** Trivy gains a way to read its database from a process of another user; image volumes are on by default in the oldest
Kubernetes the chart supports; detections wait visibly behind analyses.

**Built (2026-11-21):** the detection in the scanner, the loader of the kind `trivy-db` with the container `database` and the volume
`trivy-db`, the check of the kept analysis, one analysis per digest, the process not dumpable, the order of work, the role `all` without a
scanner; then the analyser from its own image: the init container `trivy`, the volume `trivy-bin`, the pin `TRIVY_IMAGE` with its chart
test and Renovate group, the release image without the analyser (246.5 MB to 83.3 MB on arm64), `make trivy` out of the image, and the test
profiles that start the scanner units in `vuln` alone (Q-HA-382, Q-HA-386, Q-HA-387).

**Spec:** [vulnerability-scanning.md](spec/vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-033 to R-VULN-036, R-VULN-041, R-VULN-043, R-VULN-044,
R-VULN-046, R-VULN-048, R-VULN-049, Q-VULN-196 to Q-VULN-206; [ha-and-helm.md](spec/ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-002, R-HA-065 to R-HA-067,
R-HA-070, Q-HA-378 to Q-HA-383, Q-HA-386 to Q-HA-388; [architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-036, R-ARCH-037, Q-ARCH-563, Q-ARCH-564;
[operations-and-observability.md](spec/operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-048, Q-OPS-225; [security/image-scanning.md](security/image-scanning.md)
H-1181, H-1182.

### ADR-230 · Quader signs with one identity per installation: npm's registry signatures and a receipt attestation of every artifact, signed in the worker

**Status:** Accepted (owner decisions of 2026-11-21, Q-SIG-10 to Q-SIG-13 and the reading r8 of Q-SIG-16: "Quader ist ebenso in der Lage
Artefakte zu signieren, dafür muss aber erst ein Zertifikat in Quader über Helm oder das Frontend gepflegt werden."); the mechanisms
decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough. Stage 2 of three; stage 1 is ADR-226 to ADR-228, stage 3 (a gate per
repository) gets its own specification.

**Context.** Debian was the only format Quader signed, with a key per repository. A local npm package carried no registry signature, so
`npm audit signatures` reported it as missing through a virtual repository with a remote member (H-1176), and nothing let a consumer check
that an artifact went through Quader and what its checks said. Three facts of the clients, read in their source on 2026-11-21, bound the
design: npm accepts only P-256 registry keys, compares a version's publish time with its key's expiry and aborts the whole run on an expired
or unknown key; npm verifies attestations only with a public log entry against the public Sigstore root; cosign 3 stops reading an older
`.sig` or `.att` tag as soon as any Sigstore bundle stands among an image's referrers.

**Decision.**
- One signing identity per installation: an ECDSA P-256 key and a code-signing certificate of the company's CA, from a Secret of the Helm
  values (cert-manager may issue it; mounted into the worker pods only; the values win) or uploaded in the admin area as a certificate for a
  key Quader makes and seals by the key ring; states pending, announced, current, previous, retired ([signatures.md](spec/signatures.md)
  R-SIG-045 to R-SIG-047, [ha-and-helm.md](spec/ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-071).
- Only the worker holds the key; the job `signing` signs right after a commit and signs what was stored before by discovery (R-SIG-049).
- A new key is announced before it signs; a lock refuses a signature after its key's switch; npm signatures of a previous key stay valid
  with its expiry; attestations are made again by the new identity; no keys are on npm's wire while no identity is current (R-SIG-048).
- npm: every version of a local repository gets a registry signature, listed keys in the keyid form npmjs uses; remote and virtual
  repositories keep their upstream's and their winning member's; H-1176 closes for an installation with an identity (R-SIG-050).
- Every artifact a user's repository receives gets a receipt attestation: an in-toto statement with a predicate of Quader's own (receipt,
  origin, integrity states, the malware and vulnerability snapshots with their dates, no trust state) in a Sigstore bundle with a DSSE
  envelope and the leaf certificate, without a log or a timestamp, verifiable offline with `cosign verify-attestation --trusted-root`
  against a trusted root Quader serves (R-SIG-051 to R-SIG-053).
- Attestations are signatures of the store of stage 1 with the source `issued`; for OCI a referrer, but only where it hides no older cosign
  signature; for every other format and for such an image through the API, never through npm's attestations endpoint (R-SIG-054).
- The format contract gains `AttestationSubjects` and rises to version 10 (R-SIG-044; written as 9 before the gate of stage 3 took 9, ADR-231): the format is asked when the job signs, for stored items with the host (Q-SIG-180).

**Consequences.** `npm audit signatures` passes for local packages; a cluster can demand Quader's receipt of most images; the worker's key can
make clients believe anything was received here (H-1187), an uploaded key can be opened by every role with the key ring (H-1188); the
attestation's time is Quader's claim (H-1189); an image with an older cosign signature has its receipt only through the API (H-1185); about
2.5 KiB of PostgreSQL per attested artifact, written again per rotation.

**Alternatives considered.** RSA or a second key for npm; signing in the role that answers the upload; re-signing remote npm packages; npm's
publish attestation; SLSA's verification summary; a bundle with the chain, the older cosign layout, a Notary Project signature; a timestamp
authority or a log; a referrer on every image; a sibling file; a hardware key store.

**Revisit condition:** the owner's company Sigstore in operation (a timestamp or a log); cosign reading older tags beside bundles; a company CA
that issues RSA only; stage 3, where a passing gate may issue a verification summary.

**Spec:** [signatures.md](spec/signatures.md) R-SIG-044 to R-SIG-060, Q-SIG-53 to Q-SIG-74, H-1176, H-1183 to H-1186;
[ha-and-helm.md](spec/ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-071, Q-HA-385; [formats/npm.md](spec/formats/npm.md) R-NPM-027, H-32;
[formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md) R-OCI-016; [api-and-ui.md](spec/api-and-ui.md) R-UI-002, R-API-030;
[operations-and-observability.md](spec/operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-016; [README.md](spec/README.md) INV-4;
[security/artifact-signatures.md](security/artifact-signatures.md) H-1187 to H-1193.

### ADR-231 · A repository can serve only artifacts with a verified signature: a gate at download for every format, judged from stored verdicts and failing closed

**Status:** Accepted (owner decision of 2026-11-21, Q-SIG-9 (b), against the development agent's recommendation: "besides display and alarm,
per repository a detail setting 'only artifacts with a verified signature', optionally of chosen anchors"; with Q-SIG-14 the third stage);
the mechanisms decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough. Stage 3 of three; stage 1 is ADR-226 to ADR-228, stage 2
ADR-230.

**Context.** Stage 1 stores per signature an integrity verdict and per scope a trust row with every anchor that knows the signer, recomputed
alone when anchors change; it refuses nothing. The malware gate decides at the two serve points every download passes, waits a bounded time
for a scan and answers in each client's shape; the vulnerability block refuses an image at its manifest. Three facts bound the design: half
the formats carry their signature in a request of its own after the artifact (OCI, generic, Ansible); a signature over an image index commits
to its platform manifests, and `cosign sign` of a tag signs only the index (read in cosign's source on 2026-11-21); the trust rows lag a
change of anchors by minutes, while a narrowing is only a subtraction.

**Decision.**
- A repository's setting `signatures.onlyVerified`, with `signatures.anchors` naming accepted anchors by scope and key, or any anchor of the
  repository's scope; on every class of every format but Debian; not in a creation flow; no installation switch, no project default, no
  report mode; switching it off and accepting more anchors are weakenings an Owner may not make ([signatures.md](spec/signatures.md)
  R-SIG-061).
- What passes is what shows a verified badge: a `publisher` or `provenance` signature whose trust row knows an accepted anchor; a registry's
  signature alone never, Quader's own never; one passing signature is enough (R-SIG-062).
- The format names what the gate judges (an artifact with what covers it, an attachment, a signature file, nothing) through a method of the
  signature adapter, and the contract rises by one; OCI is gated at its manifests, an index covers its platform manifests, an attachment is
  known by its content (R-SIG-063).
- The gate acts at download, at the malware gate's serve points and at OCI's manifest handlers; each gate that applies (the addressed
  repository's, the holding member's) judges in its own scope; a refusal ends a virtual walk (R-SIG-064, R-SIG-065).
- A narrowing reaches the gate at once: it subtracts removed or narrowed anchors and newer blocks from a stale trust row, from the replica's
  snapshot; a widening waits for the recomputation (R-SIG-066).
- A pending artifact gets priority work and a bounded wait shared with the malware gate's, then `503` with `Retry-After`; a remote's fill is
  held; nothing is served without a decision (R-SIG-067, R-SIG-069).
- `403 signature_not_verified` and `503 signature_check_pending` in the shapes the formats render for the malware gate; a release per
  repository and artifact by whoever triages in the security dashboard; a preview before switching on and an impact before a narrowing
  (R-SIG-068, R-SIG-070 to R-SIG-072).

**Consequences.** A curated repository refuses what no accepted signer signed, in every format but Debian; a team cannot be locked out
without seeing it; under "any anchor" any identity of the public Sigstore passes (H-1194), and a project Owner's own anchor while project
anchors are allowed (H-1195); an image's blobs and files that read as signatures pass (H-1196, H-1197); metadata documents still list refused
versions (H-1199); Docker and `ansible-galaxy` may fail a first pull through a gated remote once (H-1200); every format implements one more
method. The contract rises to version 9 with that method and `SignatureVerdicts.Refuse`, which judges the stored tag of a remote OCI
repository (Q-SIG-132; built with stage 3's first package).

**Alternatives considered.** An installation switch; a gate at upload; a registry's signature as passing; anchor IDs or a per-repository
identity pattern; gating by route kind; every OCI blob gated; trusting stale trust rows or treating them as pending; a code per reason;
releases per digest for the installation or by the Owner; curated metadata documents; a report mode; a verification summary of the decision;
an end-to-end case.

**Revisit condition:** a project that wants every repository gated (a project default); a Debian gate on a remote's covering release (asked
of the owner); a client that verifies Quader's decision itself (a verification summary).

**Spec:** [signatures.md](spec/signatures.md) R-SIG-061 to R-SIG-078, Q-SIG-75 to Q-SIG-95, H-1199, H-1200;
[security/artifact-signatures.md](security/artifact-signatures.md) H-1194 to H-1198; [repositories-and-proxy.md](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md)
R-REPO-004, R-REPO-061; [malware-scanning.md](spec/malware-scanning.md) R-MAL-013; [bastion.md](spec/bastion.md) R-BAS-015;
[formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md) R-OCI-007, R-OCI-009; [api-and-ui.md](spec/api-and-ui.md) R-UI-087;
[operations-and-observability.md](spec/operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-016.

### ADR-232 · The guide data names the addresses on which a client certificate reads the repository

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough. An addition to the format contract frozen by
[ADR-141](#adr-141--the-format-contract-is-frozen-at-version-1); the contract's version does not change.

**Context.** The owner decided on 2026-11-21 that a ClamAV installation is admitted by its client certificate as well
([formats/clamav.md](spec/formats/clamav.md) R-CLAMAV-010). The guide of `freshclam` shows the certificate's way only while an endpoint
admits certificates, with that endpoint's address (R-CLAMAV-006). A guide's template sees `formats.GuideData` alone, which named the
request's endpoint and no other.

**Decision.** `GuideData` gains `CertificateURLs`: the registry URL of the repository, without its trailing slash, on every endpoint with
`auth.client_certificates` on which a certificate subject reads the repository now, which the API asks of the decision point
(`Access.ReadableByCertificate`). It is empty for every other repository and in the guide of a format. The conformance kit runs every
guide section over one more variant, a signed-in reader with an address, so that no format's guide breaks on the field.

**Consequences.** One field more in `internal/formats/testdata/contract.txt`; every format's guide sections run over one more variant in
the kit (milliseconds). Another format that admits certificate readers later uses the field as it is.

**Alternatives considered.** A placeholder host in the guide; every endpoint with the key, whatever the level and the exposure
([Q-CLAMAV-18](spec/formats/clamav.md#q-clamav-18--the-guide-names-the-endpoints-on-which-a-certificate-reads-the-repository-now)).

**Revisit condition:** a format whose guide needs the address of another kind of endpoint.

**Spec:** [formats/clamav.md](spec/formats/clamav.md) R-CLAMAV-006, R-CLAMAV-010, Q-CLAMAV-18; [architecture.md](spec/architecture.md)
R-ARCH-025.

### ADR-233 · The background fetch hands its bounds to a format's fetch in the context of a run

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough. An addition to the format contract at version 8.

**Context.** The configuration of R-SIG-040 bounds the background fetch of a remote's signatures: `signatures.remote.max_manifests_per_subject`
and `signatures.max_object_size` decide what one run asks an upstream for. The job `signature-fetch` (internal/signatures/fetch, domain) calls
the format's `SignatureFetcher` (edge), whose signature carries a context, an upstream and a target; package 3 of stage 1 fixed the two
bounds as constants of the OCI format until the configuration existed.

**Decision.** The contract gains `SignatureFetchLimits` with `WithSignatureFetchLimits` and `SignatureFetchLimitsFrom`: the composition root
decorates the context of a run with the configured bounds (`fetch.HandlerOptions.RunContext`), and a format's fetch reads them, the defaults
(four manifests, 256 KiB) for a context without them. `FetchSignatures` keeps its signature and the contract its version.

**Consequences.** A format that fetches reads its bounds in one call; a mirror's plan, which calls the same code without the job, runs under
the defaults; the job's package stays free of the contract.

**Alternatives considered.** A fourth parameter of `FetchSignatures` (raises the contract's version and moves every implementation); a value
of the upstream (the upstream is the engine's, not the fetch's); constants of the format (the configuration would bound nothing).

**Revisit condition:** a bound a format needs that is no context value of a run.

**Spec:** [signatures.md](spec/signatures.md) R-SIG-026, R-SIG-040; [architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-008.

### ADR-237 · The signature declaration says whether a writer reads to sign and how the gate names an artifact
