**Status:** Decided by the development agent in the owner's absence, after the measurement with real clients of 2026-11-21; put to the
owner afterwards. The writer's read (Q-SIG-211) was decided by the owner on 2026-11-22: (a), with a trace of every such read
(`signature.download_by_writer` and its metric, Q-SIG-240); the naming of Q-SIG-213 awaits his review. An addition to the format contract at
version 9.

**Context.** The measurement found that `cosign sign` and `notation sign` read an image's manifest before they push its signature, so the
signature gate refused them and an image pushed into a gated repository could never be signed there; and that the gate's answers named
Quader's storage paths (`unsigned/_tags/1.0`) instead of what the client asked for (`unsigned:1.0`). Which formats sign by reading the
repository, and how a client names an artifact, is each format's knowledge; the core names no format.

**Decision.** `formats.SignatureDeclaration` gains `ReadToSign` (OCI sets it: a principal that may write to the repository reads through
its signature gate, asked only where the gate would refuse or hold, Q-SIG-211) and `ArtifactName` (the artifact in its client's words for the
gate's answers: OCI, npm, NuGet and Ansible Galaxy set it; nil keeps the path, Q-SIG-213). The format host reads both from the declaration it
already asks; the contract keeps its version.

**Consequences.** A format added later declares both with its signatures; the gate stays free of format names. A holder of the write right
pulls unsigned images of a gated OCI repository (H-1229).

**Alternatives considered.** A method of the signature adapter (raises the version and moves every format for two facts); the format's
identifier tested in the core (the core would name formats); any `HEAD` or read by digest passing the gate (a kubelet pulls by digest).

**Revisit condition:** a format whose signing tools read the artifact other than by a download a writer makes, or Quader's own promotion of
signed content between repositories (Q-SIG-211 (c)).

**Spec:** [signatures.md](spec/signatures.md) R-SIG-064, R-SIG-068, Q-SIG-211, Q-SIG-213; [architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-008.

### ADR-256 · A format asks the checks of an artifact's download at the document its client reads first

**Status:** Decided by the development agent after the measurement with real clients of 2026-11-23, under the owner's rule of 2026-11-22
that open questions are decided and written down. An addition to the format contract's host at version 10.

**Context.** `ansible-galaxy` prints the text of an error of a collection version's document and only the status line of the archive's
download, so a refusal of the malware gate, the vulnerability block or the signature gate reached its user as `HTTP Error 403: Forbidden`.
The checks run inside the item store's `Serve`, which a format cannot ask without serving, and through a virtual repository inside the
resolution's walk, which serves its first hit or fetches.

**Decision.** `formats.ItemStore` gains `Check(ctx, rq, it)`: the serve point's three checks of R-SIG-069 for a stored item, with the malware
gate asked as at a download, their wait and their records, and nothing served or counted. `formats.Resolver` gains `Check(ctx, rq, p,
info)`: the plan of `Artifact` and the virtual engine's `Stored` walk of the first two tiers (local members, remote members' caches), the
first hit checked and not served, nothing fetched. Ansible Galaxy's version document asks them in each class; NuGet needs none (its text
goes into `X-NuGet-Warning`, Q-SIG-241).

**Consequences.** A version document of a repository where a check applies costs that check's statements; an archive not stored yet is
judged at its download only (H-1541). The engine's walk of the stored tiers is the one `Artifact` walks, so the document and the download
name the same item.

**Alternatives considered.** A `Serve` mode that stops after the checks (every other effect of `Serve` would have to learn to skip it); the
format walking the members itself with `Plan` and `Stat` (the tier order a second time, in a format); the signature gate's `Refuse` alone at
the document (the malware gate and the vulnerability block would still reach the user as a status).

**Revisit condition:** a client of another format that shows the text of a document but not of the artifact it names.

**Spec:** [signatures.md](spec/signatures.md) R-SIG-064, R-SIG-068, Q-SIG-241; [formats/ansible.md](spec/formats/ansible.md) R-ANS-004;
[architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-008.

### ADR-238 · A Bastion serves every format: the registry root, the formats' Bastion facts and the handshake's format table

**Status:** The scope is the owner's decision of 2026-11-22; the design was decided by the planner in the owner's absence. An addition
to the format contract (`ContractVersion` stays 10) and the Bastion interface's version 4. The registry token's cap at `partial` is
narrowed to the repository by [ADR-254](#adr-254--read-shapes-per-package-at-a-bastion-a-registry-token-is-full-on-the-images-of-its-grant) (Q-BAS-167 decided as (b) on 2026-11-22, specified, not built). Built on 2026-11-22: the two contracts and
kit check 19 (`catalog.Facts.Bastion`, `catalog.RepresentationHeaders`, `catalog.PerRequestHeaders`, `catalog.Facts.BoundPrefixes`; the
handshake's `formats` and `boundRepository`, `Quader-Bastion-Counted`, the registry token's form; the builder's decisions Q-BAS-181 to
Q-BAS-185). Built the same day: the main installation's side (the backstop admits `/v2/`, the token service and the catalog tell the
marking their kind, the shape cap and the check below `/v2/`, the six withdrawals in the feed, the handshake's table and bound repository,
the counted marking; the builder's decisions Q-BAS-186 to Q-BAS-190), and the Bastion's side (the registry root as a family of the
Bastion, registry tokens, the format table and the bound repository on the link, replay headers, large artifacts and documents through the
spool, the counted report; the builder's decisions Q-BAS-195 to Q-BAS-203). Built the same day: the client case on kind and the
manual (an image pulled through a Bastion release of the set `oci` by Docker, Podman and a pod's kubelet; the builder's decisions
Q-BAS-204 to Q-BAS-207).

**Context.** The owner read that a Bastion serves neither container images nor Debian and decided: "Er soll alles liefern wie die
Hauptinstanz." Both exclusions were deferrals of the development agent (Q-OCI-23, Q-DEB-26, and Q-ANS-25 for Ansible Galaxy), argued
from the exposure rules of an endpoint, which a Bastion on the default endpoint does not meet. In the code, `/api/<format>/` of every
format was forwarded already, while `/v2/` was refused on both sides, no withdrawal of these formats reached the feed, and the cache
dropped the registry's headers and did not read its spelling of a content address.

**Decision.** The registry root `/v2/` is a path family of the Bastion at its own host root, its token service is the main
installation's, reached by a forward (Q-BAS-165, Q-BAS-166). A registry token is an opaque credential checked by the main installation,
its read shape at most `partial`; an anonymous one is the anonymous caller (Q-BAS-167, Q-BAS-168). A format's facts that matter before a
response, the headers a cached answer replays and the status of a rate-limit refusal, are `catalog.Facts.Bastion` and reach the Bastion
in a table of the handshake, beside the repository a bound host names (Q-BAS-170, Q-BAS-171, Q-BAS-178). Kit check 19 holds every format
to what a Bastion needs, so a format to come is served without a decision of its own (Q-BAS-179). Large artifacts stream to every caller
of a running fill (Q-BAS-172); the withdrawals of the three formats are `content` entries (Q-BAS-175).

**Consequences.** The Bastion's code learns one family and no format; the interface rises to version 4. A warm image pull costs the main
installation one conditional request per manifest and blob until read shapes per package exist (H-1242). The ClamAV definitions reach a
Bastion without their client certificates (H-1247).

**Alternatives considered.** A key at the Bastion to issue registry tokens (a minting key in the DMZ); a `Basic` challenge instead of the
token flow (no anonymous pulls); facts of a format compiled into the Bastion (a Bastion release per format); a decision per format (each
can defer again).

**Revisit condition:** a measurement through a Bastion in which the conditional requests of registry tokens matter (then read shapes per
package, Q-BAS-167 (b)); a format that needs a path family INV-6 does not have.

**Spec:** [bastion.md](spec/bastion.md) R-BAS-050 to R-BAS-060, Q-BAS-165 to Q-BAS-190, Q-BAS-195 to Q-BAS-207; [formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md) Q-OCI-23;
[formats/debian.md](spec/formats/debian.md) Q-DEB-26; [formats/ansible.md](spec/formats/ansible.md) Q-ANS-25.

### ADR-239 · Several object-store connections: every blob on every connection, a row per copy, one reconciliation and a scrub per copy

**Status:** The scope is the owner's decisions 7, 8, 9, 10 and 14 of 2026-11-22; the design was decided by the planner in the owner's
absence and is not built. Stage 1 of three; stage 2 (encryption per connection) and stage 3 (signed links) build on its seams.

**Context.** Quader assumed one bucket throughout: one configuration block, one client, one circuit breaker, one readiness check,
metrics without a store label, one content state per blob, and the specification said so (R-STOR-030, assumption A4). A research of
2026-11-22 listed seventeen places in the code that would have to learn of a second store. Recorded outages of object stores lasted one
to more than seven hours, the owner's own provider's about 17.5 hours in July 2026; none lost data. The scrub that the gap H-11 names as
its mitigation was not built, while the evidence listed it as implemented.

**Decision.** `storage.connections` is a list of one to eight connections (flat elements; the shared client is
`storage.object_store`), kept in the chart, credentials from Secrets per connection (R-STOR-050, R-HA-072). Every connection that is not
draining holds every blob; a row per copy (`blob_copies`, no foreign key to `blobs`) records where each object lies, its stored size and
whether the whole object was shown to be the blob, and the blob's content state is derived from its copies (R-STOR-052). An upload is done
when `min_copies` connections hold it (default 1), written to the first writable connections with a fall-over inside the request
(R-STOR-053); a session stays on its connection (R-STOR-054); reads take the copies in list order and fall over before the first byte
(R-STOR-055). One exclusive worker job reconciles from a queue and a pass, copies server-side within an endpoint and streams across
providers, fills a new connection and drains an old one (R-STOR-056). Collection deletes per copy and releases a copy it cannot reach to
the orphan sweep of its connection (R-STOR-057), which is built now, per connection, and adopts objects of live blobs (R-STOR-026). The
scrub reads every copy whole once per connection's period and the reconciliation repairs what it finds (R-STOR-027). A connection's
bucket, prefix and `encrypted` are fixed once it holds data, and a marker object names the installation and connection of a location
(R-STOR-051). The start check establishes per connection what the store supports and refuses or degrades by a stated rule; A1 is required
for new objects only and no guarantee rests on a conditional write (R-STOR-035). The store interface carries object metadata and every
size check compares the copy's stored size, so stage 2 changes values, not interfaces (R-STOR-062).

**Consequences.** One provider's outage costs neither uploads nor downloads of content another connection holds; with the default a new
blob lies on one connection until it is copied (H-1251). Deleted content can outlive its deletion on a connection that was down (H-1254).
The evidence of R-STOR-027 is corrected by renaming the tests that claimed it for other parts. An installation with one connection is
configured as before, with an `id` that defaults to `default`.

**Alternatives considered.** Uploads written to every connection before the answer (an outage stops uploads); a passive copy switched by
hand (R-HA-026's model, an outage needs a person); sharding blobs over buckets for capacity (STOR-026, stays deferred); a queue without a
pass (loses gaps during a rolling update); a scrub that trusts the stores' checksums (no provider offers a SHA-256 over a multipart
object).

**Revisit condition:** a measured catch-up that is too slow for one worker (then copies taken by every worker); a store that refuses the
marker object; a provider that needs a different client tuning per connection.

**Spec:** [storage.md](spec/storage.md) R-STOR-050 to R-STOR-063, R-STOR-026, R-STOR-027, R-STOR-030 to R-STOR-036, Q-STOR-220 to
Q-STOR-249; [ha-and-helm.md](spec/ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-072, Q-HA-390 to Q-HA-398; [backup-and-restore.md](spec/backup-and-restore.md)
R-BAK-030, Q-BAK-62 to Q-BAK-64; [api-and-ui.md](spec/api-and-ui.md) R-UI-196, R-UI-197, Q-UI-930 to Q-UI-932, Q-API-385, Q-API-386;
[security/object-store-connections.md](security/object-store-connections.md).

### ADR-242 · Delivery by signed links of the object store: one switch of the installation, where a link costs nothing

**Status:** Accepted (owner decision of 2026-11-22, decision 11 (a) of his working paper on the stored content); the mechanisms decided by
the planner in the owner's absence — put to the owner. Supersedes [ADR-045](#adr-045--presigned-download-redirects-as-a-per-repository-opt-in-p2).
Stage 3 of the owner's topic; stages 1 (several connections) and 2 (encryption) are specified apart. Built behind the API on 2026-11-22
(the serve point, the store and the limits; the development agent's decisions Q-STOR-350 to Q-STOR-354); the operations and the screens
on 2026-11-23 (the development agent's decisions Q-STOR-355, Q-STOR-356, Q-UI-956 and Q-UI-957).

**Context.** The owner: "Wir brauchen ein Setting um durch den Admin bestimmen zu lassen ob wir unsere Artefakte direkt oder durch
signierte s3 Links ausliefern lassen" and, for an encrypting connection, "dann müssen wir natürlich die Daten ausliefern". The store can
sign a link and nothing calls it; a repository's `storage.presignedDownloads` is stored and ignored. Read on 2026-11-22: a link skips
Quader's check of the bytes, the pacing and the parallel limit, outlives a revocation by its life, and through a Bastion would hand the
caller the main installation's store; the public registries redirect a blob's `GET` and answer `HEAD` themselves; the image clients written
in Go keep their credential for a subdomain of the registry's host, and a store refuses a signed link that arrives with one.

**Decision.**
- One row of the installation, off by default: the switch, the minimum size (1 MiB), the link's life (60 s, 10 s to an hour, bounded by
  the signing credential), a public address per connection; in the admin area's storage settings, read by every replica within 2 s
  ([storage.md](spec/storage.md) R-STOR-014, Q-STOR-280, Q-STOR-281, Q-STOR-290).
- A repository opts out with `storage.downloadLinks: false`; the addressed and the holding repository must both allow; `storage` is a
  closed object and the old member is refused (Q-STOR-282, Q-STOR-283).
- A download is a link only after every condition at the one serve point, in order: a route whose clients check a digest, `GET`, no
  Bastion, no system read, the switch, every gate on a decided passing state, conditionals and ranges answered by Quader, the minimum
  size, no pace figure for the caller (no longer a condition since [Q-LIM-99](spec/usage-and-limits.md#q-lim-99--a-speed-limit-does-not-stop-a-link-the-budgets-are-charged-at-the-issue), 2026-11-22), the limits' `Admit`,
  a connection that is not encrypted, holds a sound copy, is not failing and passed its link check (R-STOR-070, R-STOR-074, Q-STOR-284,
  Q-STOR-285, Q-STOR-291, Q-STOR-294).
- The link: Signature Version 4 for `GET`, the content type, `attachment` with the file name and `private, no-store` asked of the store;
  `https` only; a host that is no host of Quader nor below one; a `307` with `no-store` and the four content headers (R-STOR-072,
  Q-STOR-287 to Q-STOR-289, Q-STOR-293).
- Counted at issuance: the request, the size as cached bytes, one download, the audit event under `audit.record_downloads` with
  `delivery`, the request log's field, metrics (R-STOR-073, Q-STOR-292; [usage-and-limits.md](spec/usage-and-limits.md) R-LIM-040,
  Q-LIM-97, Q-LIM-98).

**Consequences.** Large downloads of OCI layers, npm tarballs and Ansible collections leave the `packages` pods for callers without a pace
figure; on a new installation that is administrators only, because every other built-in profile sets one (put to the owner). *Changed by
Q-LIM-99 on 2026-11-22: a pace figure no longer keeps a caller from links, so they reach every caller the other conditions allow, and a
caller slowed through Quader is not slowed by a link (H-1352).* A link is a
bearer for its life (H-12), outlives a change of the decisions (H-1275), is invisible to the parallel limit (H-1276), is checked by the
client alone (H-1277), and spends the store's own limits (H-1283), on [security/download-links.md](security/download-links.md). Each
connection proves at start that its store honours a link with the overrides.

**Alternatives considered.** A switch per repository (the old block); a switch without conditions; not building it; the public address in
the chart; links for ranges; the parallel lease for the link's life; a test that Quader runs itself; an always-on audit event; a signing
credential of its own.

**Revisit condition:** the owner's answer on the pace figures of the built-in profiles; an administrator who needs links of more than a few
minutes (a signing credential of its own); a format whose clients are shown to check (Debian with apt).

**Spec:** [storage.md](spec/storage.md) R-STOR-014, R-STOR-070, R-STOR-072 to R-STOR-074, Q-STOR-280 to Q-STOR-285, Q-STOR-287 to
Q-STOR-294, H-12; [usage-and-limits.md](spec/usage-and-limits.md) R-LIM-040, Q-LIM-97, Q-LIM-98; [api-and-ui.md](spec/api-and-ui.md)
R-UI-200, R-UI-201, Q-API-400, Q-UI-950 to Q-UI-955; [operations-and-observability.md](spec/operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-010;
[architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) Q-ARCH-570; [formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md) R-OCI-010, H-601; [security/download-links.md](security/download-links.md) H-1275 to H-1283.

### ADR-243 · A route declares whether its clients check a digest, and kit check 20 holds it

**Status:** Decided by the planner in the owner's absence — put to the owner. An addition to the format contract frozen by
[ADR-141](#adr-141--the-format-contract-is-frozen-at-version-1); the contract's version does not change. Built on 2026-11-22:
`formats.Route.ClientDigest`, the refusals of `Register`, kit check 20 with its two defects, the three declarations and the table test
(the builder's decisions Q-STOR-295 and Q-STOR-296). The serve point reads the declaration since 2026-11-22 (ADR-242's build), which adds
the derived `catalog.Entry.ClientDigest` (the format has a route that declares `Checks`, set by `Register` like `Mirror`) to the contract's
surface file under this ADR: the repository model reads it to answer `storage.downloadLinks` with `not_applicable` (R-STOR-014).

**Context.** A link replaces Quader's check of the bytes with the client's, which is no loss only where every client of the format checks.
Which clients check is each format's knowledge, and the owner's standing rule is that a decision taken at one format holds for every format
and for formats to come. ADR-238 added the facts a format declares for a Bastion (`catalog.Facts.Bastion`, kit check 19); this fact
belongs to one route and is read only at the main installation's serve point.

**Decision.** `formats.Route` gains `ClientDigest{Checks, Against, Evidence}`; the zero value is "does not check". `Register` refuses a
declaration on a route that is not a `GET` of the kind `Download`, or without what the clients compare against and the evidence. Kit check
20 holds a declaring route to an answer through the item store with the content address of its body. A table test lists every format's
declaring routes. A route declares only on the evidence of every client family the format supports; a family not read is "does not
check" until a builder shows it with the real client ([storage.md](spec/storage.md) R-STOR-071, Q-STOR-286).

**Consequences.** OCI's blob route and Ansible Galaxy's collection route declare; npm, NuGet, Debian, generic and the ClamAV
definitions do not. npm's tarball route declared until the npm leg's case of 2026-11-22 showed Yarn 4 installing a tarball whose object
was altered in the bucket ([Q-STOR-354](spec/storage.md#q-stor-354--yarn-4-installs-a-tarball-whose-object-was-altered-so-npms-tarball-route-declares-nothing)). A format added later streams until its author declares with evidence. One field more in
`internal/formats/testdata/contract.txt`; check 20 costs milliseconds per format.

**Alternatives considered.** A list of route names in `catalog.Facts`; a method of the format per request.

**Revisit condition:** a format whose clients check only some of its answers on one route.

**Spec:** [storage.md](spec/storage.md) R-STOR-071, Q-STOR-286, Q-STOR-295, Q-STOR-296; [architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-008
(the Go block holds the field).

### ADR-244 · Encrypted connections: Quader's own segment format bound to the content, the wrapped key once at the object, a storage key per connection under the key ring

**Status:** Accepted (owner decisions of 2026-11-22, decisions 1 (a), 2 (e), 3 (a), 4 (a), 5 (a) with his note, 6 (a), 7 (a) and 15 (a) of his
working paper on the stored content); the mechanisms decided by the planner in the owner's absence — put to the owner. Replaces the owner's
decision of 2026-11-06 recorded in R-STOR-048 (the storage format of s3-encryption-proxy, imported as a Go module), which no entry of this log
held and nothing built. Stage 2 of three; stage 1 (several connections, ADR-239) and stage 3 (signed links, ADR-242) are specified apart.

**Context.** The owner: "Es gibt ein Flag um die Daten im s3 verschlüsselt abzulegen … Ob verschlüsselt wird, kann pro Verbindung entschieden
werden … Der Instanz KEK muss rotiert werden können." A research of 2026-11-22 ran the attacks against the proxy's codec at its release 5.4.2:
it binds every segment to the object's name (a copy to another name does not open, which rules out Quader's finalize by a server-side copy and
the backup's copies without re-encryption), carries one wrap per object, commits to no key, and declares its Go interface no compatibility
promise. Quader's store compared stored sizes and hashes with plain values in eight places, which stage 1 moved to the copy's stored size. The
owner objected to keeping a wrapped key in two places ("Zweimal ablegen heißt doch es könnte auseinander laufen").

**Decision.** A connection is encrypted with `encrypted: true`, off by default, fixed once it holds data (R-STOR-075). The format
`quader-blob-v1` seals 64 KiB segments with AES-256-GCM, each with a stored nonce and additional data of the format, its index and a mark of
the last; a final segment carries the length and the SHA-256; nothing is bound to the name (R-STOR-076). The data key is wrapped once, in four
metadata keys written with the bytes: the wrap holds the data key, the digest and the size under a key derived per wrap from the connection's
storage key, beside the key's identifier, the format and a commitment to the data key (R-STOR-077). The key ring is the root; a storage key per
encrypted connection and generation and a name key lie once as sealed rows, drawn by Quader, never deleted, exported sealed by a command
(R-STOR-083, R-STOR-085; *amended on 2026-11-22: the rows are never deleted, and a retired connection's keys can be destroyed on command,
[ADR-255](#adr-255--the-storage-keys-of-a-retired-connection-can-be-destroyed-so-that-what-stays-at-a-provider-becomes-unreadable)*); the existing rotation re-seals them and touches no object (R-STOR-084). Names are an HMAC of the digest under the
name key unless `keyed_names: false` (R-STOR-086). Every copy into an encrypted connection gets a new data key, so a server-side copy is made
only between plain connections (R-STOR-087). An offline command reads and verifies blobs with the ring and the export, without a database
(R-STOR-089). Vectors are files of the repository, checked once by an independent implementation; the readers are fuzzed nightly (R-STOR-079,
R-STOR-091).

**Consequences.** A provider of an encrypted connection sees ciphertext under names that do not tell the file; sizes, times and the plain
journal stay visible (stored-content-visibility.md). A changed object fails authentication on every read, ranged ones included. Losing the key
ring now loses every encrypted blob in every bucket and backup (H-1305). The proxy cannot read Quader's objects. Every download of an encrypted
connection is streamed by Quader; an upload costs a second encryption pass where a payload checksum is wanted.

**Alternatives considered.** Importing the proxy's package or its codec alone (binding to the name, one wrap, an interface without a
promise); extending the proxy first (two products on one format's schedule); the wrapped key in the database too (two places drift after a
restore); keys per project or repository (every reference would need the data key; deduplication across projects); carrying a data key between
encrypted connections (a leak at one reaches the other); a nonce derived from the index (a session's resent part would reuse it).

**Revisit condition:** a key per project or per repository (decision 3 left the room: each wrap names its key); the handover of a data key to a
Bastion (decision 12 (b), H-1302); a measurement that the segment size costs ranged reads too much.

**Spec:** [storage.md](spec/storage.md) R-STOR-048, R-STOR-075 to R-STOR-091, Q-STOR-300 to Q-STOR-320 (and the builder's Q-STOR-321 to
Q-STOR-323 of the format's package and Q-STOR-324 to Q-STOR-329 of the keys' package), and the edits of R-STOR-001,

### ADR-245 · The Bastion's cache is encrypted in the stored format under one key from its chart

**Status:** Accepted (owner decision of 2026-11-22, decision 13 (a) of his working paper on the stored content); the mechanisms decided by
the planner in the owner's absence — put to the owner.

**Context.** A Bastion keeps a cache of what it serves in a bucket of its own or a volume per replica, plain today, with signed entries
(R-BAS-030, R-BAS-032). Encryption that ends at the boundary to the DMZ leaves a plain copy in the zone nearest to the internet. A Bastion has no
database and no key ring; its cache is disposable.

**Decision.** With `secrets.cacheKey` in the Bastion's chart, every object of the cache store but the empty access markers is an object of the
format of ADR-244 under keys derived from that one file (storage key, key identifier, name key), below a tree named by the key's identifier,
with names that carry no digest and no request path; without it the cache is as before. A new key is a new tree; the sweep removes the old ones
(R-BAS-061). Built on 2026-11-22: the record lies in front of each object's body (Q-BAS-212); entries and the spool's files are objects of the
format bound to their names, in place of the entries' key the planner had derived (Q-BAS-213).

**Consequences.** A holder of the cache store learns sizes, counts and times only (H-1318); a key change costs a refill; the Bastion still
holds no key of the main installation.

**Alternatives considered.** A storage key kept sealed in the cache's bucket (a key beside what it protects); the signing key for two purposes;
encrypting only artifacts and documents (entry names and the audit spool would stay readable).

**Revisit condition:** the handover of decision 12 (b), which gives a Bastion data keys of the main installation.

**Spec:** [bastion.md](spec/bastion.md) R-BAS-061, Q-BAS-210 to Q-BAS-215.

### ADR-250 · The handover per blob to a Bastion: a link and the data key of one released blob, in the answer to its forward

**Status:** Accepted (owner decision of 2026-11-22, decision 12 (b) of his working paper on the stored content); the mechanisms decided by
the planner in the owner's absence — put to the owner. Lifts the owner's [Q-BAS-10](spec/bastion.md#q-bas-10--the-cache-an-own-bucket-or-a-local-volume-never-the-main-installations-object-store)
of [ADR-142](#adr-142--the-quader-bastion-an-internet-facing-read-only-cache-instance-in-the-beta) for a link and a data key per released
blob and for nothing else. Specified, not built; it builds on the signed links (ADR-242), several connections (ADR-239) and, for encrypted
copies, the encryption (ADR-244).

**Context.** The owner wished that "Ein Bastion kann auch einen Read-Only Account auf ein s3 Bucket bekommen und damit die Hauptinstanz weiter
entlasten", and chose instead a link and the data key per released blob, so that no account and no key above a blob's own data key stands in
the DMZ. Since a Bastion serves images (ADR-238), its first fills are layers of gigabytes through the main installation. In the code a forward
is decided as the caller's own request and served by one serve point (`edge.ServeItem`) behind the limits' `Admit`; a format sets a file's
headers at its status line; the Bastion's client strips every `Quader-Bastion-*` header from an answer; the format's reader opens an object
with a data key alone, while its record opens only under the connection's storage key.

**Decision.**
- The Bastion offers on a miss (`Quader-Bastion-Handover: accept; max-size=<n>`, `n` what it would keep), and the main installation answers
  the forward, decided as ever, with the file's own `200` without its bytes, the class `handover` and a marking header that carries the link,
  its expiry, the digest, the sizes and, for a copy on an encrypted connection, its data key; the interface rises to version 6, after the read shapes per package took 5 ([ADR-254](#adr-254--read-shapes-per-package-at-a-bastion-a-registry-token-is-full-on-the-images-of-its-grant); *amended on 2026-11-22: it said 5*)
  ([bastion.md](spec/bastion.md) R-BAS-072, R-BAS-073, Q-BAS-230, Q-BAS-231).
- A switch per Bastion registration at the main installation, off by default, on the registration's card; no value in either chart; the
  links' details (minimum size, life, public addresses) are the installation's (R-BAS-071, R-BAS-078, Q-BAS-232;
  [storage.md](spec/storage.md) Q-STOR-342).
- At the serve point, in `internal/downloadlinks` beside the links: a recognized forward that offered, the registration's switch, an
  artifact, its content and every gate on a decided passing state, no range, the size, `Admit` (a speed figure is no condition), a copy whose
  connection's link works, a plain copy before an encrypted one, the data key from `CopyDataKey`, the credential and the signature, and for an
  encrypted copy the transactional event `bastion.data_key.handed` before the answer; counted and charged at issuance as a link
  (R-STOR-095, R-STOR-096, Q-STOR-340 to Q-STOR-346).
- The Bastion reads the object whole with a client of its own that carries no credential, trusts the system roots and its chart's trust
  bundle, follows no redirect and refuses Quader's hosts; it verifies the digest, and on an encrypted copy every segment under the handed key,
  reads no record, holds the key for the one read and writes it nowhere (R-BAS-074, R-BAS-076, Q-BAS-234, Q-BAS-237).
- A failure before the first byte is the forward again without the offer; after it the fill continues from the main installation by a range;
  a digest that fails at the end fails the fill and marks the key; a replica that cannot reach the store offers nothing for a minute
  (R-BAS-075, Q-BAS-235, Q-BAS-236). A blob withdrawn during a fill is treated as in a forwarded fill (R-BAS-077, Q-BAS-238).

**Consequences.** Large artifacts of every format travel from the store to the Bastion, and a cold fill holds no budget slot towards the main
installation. A taken-over Bastion collects the data keys of the encrypted blobs filled through it, which open their objects wherever their
ciphertext lies until the connection is replaced (H-1340, H-1311); the trail of `bastion.data_key.handed` names each. The store's operator sees
the Bastion's address (H-1343). A failed direct read is counted or charged again (H-1342). No end-to-end case: about 5 s in one integration
shard and about 4 s of unit tests, nothing per format.

**Alternatives considered.** A read-only account of the bucket for the Bastion (the owner's first wish, which he did not choose); a new interface
operation or a ticket fetched in a second step; a JSON body or a `307` as the answer; a switch of the installation or of the Bastion's chart;
documents and pass-through files too; the segment key instead of the data key; failing the fill on every failure; a rewrite of one blob under a
new data key after a compromise.

**Revisit condition:** layers above the Bastion's `max_object_bytes` that matter (then a verified pass-through); a project that must keep its
keys out of the DMZ (then an opt-out of its own on every format); many Bastions per installation (then a switch of the installation beside the
registrations'); the owner's answer on the speed figures (Q-LIM-97, Q-STOR-343; for the links decided by the development agent in
Q-LIM-99 on 2026-11-22, the same way as Q-STOR-343).

**Spec:** [bastion.md](spec/bastion.md) R-BAS-070 to R-BAS-079, Q-BAS-230 to Q-BAS-239, Q-BAS-10; [storage.md](spec/storage.md) R-STOR-095,
R-STOR-096, Q-STOR-340 to Q-STOR-347, and the edits of R-STOR-014, R-STOR-070, R-STOR-074, R-STOR-083, R-STOR-085, R-STOR-088;
[operations-and-observability.md](spec/operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-010; [security/bastion-handover.md](security/bastion-handover.md)
H-1340 to H-1345.

**As built, the data keys (package 4 of [the build plan](developer/bastion-handover.md), 2026-11-23):** a copy on an encrypted connection is
handed over with its own data key where no plain copy can serve; the key is opened from the copy the request read (one `HeadObject`, no
statement), taken after the link is signed, destroyed once the value is encoded, and `bastion.data_key.handed` is committed before the answer
leaves, a failed insert streaming ([storage.md](spec/storage.md) Q-STOR-470 to Q-STOR-472). With it H-1340 and H-1341 are live wherever a
registration's handover is on and an encrypted connection holds blobs read through it; the encoded value is H-1490.

### ADR-254 · Read shapes per package at a Bastion: a registry token is full on the images of its grant

**Status:** Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-22, after the owner's word that its favourite is built and not what was built first
([Q-BAS-167](spec/bastion.md#q-bas-167--a-registry-token-is-checked-by-the-main-installation-and-its-read-shape-is-at-most-partial),
option (b)); the mechanisms Q-BAS-240 to Q-BAS-254, and Q-BAS-260 and Q-BAS-261 of its build, decided by the development agent.
Specified; the decision point and the format contract (`PackageReachOn`, kit check 21) built on 2026-11-22, the rest not built. Narrows
[ADR-238](#adr-238--a-bastion-serves-every-format-the-registry-root-the-formats-bastion-facts-and-the-handshakes-format-table)'s cap of a
registry token at `partial` to the repository, and changes the condition of the owner's
[Q-BAS-18](spec/bastion.md#q-bas-18--metadata-shared-for-confirmed-full-readers-filtered-documents-per-caller) from a full read of the
repository to a full read of the repository or of the package a document belongs to (Q-BAS-244; named to the owner on 2026-11-22).

**Context.** Almost every image client reads with a registry token of five minutes, taken anew for each pull. Its shape is capped at
`partial` because a grant names images and the decision point does not see it, so every warm pull of an image of ten layers costs the main
installation twelve conditional requests against the miss limit of the client's address (300 a minute), and a rollout behind one address
reaches it at about twenty pulls a minute. Every reader narrowed by package patterns pays the same per artifact. In the code every format
already decides its package through the host (`Host.Authorize` with `Target.Package`), the core already notes `absent` and `counted` for a
recognized Bastion request, and the decision point classifies reach per repository only.

**Decision.**
- The decision point computes a package shape (`PackageReachOn`): `full` when the endpoint exposes everything, no path pattern tells two
  paths of the repository apart, the read of the package is allowed on the artifact state, its wiki is readable and, for a remote, the
  populate right holds; through a virtual repository its gate and every member; for a registry token only within its grant
  ([bastion.md](spec/bastion.md) R-BAS-080, Q-BAS-240, Q-BAS-243).
- The core notes the package of every rights decision the host makes; a response belongs to P when every decision named P and none named no
  package. The marking gains `Quader-Bastion-Package` and `Quader-Bastion-Package-Read`, and a document is `shared` also for a reader `full`
  on its package; the check answers per (repository, package) pair (R-BAS-081 to R-BAS-083, Q-BAS-241, Q-BAS-242, Q-BAS-244).
- The Bastion keeps a fourth kind of answer per (credential, repository, package) under the rules and the feed of every answer, renewed by
  use, records a registry token's `full` only where its unverified grant names the pair, and records the package on each cache entry; an
  entry of P is served without a request to a caller `full` on P. A caller with a known `partial` shape gets a conditional request, not a
  check, so no timing tells a cached package from an uncached one (R-BAS-084, R-BAS-085, Q-BAS-245 to Q-BAS-249).
- Kit check 21 holds every format to it: decisions before the status line, a package-less decision for a response that draws on other
  packages, the same answer for a reader of the package as for a reader of the repository (R-BAS-086, Q-BAS-250).
- The interface takes version 5 and the handover moves to 6; the reading of a token's expiry from its claims is bundled (R-BAS-087,
  Q-BAS-251, Q-BAS-252). Limits and download events stay as they are (Q-BAS-253).

**Consequences.** A warm image pull costs the main installation its token request and one check: 3 requests for Docker and the kubelet, 2
for Podman, instead of 13 to 15 (derived from the read flow, measured once when built), and a rollout behind one address reaches the miss
limit at about 100 pulls a minute. *Measured when built (2026-11-23), an image of ten layers:* Docker 29.9.3 16 → 4, Podman 5.8.9 13 → 2,
containerd 2.3.4 through crictl 19 → 6; no conditional request remains, and what is left besides the token step is a check or one forward
per new token, and Docker's first look at the tag without a credential while anonymous reads are on (H-1420). A package answer is renewed
by the check when its shape answer ended with it (Q-BAS-270), and the end-to-end case asserts that a warm pull asks nothing about an
artifact (Q-BAS-271). A warm `npm ci` by a reader narrowed in every member costs nothing within the period. Registry-token and
package-narrowed readers get the bounds of a full reader: what the feed does not carry reaches them within the revalidation periods
(H-1380), and the limits and blocks at the renewal of their answer (H-1381). The check tells the holder of the Bastion token a held
credential's shape per package (H-1382), and the sharing per package rests on the core's notes and check 21 (H-1383). About 1.3 s of unit
tests, one second-package seed per format, no new end-to-end case.

**Alternatives considered.** Keeping the cap and paying the requests (Q-BAS-167 (a), built until this is); asymmetric registry tokens the
Bastion verifies (format knowledge at the Bastion); judging a package per member; sending grant patterns to the Bastion; a route declaration
of the package parameter; an opaque package key; three package values with a status; artifacts only; a check whenever a package answer is
missing; answers carried in the token service's answer; a bound per credential; a background refresh; `content` entries per package; one
interface version shared with the handover.

**Revisit condition:** a measurement in which the remaining check per new registry token matters (then answers in the token service's
answer, Q-BAS-245 (d)); path-pattern grants that take the gain away from real installations (Q-BAS-240); revalidation traffic from
`content` entries per repository (Q-BAS-249).

**Spec:** [bastion.md](spec/bastion.md) R-BAS-080 to R-BAS-088, Q-BAS-240 to Q-BAS-254, Q-BAS-260, Q-BAS-261, Q-BAS-167, and the edits of R-BAS-011, R-BAS-012,
R-BAS-013, R-BAS-020, R-BAS-022, R-BAS-023, R-BAS-034, R-BAS-040, R-BAS-052, R-BAS-054, R-BAS-058, R-BAS-073, R-BAS-074, Q-BAS-18,
Q-BAS-198, Q-BAS-200, Q-BAS-202; the gaps H-1242, H-1380 to H-1384 and H-1390; from the build Q-BAS-265, Q-BAS-270, Q-BAS-271, the gaps
H-1395 and H-1420, H-1295 closed; [developer/bastion-package-shapes.md](developer/bastion-package-shapes.md).

### ADR-255 · The storage keys of a retired connection can be destroyed, so that what stays at a provider becomes unreadable

**Status:** Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-22, after the owner's word that its favourite is built and not what was specified
first ([Q-STOR-309](spec/storage.md#q-stor-309--a-storage-key-is-a-row-with-an-identifier-of-its-own-drawn-at-the-connections-first-start-never-deleted),
option (b), what the owner had been told when he decided the topic); the mechanisms Q-STOR-400 to Q-STOR-413, Q-BAK-74 to Q-BAK-76 and
Q-HA-416 and Q-HA-417 decided by the development agent. Built on 2026-11-23 (package 7, with the builder's decisions Q-STOR-460 to Q-STOR-462 and Q-HA-425), with the pool's keys of the backup built by package 4 the same day. Amends
[ADR-244](#adr-244--encrypted-connections-quaders-own-segment-format-bound-to-the-content-the-wrapped-key-once-at-the-object-a-storage-key-per-connection-under-the-key-ring)'s
"never deleted" (the row stays, its key goes) and touches two things said to the owner: his decision 15 (a) (the storage keys lie once, as
sealed rows) and the answer (a) of Q-BAK-65 (the pool keeps the digest's name), which the development agent gave him the same evening.

**Context.** The working paper promised that whoever leaves a provider destroys its storage key, so that what stays there becomes
unreadable. Q-STOR-309 was specified with (a), keys never deleted, and H-1308 recorded the gap. A drain deletes only the copies that have rows
and `forget-connection` deletes no object, so noncurrent versions, leftovers and the provider's own copies stay, readable to whoever holds the
database or a backup of it and the key ring. A backup's pool is shared, keyed by the digest and never copied again, so a retained backup would
name a retired connection's key for as long as the blob lives.

**Decision.**
- `quader admin storage keys destroy --connection <id>` destroys every key of a retired or unrecorded connection, every generation and the
  name key, in one transaction; a dry run by default, a confirmation bound to the installation and the keys, exit `5` while a holder refuses;
  run at a pod with the runtime database role and no key ring, never through the API ([storage.md](spec/storage.md) R-STOR-098, R-STOR-099,
  Q-STOR-400, Q-STOR-401, Q-STOR-404, Q-STOR-405, Q-STOR-410).
- The row stays, `destroyed`, `sealed_key` NULL, `destroyed_at` set; the id is retired for good, also across a restore (R-STOR-097,
  R-STOR-102, Q-STOR-402, Q-STOR-411).
- It refuses while a live replica configures the connection, while a copy, a queue row or an upload session exists, or while the newest
  retention listing of the configured target cannot be trusted or names one of the keys in a retained backup's pool (R-STOR-098, R-STOR-100,
  Q-STOR-403). It reports the exports made before (a table `storage_key_exports`), the retained backups that hold the keys sealed,
  PostgreSQL's own copies and the data keys handed to a Bastion, and does not refuse for them (R-STOR-103, Q-STOR-408, Q-STOR-412); the
  last as the files whose data key was handed and the handovers, with the audit log's bound (Q-STOR-475, at the join with the handover's
  data keys).
- Replicas destroy the keys at the change; a read meeting a destroyed key answers `destroyed_key`, marks the copy and repairs it
  (R-STOR-101, Q-STOR-406, Q-STOR-407). An import skips a destroyed key and inserts the destroyed rows it lacks (Q-STOR-409).
- The destruction is journaled, and a restore to before it destroys the keys again, except for a connection the restoring configuration
  names, whose entry is skipped as forged or stale (R-HA-054, Q-HA-416, Q-HA-417).
- **What it costs in the backup's pool** (package 4): an encrypted pool object is named `pool/sha256/<hex>.<key id>`, the blob list names
  each digest's pool object and is written after the copies, a blob pooled under a departing connection's key is copied again from a
  connection that stays, a draining connection's copy is read after every other, and every retained backup records which keys its pool and
  its database hold ([backup-and-restore.md](spec/backup-and-restore.md) R-BAK-032, Q-BAK-74 to Q-BAK-76). The re-copied bytes, and such
  blobs twice in the pool until the older backups leave retention, are the price.

**Consequences.** What the promise holds: after the destruction neither the provider nor whoever obtains its objects nor Quader can read what
the retired connection left. What it does not hold: an export made before, a Quader backup still in retention and PostgreSQL's old row
versions, log and archive still open the keys with the key ring (H-1370 to H-1372); backups the check does not see lose their encrypted pool
objects (H-1373); a data key handed to a Bastion opens its object without the storage key (H-1374); a journal entry forged with a runtime
credential can destroy a retired connection's keys at a restore before the operator does (H-1375), not a configured one's (Q-HA-417); the ciphertext stays at the provider until the bucket is emptied. About 0.3 s of unit tests, 0.1 s in `blob`, about 0.1 s in `backup` and about
2 s in `api` (measured, [stored-content-encryption.md](developer/stored-content-encryption.md#package-7-destroying-a-retired-connections-keys-as-built)).

**Alternatives considered.** Keys never deleted (Q-STOR-309 (a)); keys deleted when a connection retires (c); one generation or one key
destroyed alone; the row deleted or its value replaced by a marker; judging backups by listing the target or reading the pool; no re-pool, or
a pool object overwritten in place; a confirmation by the connection id, `--yes` or a prompt; `unknown_key` for a destroyed key; forgetting
lazily; an import that refuses or resurrects; an API operation or a chart Job; vacuuming from the command.

**Revisit condition:** an installation that must shred one generation without replacing the connection (then a re-wrap job, Q-STOR-400 (b));
a target moved often enough that H-1373 bites; a forged destruction entry met in practice (H-1375), which an authenticated journal would
close.

**Spec:** [storage.md](spec/storage.md) R-STOR-097 to R-STOR-103, Q-STOR-400 to Q-STOR-413, Q-STOR-309, and the edits of R-STOR-051,
R-STOR-077, R-STOR-078, R-STOR-082, R-STOR-083, R-STOR-085, R-STOR-087 to R-STOR-091, Q-STOR-310, Q-STOR-311, Q-STOR-325;
[backup-and-restore.md](spec/backup-and-restore.md) R-BAK-032, Q-BAK-74 to Q-BAK-76, and the edits of R-BAK-002, R-BAK-003, R-BAK-006,
R-BAK-007, R-BAK-016, R-BAK-017, R-BAK-019, R-BAK-024, R-BAK-030, R-BAK-031, Q-BAK-62, Q-BAK-65; [ha-and-helm.md](spec/ha-and-helm.md)
R-HA-054, Q-HA-416, Q-HA-417; [operations-and-observability.md](spec/operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-014;
[security/stored-content-keys.md](security/stored-content-keys.md) H-1308, H-1309, H-1370 to H-1375;
[security/stored-content-visibility.md](security/stored-content-visibility.md) H-1314, H-1316;
[developer/stored-content-encryption.md](developer/stored-content-encryption.md) package 7.

### ADR-277 · A remote repository can be curated: delivery rules in two modes, an upstream catalogue, downloads ahead and their queue, requests with examination

**Status:** Decided by the owner on 2026-11-23 (task T-24: the wish, the two modes, the deciders, the request, the fetch for
examination, and a tab each for the upstream and the queue, [Q-CUR-1](spec/remote-curation.md#q-cur-1--a-remote-repositorys-page-has-tabs-its-content-upstream-and-downloads));
the design decided by the development agent ([Q-CUR-2](spec/remote-curation.md#q-cur-2--the-words-allow-and-block-two-modes-a-plain-user-reads-no-release)
to [Q-CUR-28](spec/remote-curation.md#q-cur-28--the-upstream-is-another-surface-the-protocol-routes-keep-what-they-serve)). Specified,
not built.

**Context.** The owner, 2026-11-23, 12:38: "In Repositories, die Remote sind, fehlt mir dafür ein Reiter um das Remote zu durchsuchen
… Wir brauchen in bei Remote-Repos als ein Whitelisting und Blacklisting Konzept. Default ist Blacklisting … Remote-Repos benötigen auch
einen Reiter mit dem der User sich die aktuelle Download-Queue des Remote-repos anschauen kann"; at 12:57 the request for an allow, at
13:01 the fetch for examination without delivery. A remote fetched only for a client's request, a probe or a mirror's pass; its patterns
admitted or hid whole packages; no surface showed its upstream or a failed download.

**Decision.**
- A remote delivers everything except what is blocked (default) or only what is allowed; a rule allows or blocks a sub-section, a package
  (future versions included) or a version; the narrowest rule decides, a block wins at equal width; the patterns of a remote become rules
  ([remote-curation.md](spec/remote-curation.md) R-CUR-001, R-CUR-002).
- The refusal is a delivery gate: before a fill, at the serve point as the fourth check of the one decision, and in documents; its own
  answer in each format; a miss of a virtual member (R-CUR-003, R-CUR-004).
- The holders of `manage` and the administrator set rules and decide requests; the mode is configuration; a gate's release stays triage
  (R-CUR-005).
- The upstream catalogue is a declared port of the format contract (contract version 11) that stores nothing, with a budget, a cache and
  bounds of its own (R-CUR-007 to R-CUR-009).
- Downloads ahead at three levels with a preview and bounds; a repository's download queue as rows run by jobs, failures in the failure's
  own words, retries; the probe's background download a row of it (R-CUR-010 to R-CUR-013).
- A download ahead does not depend on the rules: what it stores and the rules do not deliver is stored for examination, scanned, shown with
  its verdicts and removed after 30 days without a decision; a request starts that examination at once (R-CUR-014 to R-CUR-016).

**Consequences.** Every format with a remote class declares its catalogue and filters its documents by the rules (kit checks 21 and 22);
a Debian remote's curated view is a virtual repository over it; the page of a remote repository has tabs; R-UI-052, R-REPO-005, R-REPO-024,
R-REPO-065, R-AUTHZ-008, R-API-081 and INV-11 changed. The security view is [security/remote-curation.md](security/remote-curation.md).

**Built: the upstream catalogue (2026-11-24, package R3).** The five formats implement `formats.Catalogue`, and `Register` refuses a remote
adapter without it. The contract's surface grew by additions that keep version 11: the leaf `discover` gained `UnavailableError`,
`RepositoryIDer`, `VersionFacts.UnpackedSize`, the page bounds, `ErrBadLevel` and its paging helpers
([Q-CUR-60](spec/remote-curation.md#q-cur-60--the-catalogues-upstream-is-lent-by-the-mirror-host-which-the-roles-of-the-management-api-now-build)
to [Q-CUR-65](spec/remote-curation.md#q-cur-65--a-bulk-and-a-preview-read-the-catalogue-a-preview-is-one-page-of-the-bulks-bound));
`internal/formats/testdata/contract.txt` holds them.

**Built: a level the upstream does not have (2026-11-24, after the owner's report "Die Suche nach meinem namespace scheitert.").** A
further addition that keeps version 11: `discover.LevelPage.Unknown` (`*discover.UnknownLevel` with `Rule`, `Forbidden` and
`Suggestion`) and `discover.NameRule` with its two values. A format that tells a level its upstream does not have from an empty one sets
it at a constant cost, a format that cannot sets nothing and answers as before; kit check 22 holds a case's `UnknownLevel`
([Q-CUR-165](spec/remote-curation.md#q-cur-165--a-level-the-upstream-does-not-have-says-so-with-the-formats-naming-rule-and-one-suggestion-built-from-it)).

### ADR-278 · The order of a format's versions is a sort key stored with every version row

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough
([Q-API-429](spec/api-and-ui.md#q-api-429--the-order-of-a-formats-versions-is-a-sort-key-stored-with-every-version-row)). It changes the
frozen format contract: contract version 12.

**Context.** The version list in the order of the versions and the latest version of every listed package read every version's name and
ordered it in the service by the format's `Compare`: with 100,000 versions of one package 0.4 s a page and 0.66 s the package list, with
100,000 tags of a remote image 0.58 s and 1.24 s (measured on 2026-11-24, [packages.md](developer/packages.md#a-package-with-100000-versions-h-1683-measured)).
No statement can sort by a format's `Compare`.

**Decision.**
- A format's view adapter gives the sort key of its order (`ViewAdapter.SortKey`, [versionkey](../internal/formats/versionkey/versionkey.go)):
  bytewise the order of `Compare`, a string that is no version first, two strings two keys. Kit check 11 holds it to `Compare`.
- The host's package writer stores the key and the format's pre-release answer with every version row; a remote OCI repository's tag
  entries derive the same key in PostgreSQL from the stored tag (migration 00116, compared byte for byte by an integration test).
- The rows written without a key (before migration 00116, or by a replica of the release before it during a rolling upgrade) keep it
  NULL until the background migration `version_sort_key` fills it with the same function the writer uses; it records its completion only
  after a pass that leaves no such row
  ([Q-HA-492](spec/ha-and-helm.md#q-ha-492--the-fill-of-the-versions-sort-keys-records-its-completion-after-a-pass-that-leaves-no-row-without-a-key)).
  Meanwhile the statements return a package's rows without a key besides the keyed batch and the service gives each the key its format
  gives it ([Q-API-430](spec/api-and-ui.md#q-api-430--a-version-row-without-a-stored-sort-key-is-ordered-by-the-key-its-format-gives-it)).
- A page in the order of the versions is one keyset statement per holder on an index; the latest version of a listed package is the first
  visible entry of an index of its releases, else of its pre-releases; the package list sums the downloads of the page's packages alone.

**Consequences.** Every format with a view implements `SortKey`; an installation upgrades with its version rows (R-HA-020), and a page
reads a package's rows without a key whole until the fill has reached them; a change of a format's encoding is a migration step that
sets its stored keys to NULL, which the fill recomputes. **Revised on 2026-11-24:** migration 00116 had refused a database that held
version rows, which refused every upgrade. The order of publication of a package several repositories hold, and the count of a
package's versions in the list, still read every version (H-1683).

### ADR-279 · Administrators see the downloads from upstreams live, and the last 100 finished

**Status:** Decided by the owner on 2026-11-24 (task T-26: the wish, the place at the top right, the running downloads with their progress
and speed, the last 100 with their duration and average speed); the design decided by the development agent
([Q-OPS-419](spec/operations-and-observability.md#q-ops-419--a-download-is-the-body-of-an-artifact-from-a-remote-repositorys-upstream-whatever-caused-it)
to [Q-OPS-424](spec/operations-and-observability.md#q-ops-424--one-key-the-publication-interval-the-list-holds-100),
[Q-UI-1070](spec/api-and-ui.md#q-ui-1070--the-downloads-button-stands-between-documentation-and-the-theme-and-counts-what-runs) to
[Q-UI-1073](spec/api-and-ui.md#q-ui-1073--the-panel-refreshes-by-polling-while-it-is-seen-and-announces-nothing)). The backend and the
API are built (T-26 package A, 2026-11-24), and the top bar's button and its panel (T-26 package B, 2026-11-24).

**Context.** The owner, 2026-11-24, 08:20: "Ich will als Admin oben Rechts eine Downlaod Übersicht haben wie aus dem Screenshot. Dort
werden alle laufenden Downloads, ihr Forschritt, Download-Geschwindigkeit abgebildet. Es werden nur Downloads von Upstream Repos
angezeigt. Zusätzlich zu den laufenden Downloads werden auch die letzten 100 abgeschlossenen Downloads abgebildet zu sammen mit ihrer
Download-Dauer und der durchschnittlichen Geschwindigkeit". Nothing showed what an installation was loading from its upstreams: the
queue of one remote repository showed its own rows, and a client's miss or a mirror's pass showed nowhere while it ran.

**Decision.**
- A download is the body of an artifact from a remote repository's upstream after a success answer, whatever caused it: a client's miss,
  a row of the download queue, a mirror's pass, the vulnerability scanning's database; one hook where the engine reads the body
  ([operations-and-observability.md](spec/operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-049).
- A tracker in memory per replica; one row of PostgreSQL per replica every two seconds while something runs; readers take rows at most
  three intervals old; no Valkey (R-OPS-050).
- The last 100 are a table trimmed to 100, not backed up; a stopped replica's downloads end `interrupted` (R-OPS-051).
- Two operations under `content:metadata-read`: the administrator and the auditor (R-OPS-052).

**Consequences.** R-API-038, R-ARCH-030, R-BAK-004, R-REPO-025 and R-CUR-011's page changed; R-UI-002 names the button, R-UI-210 to
R-UI-212 the button and its panel, and R-CUR-018's tab Downloads takes a package's name from its address. The security view is
[security/upstream-downloads.md](security/upstream-downloads.md); the code is described in
[developer/upstream-downloads.md](developer/upstream-downloads.md).

## Design invariants

The invariants of [spec/README.md](spec/README.md#design-invariants) are the baseline every spec
page builds on. A page may refine an invariant but must not contradict it; where a page finds one
wrong, it keeps it and raises a question, which is listed with the entry. Where the decision on
such a question changes the invariant, the entry records the new rule and the question that
changed it; the edit to spec/README.md is that question's cross-page consequence. On 2026-10-28
the owner's constraints ([ADR-092](#adr-092--high-availability-on-ha-postgresql-ha-valkey-with-sentinel-and-s3) to [ADR-095](#adr-095--no-readwritemany-storage)) changed INV-2, INV-3, INV-11, INV-12 and INV-13
and added INV-18 and INV-19:
- **INV-2:** roles `web`, `worker` and `backup`, split from the start; `all` only for development
  ([ADR-013](#adr-013--one-binary-roles-split-from-the-start-identical-replicas-per-role-inv-2)). Changed again by the owner on
  2026-11-04 ([ADR-153](#adr-153--quader-is-cut-into-task-areas-roles-of-one-binary-network-seams-only-at-trust-or-load-boundaries), [ADR-155](#adr-155--three-roles-api-packages-and-worker-variants-are-pools)): roles `api` (route families `ui`, `api`, `ci_exchange`; sessions and login secrets), `packages` (`packages`,
  `files`; tokens only) and `worker` (queues, pools by queue), each its own Deployment; `web` is `api` and `packages` in one
  process, kept as the bridge of the upgrade across the cut ([Q-ARCH-295](spec/architecture.md#q-arch-295--what-becomes-of-the-role-name-web));
  since 2026-11-19 the chart renders it no longer, and the binary keeps it for development and tests
  ([Q-HA-315](spec/ha-and-helm.md#q-ha-315--the-charts-upgrade-bridge-across-the-cut-is-removed-the-binary-keeps-the-role-web-for-development-and-tests)).
  Since 2026-11-20 a role `scanner`, the analysis of container images without any secret of the database, the object store or Valkey
  ([ADR-212](#adr-212--the-image-analysis-runs-in-a-role-scanner-that-holds-no-secret)).
- **INV-3:** PostgreSQL is the system of record; Valkey holds shared ephemeral state only, and the
  change log in PostgreSQL replaces `LISTEN/NOTIFY` ([ADR-014](#adr-014--postgresql-is-the-system-of-record-valkey-holds-only-shared-ephemeral-state-inv-3)).
- **INV-11:** cross-replica collapsing through a Valkey lock ([ADR-022](#adr-022--pull-through-proxy-semantics-inv-11)).
- **INV-12:** HA PostgreSQL, HA Valkey with Sentinel and S3; load beyond one replica; drains
  without outage; bounded PostgreSQL connections ([ADR-023](#adr-023--high-availability-and-horizontal-scale-on-ha-postgresql-ha-valkey-and-s3-inv-12)).
- **INV-13:** one Deployment per role, the backup CronJob, no ReadWriteMany volume ([ADR-024](#adr-024--the-helm-chart-is-the-supported-deployment-inv-13)).
- **INV-18** (new): no state between requests on a replica ([ADR-096](#adr-096--no-state-between-requests-on-a-replica-inv-18)).
- **INV-19** (new): consistent backups to S3, restored into an empty installation ([ADR-097](#adr-097--consistent-backups-to-s3-restored-into-an-empty-installation-inv-19)).

Earlier, decisions on spec pages changed INV-6, INV-8, INV-12 and INV-17, and aligned the wording
of INV-4, INV-10 and INV-15 with decisions that refine them:
- **INV-4** wording: SHA-512 for every blob ([Q-STOR-2](spec/storage.md#q-stor-2--sha-512-for-every-blob-or-only-on-demand); [ADR-015](#adr-015--content-addressed-blob-store-on-s3-inv-4)).
- **INV-6:** the npm exchange prefix and the `/v2/` reservation at the host root, and Quader owns
  its host root ([Q-NPM-1](spec/formats/npm.md#q-npm-1--host-root-routes-next-to-inv-6), [Q-HA-4](spec/ha-and-helm.md#q-ha-4--reserve-v2-on-the-client-listener-for-oci); [ADR-017](#adr-017--url-layout-on-two-listeners-inv-6)). [Q-ARCH-11](spec/architecture.md#q-arch-11--url-layout-and-port-numbers-inv-6) confirmed the layout
  and the ports unchanged.
- **INV-8:** the `__Host-` cookie names ([Q-AUTH-2](spec/identity-and-authentication.md#q-auth-2--session-cookie-name); [ADR-019](#adr-019--quader-issues-opaque-prefixed-tokens-inv-8)).
- **INV-10** wording: the `CI_JOB_TOKEN` fallback is P2 ([Q-CI-5](spec/gitlab-ci-oidc.md#q-ci-5--build-the-ci_job_token-fallback-at-all); [ADR-021](#adr-021--gitlab-ci-identity-through-id-token-exchange-inv-10)).
- **INV-12:** the readiness rule ([Q-STOR-1](spec/storage.md#q-stor-1--readiness-tied-to-object-storage-reachability-inv-12), [Q-OPS-2](spec/operations-and-observability.md#q-ops-2--should-object-storage-reachability-gate-readiness), [Q-HA-1](spec/ha-and-helm.md#q-ha-1--readiness-on-object-storage-failure); [ADR-023](#adr-023--high-availability-and-horizontal-scale-on-ha-postgresql-ha-valkey-and-s3-inv-12)).
- **INV-15** wording: login providers are file configuration only ([Q-AUTH-1](spec/identity-and-authentication.md#q-auth-1--where-login-provider-configuration-lives); [ADR-026](#adr-026--one-configuration-file-plus-database-held-configuration-inv-15)).
- **INV-17:** public, documented endpoints instead of only `/api/v1` ([Q-API-4](spec/api-and-ui.md#q-api-4--inv-17s-wording-and-byte-transfers-on-files); [ADR-028](#adr-028--the-ui-uses-only-the-public-api-inv-17)).

On 2026-10-29 the endpoints of [spec/endpoints.md](spec/endpoints.md) changed three invariants
([ADR-128](#adr-128--endpoints-one-listener-each-identified-by-the-listener-with-exposure-rules-as-a-ceiling)):
- **INV-6:** one client listener per endpoint, the endpoint identified by the listener, the
  `/.well-known/` reservation and host-root bindings ([Q-EP-1](spec/endpoints.md#q-ep-1--how-the-endpoint-of-a-request-is-identified), [Q-EP-6](spec/endpoints.md#q-ep-6--how-far-wildcard-hosts-and-host-root-bindings-go)).
- **INV-9:** the effective permission is also intersected with the endpoint's exposure, for every
  subject ([Q-EP-12](spec/endpoints.md#q-ep-12--whether-administrators-pass-the-exposure-ceiling)).
- **INV-15:** endpoints in the file, their exposure rules in PostgreSQL ([Q-EP-2](spec/endpoints.md#q-ep-2--where-endpoint-configuration-and-exposure-rules-live)).

### ADR-012 · One toolchain, one image (INV-1)

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough

**Context.** UI, management API and package protocols could ship as separate deliverables with
separate versions.

**Decision.** Go 1.27.3 and Angular 22. The Angular build is embedded into the Go binary with
`embed`, so one container image serves the UI, the management API and every package protocol.

**Consequences.** UI and server are versioned, tested and rolled back together; the UI cannot be
deployed on its own. UI and API share one origin, so no cross-origin setup is needed
([ADR-030](#adr-030--one-origin-for-ui-api-and-package-content)). Each UI locale adds a build to the binary ([Q-UI-5](spec/api-and-ui.md#q-ui-5--internationalization-mechanism)).

**Alternatives considered.** A separate UI image behind the edge: independent UI releases, but two
artifacts to keep compatible and either path routing at the edge or cross-origin requests. Serving
the UI from a CDN: breaks air-gapped installations, which [R-UI-001](spec/api-and-ui.md#r-ui-001--technology-baseline-and-delivery) supports explicitly.

**Spec:** [INV-1](spec/README.md#design-invariants), [R-ARCH-001](spec/architecture.md#r-arch-001--one-binary-identical-replicas-process-roles), [R-ARCH-004](spec/architecture.md#r-arch-004--angular-workspace-layout),
[R-UI-001](spec/api-and-ui.md#r-ui-001--technology-baseline-and-delivery).

### ADR-013 · One binary, roles split from the start, identical replicas per role (INV-2)

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough; the role table changed by the owner's cut into
task areas on 2026-11-04 ([ADR-153](#adr-153--quader-is-cut-into-task-areas-roles-of-one-binary-network-seams-only-at-trust-or-load-boundaries), [ADR-155](#adr-155--three-roles-api-packages-and-worker-variants-are-pools)), specified for phase 6a

**Context.** High availability ([ADR-005](#adr-005--high-availability)) needs replicas that can be added, removed and
replaced without coordination steps. Changed by the owner's constraints of 2026-10-28
([ADR-093](#adr-093--horizontal-scale-random-distribution-split-roles-drains-without-outage)): the load exceeds one replica, requests reach replicas at random, and several worker
types and a split service are allowed. Until then every replica served HTTP and background work,
the chart's default role was `all`, and the split into `api` and `worker` Deployments was P1. That
default and that priority are replaced; the client-facing role is now named `web`.

**Decision.** One binary and one container image, `quader`, with the subcommands `serve`,
`migrate`, `backup` and `admin`. A role is a set of enabled subsystems chosen by configuration, not
a separate build:
- **`web`** serves every HTTP request: UI, management API, package protocols and raw files.
- **`worker`** runs the background work of the job queue and holds the leases.
- **`backup`** runs the backup and restore commands as a Kubernetes Job or CronJob.

`process.role` has no default, and `quader serve` refuses to start without `web`, `worker` or `all`.
The chart deploys `web` and `worker` as separate Deployments from the start, each with its own
replica count, autoscaler, disruption budget, grace period and topology spread, and never renders
`all`, which exists only for a binary started outside the chart during development. Every replica
of a role is identical and interchangeable; there is no primary.

**Consequences.** Scaling is the replica count of a role, and each role scales and drains on its
own. Which subsystem runs in which role is [ADR-104](#adr-104--subsystems-per-role-web-serves-worker-owns-background-work-and-leases). Anything a later request needs lives in
PostgreSQL, Valkey (ephemeral only) or object storage; in-process state is limited to rebuildable
caches and the scratch space of the running request or job ([ADR-096](#adr-096--no-state-between-requests-on-a-replica-inv-18)). Work that must run once
runs as a job or under a lease on a `worker` replica ([ADR-034](#adr-034--one-postgresql-job-table-for-maintenance-api-operations-and-internal-work), [ADR-077](#adr-077--singleton-work-under-advisory-lock-leases-with-fencing)). The role split is MVP
([R-HA-002](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-002--role-split-into-api-packages-and-worker-deployments), whose heading keeps the earlier name `api`), and splitting a role into pools is P1
([R-HA-062](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-062--further-splits-of-a-role-into-several-deployments)). The replica registry's table, heartbeat, pruning of stale rows and read-only API are
MVP, and so is the UI's system status screen that shows them ([Q-HA-12](spec/ha-and-helm.md#q-ha-12--replica-registry-at-mvp), option (c); [R-UI-038](spec/api-and-ui.md#r-ui-038--system-status)).
Since 2026-10-28 the registry also records each replica's node and the Sentinels it reaches, so the
status screen groups replicas by role and states drain safety per role ([Q-UI-7](spec/api-and-ui.md#q-ui-7--roles-drain-readiness-and-valkey-on-the-system-status-screen), option (b)).

**Alternatives considered.** A primary node with failover: an election to get right and a single
point of failure while it runs. A separate worker binary or image: two artifacts for one release.
Peer membership between replicas (gossip, consensus): needs replica-to-replica networking, which
this design avoids entirely ([R-HA-001](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-001--active-active-replicas-without-a-primary-node)). `all` as the chart's default with an optional split, the
earlier decision: background work competes with request latency for CPU and memory, and one drain
removes both functions from a node at once.

**Changed on 2026-11-04.** The owner cut Quader into task areas: roles of one binary, each its own Deployment, with network
seams only at trust or load boundaries ([ADR-153](#adr-153--quader-is-cut-into-task-areas-roles-of-one-binary-network-seams-only-at-trust-or-load-boundaries)), and chose three roles ([ADR-155](#adr-155--three-roles-api-packages-and-worker-variants-are-pools)). The role table of this entry is replaced by
[R-ARCH-001](spec/architecture.md#r-arch-001--one-binary-identical-replicas-process-roles)'s (specified for phase 6a, not built
yet):
- **`api`** serves the route families `ui`, `api` and `ci_exchange` and holds the sessions, the OIDC client secrets and the
  break-glass password;
- **`packages`** serves the route families `packages` and `files` with tokens only, evaluates no session cookie and fills the
  client misses;
- **`worker`** runs the job queue, the leases, the scheduler, the mirror's passes and the advisory sync, split into pools by
  queue where an installation wants it;
- **`backup`** and **`bastion`** stay as they were; **`all`** stays the development role;
- **`web`**, until then every HTTP request, stays in the binary as `api` and `packages` in one process and was rendered by the
  chart only as the bridge of the upgrade across the cut ([Q-ARCH-295](spec/architecture.md#q-arch-295--what-becomes-of-the-role-name-web));
  since 2026-11-19 the chart renders it no longer, because no Quader release precedes the cut, and the binary keeps it for
  development and tests ([Q-HA-315](spec/ha-and-helm.md#q-ha-315--the-charts-upgrade-bridge-across-the-cut-is-removed-the-binary-keeps-the-role-web-for-development-and-tests)).

The chart deploys `api`, `packages` and `worker` as separate Deployments, each with its own replica count, autoscaler,
disruption budget, ingress policy ([ADR-154](#adr-154--network-policies-are-ingress-rules-between-the-charts-pods-each-with-its-port)) and topology spread; the edge splits each host by path prefix between the `api` and
`packages` Services ([R-HA-037](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-037--service-ingress-and-tls-at-the-edge)). A variant of a role by
path prefix or by queue is a pool of that role, rendered from values
([R-HA-062](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-062--further-splits-of-a-role-into-several-deployments), now MVP). Until then this entry
named `web` and `worker` as the chart's two Deployments and said that a further split was P1.

**Spec:** [INV-2](spec/README.md#design-invariants), [R-ARCH-001](spec/architecture.md#r-arch-001--one-binary-identical-replicas-process-roles), [R-HA-001](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-001--active-active-replicas-without-a-primary-node),
[R-HA-002](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-002--role-split-into-api-packages-and-worker-deployments), [R-HA-003](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-003--replica-registry-as-the-coordination-view), [R-HA-062](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-062--further-splits-of-a-role-into-several-deployments); decided: [Q-HA-12](spec/ha-and-helm.md#q-ha-12--replica-registry-at-mvp), [Q-UI-7](spec/api-and-ui.md#q-ui-7--roles-drain-readiness-and-valkey-on-the-system-status-screen).

### ADR-014 · PostgreSQL is the system of record; Valkey holds only shared ephemeral state (INV-3)

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough

**Context.** Configuration, metadata, identities, audit, jobs and coordination all need durable,
shared state. Each additional stateful system needs its own HA, backup and upgrade story. Changed
by the owner's constraints of 2026-10-28 ([ADR-092](#adr-092--high-availability-on-ha-postgresql-ha-valkey-with-sentinel-and-s3)): HA Valkey with Sentinel is part of every
production installation. Until then this entry decided "No Redis": PostgreSQL held all
cross-replica coordination, including the fetch lock of cache fills and `LISTEN/NOTIFY`
invalidation. That decision is superseded; Valkey takes part within the limits below.

**Decision.** PostgreSQL is the system of record. It holds repository configuration, package and
file metadata, users, groups, tokens, permissions, audit events, the durable job queue, the change
log that carries cross-replica invalidation, and backup run records; the backup target, not the
database, is the record of the backups themselves. Valkey holds shared ephemeral state only:
- cross-replica request collapsing;
- the negative cache of remote repositories;
- rate-limit counters with cluster scope;
- the fast path of change messages and signals;
- short-lived coordination.

Three rules bound Valkey:
- **Nothing served, nothing that grants.** No content, metadata or credential that Quader serves,
  and no positive authentication or authorization result, is read from Valkey.
- **Never the only copy.** Losing Valkey or its contents (an outage, a Sentinel failover with
  asynchronous replication, a flush, a restart) costs performance only, never correctness or data.
- **Exclusion stays in PostgreSQL.** Mutual exclusion whose failure would corrupt data (schema
  migrations, singleton jobs that must not run twice) uses PostgreSQL.

No shared filesystem and no embedded database. A backup does not include Valkey. Migrations are
embedded in the binary and applied by `quader migrate` (Helm pre-install and pre-upgrade Job) under
a PostgreSQL advisory lock. Migrations follow expand/contract, so N and N-1 run side by side during
a rolling upgrade.

**Consequences.** PostgreSQL's availability is Quader's availability for nearly every request;
Valkey's is not ([ADR-023](#adr-023--high-availability-and-horizontal-scale-on-ha-postgresql-ha-valkey-and-s3-inv-12), [ADR-100](#adr-100--valkey-degrades-quader-but-never-gates-readiness-except-for-configuration-errors)). The change log replaces `NOTIFY`: a writing
transaction increments its change area's epoch and inserts a change row, every replica polls the
log, and a Valkey message can only evict early ([Q-ARCH-15](spec/architecture.md#q-arch-15--cross-replica-invalidation-without-listennotify), [ADR-031](#adr-031--caches-validate-themselves-notifications-only-evict-early)). [R-ARCH-030](spec/architecture.md#r-arch-030--valkey-usage-map)
assigns every cross-replica mechanism to one of the two stores ([ADR-098](#adr-098--valkey-holds-coordination-and-the-negative-cache-nothing-served-and-nothing-that-grants)). A connection budget per
role is part of sizing ([R-HA-016](spec/ha-and-helm.md#r-ha-016--connection-budget-and-pool-sizing), [ADR-101](#adr-101--connection-model-a-transaction-scoped-main-pool-behind-an-optional-pooler-sessions-only-on-workers)). Decided:
- **Query layer** ([Q-ARCH-2](spec/architecture.md#q-arch-2--postgresql-driver-and-query-layer), option (d); revisited on 2026-10-28, unchanged). A hybrid on
  pgx's native API: sqlc for every static query, and one confined builder, `listq`, for the
  dynamic list and search queries, with bound values and allowlisted identifiers. Quader no longer
  uses `LISTEN`, and pgx's exec modes let the main pool run through a transaction-mode pooler.
- **Counters stay in PostgreSQL** ([Q-STOR-12](spec/storage.md#q-stor-12--counters-that-several-replicas-update-usage-quotas-and-download-statistics), option (a)). Usage and quota counters are
  append-only deltas that every `worker` replica folds every 5 s, because a quota must survive a
  loss of Valkey's data; a restore recounts them.
- **No `database/sql`.** Neither `database/sql` nor `pgx/v5/stdlib` is imported anywhere, which an
  architecture test enforces ([R-ARCH-019](spec/architecture.md#r-arch-019--database-access-connection-naming-and-budget)).
- **Migration runner.** A Quader-owned runner on native pgx ([Q-ARCH-3](spec/architecture.md#q-arch-3--migration-runner), [ADR-033](#adr-033--versioning-promises-per-surface-and-a-schema-compatibility-gate)).
- **Version floor.** PostgreSQL 16 ([Q-HA-2](spec/ha-and-helm.md#q-ha-2--postgresql-version-floor)).

**Alternatives considered.** PostgreSQL as the only stateful dependency besides object storage
("No Redis"), the earlier decision: every replica held a `LISTEN` session and a pool of
session-locked fetch connections, so direct sessions grew with the replica count, which INV-12
now forbids; superseded by the owner's constraint. Valkey as a second system of record (sessions,
counters, the job queue): a Sentinel failover with asynchronous replication can lose acknowledged
writes. A coordination service such as etcd: the same cost, and not the service the owner named.
An embedded database per replica: no shared state, so no HA.

**Spec:** [INV-3](spec/README.md#design-invariants), [R-ARCH-016](spec/architecture.md#r-arch-016--background-job-framework-on-postgresql), [R-ARCH-018](spec/architecture.md#r-arch-018--in-process-caches-and-cross-replica-invalidation), [R-ARCH-019](spec/architecture.md#r-arch-019--database-access-connection-naming-and-budget),
