untyped `Request.HostState` slot that the dispatcher filled by calling the implementation package; npm copied the whole request to
tell the spool a body length that is not the request's; and an error shape had no way to name the repository it refused. NuGet
needs the last two (a multipart part, an absolute URL in a 404), and the contract freeze (E3.3) cannot carry the first.

**Decision.** The dispatcher talks to the host through `formats.Host` only: `Host.Begin(rq)` returns the function that releases the
request's state, which the host keeps in the context of the request. The declared length of a spooled body is an option of the
spool (`IngestOptions.Length`). A refusal receives the format, the repository key as addressed and the base URL as a `Refusal`
value in the request's context. A route declares `APIKey` when it accepts the format's API-key header.

**Consequences.** The contract has no untyped member and no method that only one implementation package can serve. A format reads
a request fact from a typed accessor or an option. The context carries two values (the host's state, the refusal) that no format
reads except through their accessors.

**Alternatives considered.** New parameters of `WriteError`; a `Begin` that returns the request; keeping the untyped slot. Decided
in [Q-ARCH-263](spec/architecture.md#q-arch-263--a-refusal-learns-the-repository-key-and-the-base-url-from-the-request-it-is-rendered-with),
[Q-ARCH-264](spec/architecture.md#q-arch-264--the-declared-length-of-a-spooled-body-is-an-option-of-the-spool),
[Q-ARCH-265](spec/architecture.md#q-arch-265--the-host-begins-a-request-through-the-host-interface-and-keeps-its-state-in-the-requests-context)
and [Q-ARCH-266](spec/architecture.md#q-arch-266--a-route-declares-that-it-accepts-the-api-key-header).

**Spec:** [spec/architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-008, R-ARCH-009, R-ARCH-014.
## Compatibility checks and the TypeScript hold

### ADR-139 · Compatibility is checked against the latest release in CI

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough

**Superseded until the first stable release** by [Q-ARCH-340](spec/architecture.md#q-arch-340--no-backward-compatibility-until-the-first-stable-release) (owner, 2026-11-06): the `compat` job is switched off
(`if: false`, and out of the needs of Semantic Release); `make compat-check` and `test/compat/` stay and still run by hand; Quader
is pre-alpha and keeps no backward compatibility until then.

**Context.** R-ARCH-025 and R-ARCH-026 promise that the management API and the migration files stay compatible with what users
installed. Nothing in CI compared them with a release, so a breaking change in `api/openapi.yaml`, or an edited migration, would
have shipped unnoticed.

**Decision.** The `compat` job of the Test and Release workflow runs `make compat-check` on every change. It compares
`api/openapi.yaml` with the newest `v0.*` release tag whose commit is not HEAD's, with oasdiff at its pin in
`tools/versions.env`, and fails on an error-level change. It checks the migration directory since that release: only additions,
with the numbering continuing. Semantic Release needs the job, so a failing check blocks the release. There is no waiver.

**Consequences.** A breaking change in `/api/v1`, or an edited migration, cannot reach a release by accident; an intended one
must become a new API version. The job reads the tags, so its checkout fetches the whole history (`fetch-depth: 0`,
`fetch-tags: true`), and a clone without tags fails rather than passes. The job covers the OpenAPI document and the migration
files only. The other surfaces of R-ARCH-025 and its Helm upgrade test are not part of it.

**Alternatives considered.** A snapshot of the spec committed at each release; the previous commit of main as the baseline; a list of
waived changes; oasdiff as a `go.mod` tool directive. Decided in
[Q-ARCH-273](spec/architecture.md#q-arch-273--how-is-the-openapi-breaking-change-checker-pinned-and-run) and
[Q-ARCH-274](spec/architecture.md#q-arch-274--what-is-the-baseline-and-what-do-the-checks-accept).

**Spec:** [architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-025 and R-ARCH-026; code in `test/compat`, the `compat-check` target of the
`Makefile`, and the job `compat` of `.github/workflows/release.yml`.

### ADR-140 · TypeScript is held below 6.1 until Angular's peer range admits 7.x

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough

**Context.** Renovate PR #42 proposes TypeScript 6.0.3 → 7.0.2 in `web/package.json`. The newest Angular 22 patches
(`@angular/compiler-cli` 22.2.4 and `@angular/build` 22.2.5) declare `typescript >=6.0 <6.1`, and typescript-eslint 8.72.1 declares
`<6.1.0`. TypeScript 7.0.2 exports no compiler API from its package root, which the bundles of `@angular/compiler-cli` import. A
lock file takes 7.0.2 only by overriding those peer ranges. Checked on 2026-11-01; the Angular build with 7.0.2 was not run.

**Decision.** A packageRule in `renovate.json` sets `allowedVersions: "<6.1"` for `typescript`. Renovate does not propose the 7.x
update. Patch releases of 6.0 continue.

**Consequences.** The UI stays on TypeScript 6.0 until the condition holds. The hold is one rule with its reason in its description,
and a person lifts it. A later 6.1 is held too, because the peer ranges stop there. Whether Renovate closes the open PR #42 on its
next run is not verified: the rule has not run.

**Alternatives considered.** Merging PR #42 and fixing the build (not possible while Angular declares the range); grouping
typescript with the Angular packages (a group cannot change the ranges); closing PR #42 by hand each time; `ignoreDeps` for
typescript (no bound). Decided in
[Q-ARCH-275](spec/architecture.md#q-arch-275--how-is-the-typescript-7-update-held).

**Revisit condition:** `@angular/compiler-cli` and `@angular/build` admit typescript 7.x, and typescript-eslint admits it too. The
rule is then removed in the same change that moves TypeScript.

**Spec:** [architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) Q-ARCH-275; `renovate.json`; [releasing.md](developer/releasing.md#renovate).

## The format contract freeze

### ADR-141 · The format contract is frozen at version 1

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough

**Context.** M3's exit criterion E3.3: at the end of M3 the format contract (R-ARCH-008, R-ARCH-009) has `ContractVersion`
1, both formats pass the conformance kit, any contract change NuGet needed was applied to npm in the same change, and from
then on every contract change is an ADR. Until the freeze the contract changed with every format that landed
(Q-ARCH-213). [ADR-136](#adr-136--the-format-contract-freezes-at-version-1-as-the-smaller-contract-and-grows-by-optional-interfaces)
fixed the shape of what freezes: the smaller contract, growing by optional interfaces (Q-ARCH-256). NuGet's work then
added, each in one change with npm: the fill hook and the discovery document as optional interfaces of the remote adapter
(Q-ARCH-267, Q-ARCH-268; npm needs neither and is untouched); the pass-through query as a method with a refusing default
in `RemoteBase`, and the plan, withheld-term and read-scope questions and the artifact gate as services of the fetcher and
the resolver (Q-ARCH-270 to Q-ARCH-272); the artifact prefix as a method of the virtual adapter, which npm implements
since the same commit; the stored versions as a method of the view adapter (Q-ARCH-253), which kit check 11 runs for both;
and the typed request facts of [ADR-138](#adr-138--what-the-core-knows-of-a-request-reaches-a-format-as-a-typed-value-never-as-an-untyped-slot-or-a-request-copy).
The freeze review (WP3.5, 2026-11-02) found no npm or NuGet concept left in a shared type, method or field name: what
remains are labelled examples in comments. It corrected the comments that still described the contract before the freeze,
and it found that the tests could not hold the rule "every change is an ADR": only the types the spec blocks declare
were compared member by member, and the kit let routes and hooks pass checks it never ran.

**Decision.** The format contract is frozen at `ContractVersion` 1: the exported surface of `internal/formats` and of the
catalog leaf `internal/formats/catalog` that a descriptor embeds, as `internal/formats/testdata/contract.txt` records it.
From here on:
- Every change of that surface is an ADR of its own, in the same change as the code, the spec blocks and the regenerated
  surface file. `TestR_ARCH_025_TheFrozenContractChangesOnlyWithItsSurfaceFile` fails until the file is regenerated, so
  no change passes unnoticed (Q-ARCH-280).
- Additive evolution, the rule of Q-ARCH-256 in R-ARCH-025: a behaviour whose presence the core must know, because it
  changes what an engine does, is an optional interface of `internal/formats` with a field in `Capabilities`, found by
  `CapabilitiesOf` when the format registers; a behaviour every format answers, whose default is a correct answer for a
  format without it, is a method with that default in `Base` or `RemoteBase`; a service for formats is a method of
  `Host`, `PackageWriter`, the stores, `RemoteFetcher` or `Resolver`, which formats call and never implement. None of
  these changes a registered format, and `ContractVersion` stays 1.
- A breaking change (a method or field leaves, a signature changes, an argument gains a rule or a result a case) raises
  `ContractVersion` to 2 in the same change, moves every registered format onto it, and its ADR names what breaks;
  `Register` refuses a format still written against 1. The narrowed signatures of Q-ARCH-260 (a format names only its
  own repository, H-329) are the first such change on record.
- The conformance kit is the evidence: npm and NuGet pass all eleven checks with none skipped, and what a check does not
  look at is a fixture entry with its reason (`NoRevision`, `NoContent`; Q-ARCH-281). A new behaviour brings its kit check
  in the change that adds it, and a check added later applies to every format in its change.

**Consequences.** The surface file is a second written form of the contract, but a generated one: it cannot drift, and its
diff is the checklist of the review. Comments, the spec prose and unexported code change freely. The test does not tell
an addition from a breaking change; the ADR does, and the version line sits in the same diff. The P1 work that needs a
seam (retention, the trash can's restore, the NuGet symbol-index job and reindex) and M4b's `VulnerabilityAdapter` each
bring an ADR. Left as they are across the freeze, and not breaking when they come (Q-ARCH-261, Q-ARCH-262): the
rendition ETag helper, a typed environment instead of `Bind`, the engine value types and the recorded populate decision
through a virtual repository. Check 7 does not look at the npm audit's forwarded answer (its own tests do) or at NuGet's
three P1 routes, and the fixtures say so.

**Alternatives considered.** Freezing by review alone (the rule stays prose); every type in the spec blocks (the spec page
as an API listing, and still no signal that a change needs an ADR); an API compatibility checker against the last release
(a new pinned tool that passes additions, which here need an ADR too); raising the version at the freeze (nothing broke:
npm and NuGet moved with every change before it). Decided in
[Q-ARCH-280](spec/architecture.md#q-arch-280--how-is-the-frozen-format-contract-guarded-so-that-no-change-passes-without-its-adr)
and [Q-ARCH-281](spec/architecture.md#q-arch-281--how-does-the-conformance-kit-keep-a-format-from-passing-a-check-it-does-not-run);
the evolution rule in [Q-ARCH-256](spec/architecture.md#q-arch-256--the-dormant-methods-leave-the-frozen-contract-and-the-contract-grows-by-optional-interfaces).

**Revisit condition:** a second module consumes the contract, or a format is built outside this repository; then the
surface file gives way to a compatibility checker against the release, and the version becomes an external promise.

**Spec:** [spec/architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-008, R-ARCH-009, R-ARCH-010, R-ARCH-025;
[coverage/roadmap.md](coverage/roadmap.md#m3--nuget) E3.3 and WP3.5.

### ADR-149 · The format contract gains `SetupData.Bastion` under version 1

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** The client setup of a repository for a Bastion (R-BAS-007, [Q-BAS-96](spec/bastion.md#q-bas-96--a-bastion-is-a-target-of-the-setup-page-and-of-the-guides-read-only-and-by-link-for-everyone))
renders the snippets on the base URL the Bastion reported and offers no publish snippets; for npm the configure snippet sets
`replace-registry-host=always`, so that a lockfile written against another host resolves through the Bastion. The format's setup
renderer is the only place that knows its snippets, so it must learn that the target is a Bastion. The format contract is frozen at
version 1 ([ADR-141](#adr-141--the-format-contract-is-frozen-at-version-1)), and every change of it is an ADR of its own.

**Decision.** `formats.SetupData` gains the field `Bastion bool`, true when the setup is rendered for a Bastion. It is an addition: a
format that does not read it renders exactly what it rendered before, so `ContractVersion` stays 1 and no format has to move. npm reads it
for `replace-registry-host`; the core drops publish snippets for every format when it is set. The surface file
`internal/formats/testdata/contract.txt` is regenerated in the same change.

**Consequences.** A later format may read the field; a format that ignores it gives a Bastion its ordinary snippets on the Bastion's
base URL, which is correct for every format whose clients do not pin hosts in their lockfiles.

**Alternatives considered.** A second render entry point for Bastions (a changed interface, which would raise the version and move every
format); rewriting npm's snippet in the core (format knowledge outside the format, against R-ARCH-008).

**Revisit condition:** a format needs more about the Bastion than the flag (its name or its registration), which would be a field of its own
and an ADR of its own.

### ADR-150 · The format contract gains the optional vulnerability adapter

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** Vulnerability scanning (M4b, [ADR-131](#adr-131--own-vulnerability-scanning-with-a-dashboard-in-the-beta)) matches
the stored versions of a format against OSV advisories with the format's own version order and name normalization
([R-VULN-009](spec/vulnerability-scanning.md#r-vuln-009--version-matching-per-format),
[Q-VULN-15](spec/vulnerability-scanning.md#q-vuln-15--how-formats-join-after-the-contract-freeze)). The format contract is frozen at
version 1 ([ADR-141](#adr-141--the-format-contract-is-frozen-at-version-1)), and every change of it is an ADR of its own.
Two things reach the formats: the adapter, which a format implements so that the core can match its versions, and the
scanning's data, which a format's audit routes (npm's `-/npm/v1/security/advisories/bulk`, NuGet's `VulnerabilityInfo` page)
read.

**Decision.** The contract gains, as additions:
- the optional interface `formats.VulnerabilityAdapter` (R-VULN-009: `Ecosystem`, `AdvisoryName`, `AdvisoryVersion`,
  `CompareVersions`), found by `CapabilitiesOf` when the format registers and recorded as `Capabilities.Vulnerability`, nil
  for a format without it, whose repositories are `not_covered`; `CapabilitiesOf` stays the one place that asserts to an
  interface of the contract;
- the Host service `Host.Vulnerabilities() formats.VulnerabilityData`, which a format's audit routes call and never
  implement: the state of an ecosystem's advisory data, the advisories of names, all advisories of an ecosystem, the internal
  names, and the matcher. A host that has not wired the scanning answers `formats.NoVulnerabilityData()`, for which every
  ecosystem is not complete, so a format never meets nil;
- the catalog leaf's `Entry.Ecosystem`, derived by `formats.Register` from the adapter, so that the repository model, which
  cannot import the contract, knows which formats the member `vulnerabilities` applies to.

The types the new methods speak are the leaf types of `internal/vuln/advisory` and `internal/vuln/match`; the contract imports
them and a format may too (the architecture test's allow-list gains exactly these two packages, not the scanning's domain).
`match.Adapter` has the method set of `VulnerabilityAdapter`, so the scanning's domain, which is below the contract, takes a
format's adapter by structural typing. `ContractVersion` stays 1: no registered format changes, and no other format has to
implement the adapter. npm and NuGet implement it in the work package that builds the matching. The spec blocks of R-ARCH-008
and the surface file `internal/formats/testdata/contract.txt` are updated in the same change.

**Consequences.** A later format joins the scanning by implementing four methods and its repositories change from
`not_covered` to scanned; no change of the core. The conformance kit runs the matching corpus for a format that has the adapter
(Q-VULN-15). The `Host` interface gains a method that only the core implements (`internal/formathost` and the kit's in-memory
host), so a format value is unchanged.

**Alternatives considered.** A method on `Format` (every format would have to decide; a changed method set of a frozen
interface, which raises the version, Q-VULN-15 option b); a table of version orders in the core (format rules in the core,
against R-ARCH-008); handing the scanning's ports to a format as a bound data port (the data port is a format's own table,
Q-ARCH-193, and the audit's data is the core's).

**Revisit condition:** more optional interfaces accumulate (Q-VULN-15's condition), which would justify a contract version.

**Amendment (phase 6 fix wave, [Q-VULN-73](spec/vulnerability-scanning.md#q-vuln-73--the-frozen-contract-records-the-leaves-it-speaks-in-enabled-is-a-port-field-the-matcher-is-called-not-passed)).**
`VulnerabilityData` also carries `CountAudit`, `Enabled`, `LocalByDefault`, `PageKey` and `Page` (the audits of R-VULN-017 and
R-VULN-018: the metric, the two switches and the cache of the NuGet page), all additions in the sense of R-ARCH-025.
`Enabled` is set explicitly by the composition root (`formathost.VulnPorts.Enabled`), not derived from the wired ports.
`Affects` is removed from the interface: the matcher is a pure function of the leaf `internal/vuln/match`, which a format
imports and calls itself. The surface file now also records the types of `internal/vuln/advisory` (with its constants) and
`internal/vuln/match`, so a change of a type the contract returns fails `TestR_ARCH_025` like a change of the contract.
The same fix wave added `match.Prepare` and the method `Entry.Affects` (an affected entry normalized once and evaluated
against many versions, for the bounded local audit of [Q-VULN-71](spec/vulnerability-scanning.md#q-vuln-71--what-the-client-audits-and-the-list-filters-tell-a-caller)): an addition, recorded in the surface file.

**Spec:** [spec/vulnerability-scanning.md](spec/vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-009, Q-VULN-15, Q-VULN-23, Q-VULN-73;
[spec/architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-008.

## Quader Bastion

### ADR-142 · The Quader Bastion: an internet-facing, read-only cache instance in the beta

**Status:** Accepted (owner constraint, 2026-10-31 and 2026-11-02). Its cache rule Q-BAS-10 (never the main installation's object store) is
lifted in part by the owner on 2026-11-22: a link and the data key per released blob ([ADR-250](#adr-250--the-handover-per-blob-to-a-bastion-a-link-and-the-data-key-of-one-released-blob-in-the-answer-to-its-forward)).

**Context.** On 2026-10-31 the owner asked for a second, smaller deployment that serves a main installation's packages close to
its consumers, read-only, asking the main installation about credentials instead of holding a copy of them; it was planned as
milestone M13 after the beta. On 2026-11-02 the owner moved it into the beta as phase 5b, before vulnerability scanning, and
decided its shape in a series of decisions: an exposed artifact instance that gives external parties read access, caches
artifacts and takes as much load as possible off the main installation, exposed to the internet and to denial-of-service
attempts.

**Decision.** The Quader Bastion is the role `bastion` of the Quader image, deployed only by its own chart `quader-bastion`, without
PostgreSQL, a web interface, a login or settings outside the chart. It connects to the main endpoint of the main installation
with a token an administrator of the main installation issues for it, which reads no package; it fetches with each caller's own
token, caches the bytes in an own bucket or a local volume (never the main installation's object store), and serves a cached item
to a caller only after the main installation said that caller may read it. It keeps those answers for a configurable period,
follows a revocation feed every few seconds, keeps answers for a grace period while the main installation is unreachable and then
serves nothing. It mirrors the main installation's URL space, the main installation renders documents for its host, and documents
are shared only with callers the main installation confirmed as reading the whole repository. Valkey is optional. It blocks in two
stages, the Bastion's own and a coarser one at HAProxy Ingress; volumetric attacks are the network provider's. Downloads served
from its cache are reported to the main installation's audit. Its token is renewed by hand with an overlap. Its interface with the
main installation has a version of its own, equal on both sides, and a mismatch is alerted.

**Consequences.** A beta phase and a spec page; the roadmap's M13 points at the page. INV-2 gains the role, INV-13 the chart,
INV-8 the token prefix (ADR-144), and INV-3 a refinement for the Bastion's Valkey (ADR-143). The catalog entries the page covers
(RMT-040, RMT-041, RMT-044, DIST-024, DIST-025) are raised to MVP. The further endpoint as the way to reach outside parties is
replaced by the Bastion; endpoints stay a capability of the main installation.

**Alternatives considered.** None; set by the owner. The owner's options are recorded as Q-BAS-1 to Q-BAS-21.

**Spec:** [spec/bastion.md](spec/bastion.md), [spec/README.md](spec/README.md#owner-constraints),
[projektplan/BETA.md](projektplan/BETA.md#phase-5b--quader-bastion-m13).

### ADR-143 · The Bastion decides through the main installation's own routes and answers it keeps briefly

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough

**Context.** The owner's decisions leave the Bastion without format knowledge and without a copy of identities, yet require it to
serve cached content only to callers the main installation allowed, to share documents only with confirmed full readers, and to
drop revoked tokens within seconds; Valkey may share the main installation's answers, which INV-3 forbade for the main
installation because whoever writes Valkey could grant.

**Decision.** A cached artifact is checked by a conditional request with the caller's own credential through the real route, which
the main installation answers from PostgreSQL after its normal decision; responses to Bastion requests carry marking headers the
core derives from the route kind and the caller's read shape (`full` over every member of a virtual repository, the populate right
included). The revocation feed reads the journaled audit events with a lookback and adds withdrawn content; answers validate
themselves at use against the receipt times of feed entries; answers stored in Valkey are signed; cached artifacts are revalidated
after a period, so withdrawals the feed does not carry are bounded too.

**Consequences.** One decision path: the Bastion never decides what the main installation's routes would not. Callers with
narrowed reads cost one conditional request per artifact and period; callers who read the whole repository cost none. INV-3 is
refined for the Bastion, not for the main installation. Gaps H-383, H-385 and H-387 record what remains.

**Alternatives considered.** A check operation that classifies paths into coordinates (a second classifier next to the format's
routes); the Bastion parsing paths per format (format knowledge); the change log as the feed (internal payloads, broadenings,
resets on pruning); deleting answers on feed entries without use-time validation (a race that keeps a revoked token for the
period); unsigned answers in Valkey (a Valkey writer could grant). Decided in Q-BAS-27 to Q-BAS-33.

**Revisit condition:** callers with narrowed reads dominate a Bastion's traffic, or every withdrawal gains a feed entry.

**Spec:** [spec/bastion.md](spec/bastion.md) R-BAS-012, R-BAS-013, R-BAS-015, R-BAS-020, R-BAS-022, R-BAS-026, R-BAS-032,
R-BAS-034.

### ADR-144 · The Bastion token is a type of its own, and the interface a version of its own

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough (the version's existence and the equality rule are
the owner's, ADR-142)

**Context.** The owner requires a token issued by an administrator of the main installation that only has tokens checked and reads
no package, and an interface version raised only when the interface changes.

**Decision.** The Bastion token has the type `bst` (`qdr_bst_`) and belongs to a principal of the kind `bastion` that holds no
grants; every route but the Bastion interface refuses the type before a lookup. Registrations are managed with `endpoints:*`,
revocation also with `tokens:revoke`. The interface lives under `/api/v1/bastion/` on the main endpoint, with the Bastion token in
`Quader-Bastion-Authorization` on forwarded requests; every change of the interface raises `bastion.InterfaceVersion`, guarded by a
surface file and its test, like the frozen format contract.

**Consequences.** INV-8 gains a prefix; R-AUTH-022 a type; R-AUTHZ-002 a principal kind; R-ARCH-025 a surface. Main installation
and Bastions upgrade together when the version rises.

**Alternatives considered.** A service-account token narrowed by scope (reads no package only as long as no grant reaches the
service account); a shared static secret (no issuance or revocation); a listener of its own for the interface; additive changes
within a version. Decided in Q-BAS-23 to Q-BAS-26.

**Revisit condition:** a second kind of machine client needs the same token shape, or lockstep upgrades become a burden after the
stable release.

**Spec:** [spec/bastion.md](spec/bastion.md) R-BAS-004, R-BAS-005, R-BAS-008, R-BAS-009.

### ADR-145 · The grants of a project policy are stored where the previous release does not read them

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough

**Context.** Projects (R-AUTHZ-026) let a delegate write policies whose pattern and class selectors apply to the project's
repositories only. The released 0.9.x binaries build their grant index without any notion of a project; during a rolling
upgrade, and after a rollback, such a replica reads a project policy as a global one and grants on every repository what the
delegate wrote for the project. Only a contract step raises the schema's compatibility floor (R-HA-018).

**Decision.** The entries of project policies live in `authz_project_policy_entry`, which the previous release does not
read; for it a project policy has no entries and covers nobody. A composite foreign key lets the table hold rows of project
policies only, and a trigger on `authz_policy_entry` refuses rows for them, so a rewrite by the old release fails. The
current release reads both tables in the same statements.

**Consequences.** Fail closed by construction, in the database. The index build, the policy read, the policy write, the
cleanup of a principal's entries and the test harness handle two tables. A rollout shows a project's rights as absent on
old replicas (availability, not security). A contract step may merge the tables once no 0.9.x installation
runs.

**Alternatives considered.** Refusing project policies while a 0.9.x replica lives (checked at write time only; a later
replica or a rollback reads existing ones as global); accepting the window; a selector form the old build skips with an
error log. Decided in Q-AUTHZ-174.

**Revisit condition:** no installation can run 0.9.x any more.

**Spec:** [spec/authorization.md](spec/authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-026, R-AUTHZ-028.

### ADR-146 · An operation admits project administrators through a declaration of its own

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough; superseded in part by [ADR-156](#adr-156--projects-own-their-repositories-members-hold-roles-names-are-scoped-to-the-project) (2026-11-06): the declaration names the project from the path and the least role (`project: path.projectKey`, `projectRole`), and the shared step narrows to that project itself

**Context.** Every management operation names the permission it needs in `x-quader-permission`, and one shared step enforces
it before the handler (R-API-008). A project administrator holds no capability, and which project an operation addresses
is often known only to the handler.

**Decision.** A declaration may carry `projectAdmin: <right>` next to `permission`: the step admits the holder of the
capability, or a caller that administers at least one project (whatever the right), and the handler narrows to the addressed
project with `requireProject`, `requireProjectOfRepository` or `delegatedScope`. The engine answers three questions on the
request's index (`ProjectsOn`, `AdministersOn`, `AdministersRepositoryOn`). `GET /authz/me` carries `projects`.

**Consequences.** The document says who may call each operation; a build that does not know the member refuses the
document at start-up; a refused caller is refused before any lookup. The step is coarse, so a handler that forgets to
narrow lets a project administrator reach another project: the helpers exist to make that a one-line call, and the
integration tests of R-AUTHZ-026 cover every operation of the table.

**Alternatives considered.** `authenticated: true` and a handler check (the document stops saying who may call); a resolver
per operation in the step (a source for every case). Decided in Q-AUTHZ-180.

**Revisit condition:** an operation needs a project source the handler cannot supply after the step, or a third kind of
delegate appears.

**Amendment (Decided by the development agent, 2026-11-02; owner review at the walkthrough).** The step does not ask for the
declared right, only for administration of at least one project. Reason: a caller whose only project had the switch off
got 403 `forbidden`, one that also administered a project with the switch on got 403 `project_switch_off` for the same
request; the answer must not depend on other projects. The handler narrows (404 for a project not administered, 403
`project_switch_off` for the addressed project's switch off). Decided in Q-AUTHZ-180 (amendment).

**Spec:** [spec/authorization.md](spec/authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-026; [spec/api-and-ui.md](spec/api-and-ui.md) R-API-008.


### ADR-147 · A CI token carries its frozen grants in its cache entry, and the management API refuses CI tokens by default

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough

**Context.** A CI token (R-CI-017) has rights no policy row holds: the inline grants rendered at the exchange, the cap `read`
of a cross-project token and the project identity of its package-ownership records (R-AUTHZ-014). The evaluator must not
query PostgreSQL for them (R-AUTHZ-015), a revocation must reach every replica within the bound of R-AUTH-023, and a CI token
must stay off the management API except for its own `GET` and `DELETE /tokens/current` (R-CI-013).

**Decision.** The exchange writes the frozen bundle (`claims.Frozen`: issuer, project, contributing mappings and groups,
rendered inline grants, caps) to `api_token.ci_context` in the transaction that inserts the token. The token cache entry of
the validator carries it (`token.Info.CI`) through the stage and the chain to `authz.Subject.CI`; the principal set of the
subject is its mappings, so policy and group grants stay live. The shared authorization step of the management API refuses a
CI principal with 403 `ci_token_restricted` on every operation except public ones, those of the action form and those that
declare `x-quader-ci: admitted`.

**Consequences.** Use of a CI token costs no extra read, and the grants die with the token by its own revocation path. The
cache entry grows by the bundle. A new management operation is closed to CI tokens until its declaration says otherwise. The
package-protocol endpoints and `/files/…` are outside the table and admit CI tokens like any token, bounded by scope and
grants. The bundle is also the issuance record's `grants`, so the administrator reads what the token holds.

**Alternatives considered.** Loading issuances into the grant index (a rebuild on every exchange and a row per live token on
every replica); a per-token cache of the issuance record (a second cache beside the token cache); a route table in the
authentication stage or a check in each handler for the gate (an open default). Decided in
[Q-CI-17](spec/gitlab-ci-oidc.md#q-ci-17--how-a-ci-token-reaches-the-authorization-evaluator-at-use-time) and
[Q-CI-18](spec/gitlab-ci-oidc.md#q-ci-18--where-the-gate-lives-that-admits-ci-tokens-on-a-few-operations-only).

**Revisit condition:** the bundle of a token grows past a few KiB in practice, or an operation of the action form turns out
to be one a CI token must not call.

**Spec:** [spec/gitlab-ci-oidc.md](spec/gitlab-ci-oidc.md) R-CI-013, R-CI-017;
[spec/authorization.md](spec/authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-014.

## Schema migrations

### ADR-148 · Migrations on main are immutable, and a defect is fixed forward

**Status:** Decided by the owner on 2026-11-02 — option (b) of [Q-ARCH-283](spec/architecture.md#q-arch-283--is-a-migration-on-main-immutable-and-what-does-the-check-hold-to)

**Superseded until the first stable release** by [Q-ARCH-340](spec/architecture.md#q-arch-340--no-backward-compatibility-until-the-first-stable-release) (owner, 2026-11-06): a migration may be edited, and a changed
migration needs a new database; the immutability check, part of the `compat` job, is switched off.

**Context.** On 2026-11-02 the migration `00019_projects.sql`, committed on `main` in `007c3dfc`, was rewritten in `f5273866` into
expand steps. The owner's dev cluster had applied the first version, and every rollout then failed with a checksum mismatch; the
database was reset. The compatibility check compared the migrations only with the latest `v0.*` tag, and the tags `v0.11.0` to `v0.12.0`
point at commits of `main` made after the rewrite, so the check could not see it. The installation is pre-alpha, so a reset before the beta is an
accepted cost; reliability of installed data becomes priority 1 once the beta plan is complete.

**Decision.** A migration file on `main` is immutable, released or not: it is never edited (not even in a comment or whitespace),
renamed or removed. A defect is fixed forward with a new step of the class the change needs (R-HA-018). A CI check reads the history
of `main` and fails on any change after a file's first commit, except the historical edits named one by one in
`test/compat/migrations_history_test.go`; the same target, `make compat-check`, runs it on every pull request and push to `main`.

**Consequences.** An edit to a migration fails the pull request, before any database applies it. The check needs the whole history
(`fetch-depth: 0`), and a force-push to `main` would remove the commits it reads. The developer guide states the rule for a
contributor ([database.md](developer/database.md#how-to-add-a-migration)).

**Alternatives considered.** The latest release only, as before (an edit before the newest tag passes); immutability once applied
anywhere (no check can know which databases applied a file; the runner's checksum refuses it only where the file was applied).

**Revisit condition:** the beta plan is complete, or the history of `main` is rewritten, or a migration has to change after it
reached a database.

**Spec:** [spec/architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-026 and Q-ARCH-283; [spec/ha-and-helm.md](spec/ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-018.

## Remote full mirror

### ADR-151 · A remote repository can mirror its upstream in the background

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough. The request is the owner's (2026-11-02): pull-through
stays the default of a remote repository, and a remote can also be set to full mirror, in which Quader downloads and keeps what it
can discover at the upstream on its own.

**Context.** A remote repository fetches what clients ask for and nothing ahead of time (INV-11). A build that needs a package
the cache never saw fails while the upstream is down, and a public registry throttles installations that fetch in bursts. A
mirror of a public registry would be terabytes, so a mirror needs bounds, and it must never take capacity from clients.

**Decision.** A remote repository has the mode `pullThrough` (the default) or `mirror`, members `remote.mode` and `remote.mirror`
of its document ([spec/repositories-and-proxy.md](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-050). In mode `mirror`, passes as jobs
of the job framework on their own queue `mirror` (one per repository at a time, dispatched every minute, R-REPO-053) discover the upstream's packages through the
format (a feed, a listing or exact names; R-REPO-051), bounded by the include and exclude patterns, the newest versions per
package and a byte bound, which a mirror of a format's well-known upstream must have (R-REPO-052). A pass keeps its state in
PostgreSQL, outside its jobs, fenced by its job and the process that claimed it, and continues after a drain, a restart, a failover, a failure (with
a bounded back-off) or a long rate-limit wait. Rate-limit answers are honoured (`Retry-After`, back-off with jitter, a window
that halves) and never move the clients' circuit (R-REPO-054). The background takes a share of the fetch budget on top of the
clients' unchanged shares, which client fetches pre-empt, in the process and across replicas through a signal (R-REPO-055).
Its fills go through the ordinary remote path, so every rule of a fill applies, and are audited as cache fills with the system
as actor; a status operation, a pass on request, metrics and two alerts make it observable (R-REPO-056, R-REPO-057). The
catalog's pull replication (API-082 to API-085) is pulled forward in this shape; push, bulk switches, peer channels, a global
block and checksum replication stay P2 (Q-REPO-143).

**Consequences.** A remote in mode `mirror` serves clients as before and holds what its bounds admit before anyone asks; a
restore keeps the last complete pass and continues from it (R-REPO-058). Who may switch the mode is the installation's decision
(`repositories:write-config`); a project administrator pauses or turns off (Q-REPO-142). INV-11's "nothing is fetched ahead of
time" held for mode `pullThrough` until a probe started the download of its version
([ADR-207](#adr-207--a-probe-starts-the-download-of-its-version-in-the-background-the-format-contract-is-at-version-7)).

**Alternatives considered.** A replication document per repository in the catalog's shape (Q-REPO-130 (b)); a repository class
`mirror` (against INV-5); a long-running job per mirror (Q-REPO-131 (c)); shrinking the client shares for the background
(Q-REPO-140 (a)); counting background rate limits toward the circuit (Q-REPO-139 (a)).

**Revisit condition:** a mirror needs more than one upstream, or installations run so many mirrors that per-repository passes
and operations do not scale.

**Spec:** [spec/repositories-and-proxy.md](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-050 to R-REPO-059 and Q-REPO-130 to Q-REPO-148;
[spec/formats/npm.md](spec/formats/npm.md) and [spec/formats/nuget.md](spec/formats/nuget.md), section "Mirror discovery";
[spec/architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) Q-ARCH-284 to Q-ARCH-288.

### ADR-152 · The format contract gains the optional mirror lister

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** The mirror engine is a domain package; what an upstream offers and what a package consists of are format
knowledge. The format contract is frozen at version 1 ([ADR-141](#adr-141--the-format-contract-is-frozen-at-version-1)), and
every change of it is an ADR of its own.

**Decision.** The contract gains, as additions: the alias `formats.MirrorLister` of the leaf interface `discover.Lister`
(`MirrorMethods`, `MirrorNames`, `MirrorPlan`, `MirrorHosts`), an optional interface of the remote adapter that
`CapabilitiesOf` records as `RemoteCaps.Mirror`; and the catalog fact `Entry.Mirror`, which `CatalogEntry` derives from it, so
that the repository model, which cannot import the contract, refuses `remote.mode: mirror` for a format without it. The types
the methods speak are the leaf `internal/mirror/discover`: the methods and passes, the cursor, the scope, the page request
and page, the plan and its items, the `Upstream` the engine lends a format (its `Get` and `Document` go through the
repository's client and the remote engine with the background priority) and the `RateLimited` error that a format returns
unchanged. The architecture test's allow-list for formats gains exactly that leaf; the surface file records its types and
constants. `ContractVersion` stays 1: no registered format has to implement the interface. npm and NuGet implement it in the
work packages of phase 6b (Q-ARCH-288); no remote adapter implements the lister until the engine exists, so `mode: mirror` is refused with `not_applicable` (R-REPO-050).

**Consequences.** A later format joins the mirror mode by implementing four methods; no change of the core. The engine takes a
format's lister by its type, without importing the contract (Q-ARCH-284).

**Alternatives considered.** A port in the engine and an adapter in `internal/formathost` (every type twice); a method of
`RemoteAdapter` with a default (a changed method set of a frozen interface).

**Revisit condition:** more optional interfaces accumulate (ADR-150's condition), which would justify a contract version.

**Spec:** [spec/architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-008 and Q-ARCH-284; [spec/repositories-and-proxy.md](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-050.

## Backup lane contracts

### ADR-157 · The backup lane is cut into ports, formats and registries that its work packages fill in files of their own

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** The backup lane (phase 7: create, retention and sweep, restore, the revocation journal, the npm and NuGet parts, the
API and the chart) is built by several work packages in parallel. Without shared contracts they would edit the same files: the
on-target format is read by the create pipeline, the sweep, verify and restore; the run record by every operation, the API and the
collector; the restore's derived state belongs to the pages that own it.

**Decision.** The shared shapes are fixed first, in packages that no work package owns afterwards
([Q-BAK-14](spec/backup-and-restore.md#q-bak-14--the-package-cut-of-the-backup-lane)):
`internal/backup/format` (backup ID, layout, marker, manifest, blob list and its merge), `internal/backup/target` (the port of the
S3 target, with an in-memory fake), `internal/backup/fixup` (the registry of restore fix-ups and remote-cache purgers),
`internal/backup` (exit codes, run states, the run store, the lease handle, the ports to the source database and blob store, the
operation interfaces, the metric families) and `internal/journal` (below). The AWS SDK stays in `internal/blob/s3`
([Q-BAK-15](spec/backup-and-restore.md#q-bak-15--the-s3-implementation-of-the-target-port-is-built-in-internalblobs3)); the pins are
inserted in batches ([Q-BAK-17](spec/backup-and-restore.md#q-bak-17--the-to-copy-set-is-inserted-in-batches-with-unnest-not-with-copy-from-stdin));
the backup commands load a configuration of their own and map every failure to the exit codes of R-BAK-013
([Q-BAK-18](spec/backup-and-restore.md#q-bak-18--the-backup-commands-load-their-configuration-as-commandbackup-and-every-failure-maps-to-one-exit-code-and-one-failure-code)).
Each command of `cmd/quader` has a file of its own with a constructor that returns `backup.NotBuilt` until its work package replaces
the body. `backup` is a command of the one binary, not a role ([Q-ARCH-342](spec/architecture.md#q-arch-342--backup-is-a-command-journal-is-a-domain-package-and-the-lanes-registries-are-listed-as-frozen-state)).

**Consequences.** The packages of the lane own disjoint files ([docs/developer/backup.md](developer/backup.md)). The run record, the
fenced heartbeat and the one-active rule exist once, with an integration test. A parallel build can run against `targettest.Mem` and
fakes of the ports before the S3 adapter exists.

**Alternatives considered.** One `internal/backup` package; the SDK in the backup package; a `backup` serving role; a restore that
lists its own fix-ups.

**Revisit condition:** a package of the cut grows a second reason to change, or a target other than S3 is added.

**Spec:** [spec/backup-and-restore.md](spec/backup-and-restore.md) Q-BAK-13 to Q-BAK-19, R-BAK-004, R-BAK-009, R-BAK-010, R-BAK-013, R-BAK-022;
[spec/architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-002 and Q-ARCH-342.

### ADR-158 · A journal object is an envelope around the producer's entry, and replay is a registry of handlers

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** The revocation journal (R-HA-054) has producers in every domain, which already write their entries through the audit
event, and two commands replay it (`quader backup restore`, `quader admin post-restore`). The update rule that decides between
applying, skipping and suspending is shared; the comparator that feeds it belongs to the page that owns the object.

**Decision.** A journal object is `{v, id, at, event, entry}` with the producer's entry verbatim
([Q-HA-140](spec/ha-and-helm.md#q-ha-140--a-journal-object-is-an-envelope-around-the-producers-entry)). A domain replays its events with
`journal.Register` in a file of its own, and applies the update rule with `journal.ApplyUpdate[T]` over a `journal.Narrower[T]` that it
implements ([Q-HA-141](spec/ha-and-helm.md#q-ha-141--replay-handlers-are-registered-per-event-name-by-the-domain-that-owns-the-event),
[Q-AUTHZ-230](spec/authorization.md#q-authz-230--the-comparators-of-r-authz-031-are-journalnarrowert-implementations-in-the-owning-packages)).
The reader lists the UTC days of the window and reports an object it cannot read
([Q-HA-142](spec/ha-and-helm.md#q-ha-142--the-replay-reads-the-journal-by-day-prefixes-and-reports-what-it-cannot-read)).

**Consequences.** The identity, authorization, CI, exposure, npm and NuGet parts are added by separate owners without a shared
switch; an event type without a handler is reported `skipped`. The gap that a journal object can be overwritten with the runtime
credential stays open ([H-553](spec/backup-and-restore.md#h-553--a-journal-object-can-be-overwritten-with-the-runtime-credential)).

**Alternatives considered.** The entry as the object; one replay function with a switch on the event; one comparator package.

**Revisit condition:** an entry needs a value that the outbox row does not carry, or a replay needs a batch of entries.

**Spec:** [spec/ha-and-helm.md](spec/ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-054 and Q-HA-140 to Q-HA-142; [spec/authorization.md](spec/authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-031.

### ADR-159 · The data state the format contract carries says whether the ecosystem has synced since the last restore

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** `advisory.DataState`, the state of an ecosystem's advisory data that a format reads from the replica's cache
(`formats.Vulnerability.State`), is part of the frozen format contract (ADR-141, R-ARCH-025). The blocks that a restore replays
(R-VULN-026) rest on records the restored advisory data may not hold, so the evaluation and the remote miss must know whether the
data is older than the restore ([Q-VULN-132](spec/vulnerability-scanning.md#q-vuln-132--a-blocked-finding-whose-version-is-gone-counts-until-its-ecosystem-has-synced-since-the-restore-at-the-remote-miss-and-at-a-commit)).

**Decision.** `DataState` gains the field `NotSyncedSinceRestore`, true when `system_state.restored_at` is set and the ecosystem's
`synced_at` is before it or empty. It is an addition: the zero value is the earlier behaviour, no format reads or sets it, and
`ContractVersion` stays 2. The frozen surface file is regenerated with `go test ./internal/formats -run TestR_ARCH_025 -update-contract`.

**Consequences.** The replica's state cache computes the field with the row it loads (`VulnStateList`), so no request pays a query for
it. A format that renders the state (the NuGet vulnerability index) keys its rendering by `Epoch` as before and ignores the field.

**Alternatives considered.** A second port next to `States` for the restore fact (a second cache and a second call on every
download); the evaluation reading `restored_at` itself on each miss (a query per miss).

**Revisit condition:** a format needs the restore time itself, not only whether the data predates it.

**Spec:** [spec/vulnerability-scanning.md](spec/vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-011, R-VULN-015, R-VULN-026, Q-VULN-132.

### ADR-160 · The catalog says which formats always verify the announced digest

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** `Descriptor.VerifyAnnouncedDigests` makes the remote engine compare a fetched artifact with the digest the format's metadata announces whatever `integrity.checksumPolicy` says (npm, R-REPO-041, R-NPM-025). The repository validation sees only `catalog.Facts`, so it could not tell that the policies `ignore` and `pass-through` change nothing for such a format and left them settable ([Q-NPM-79](spec/formats/npm.md#q-npm-79--npm-always-verifies-the-announced-digest-and-the-policies-that-would-not-are-refused)). The contract is frozen at version 2 (ADR-141, R-ARCH-025): every change of it is an ADR.

**Decision.** `catalog.Facts` gains the field `ChecksumAlwaysVerified`, true for npm. It is an addition: the zero value is the earlier behaviour, no other format sets it, and `ContractVersion` stays 2. The repository validation answers 422 `not_applicable` at `/remote/integrity/checksumPolicy` for `ignore` and `pass-through` on a format that sets it, as it does for `require` on a format with `ChecksumRequireUnsupported` (Q-ARCH-269). `formats.Validate` refuses a format whose `VerifyAnnouncedDigests` and `ChecksumAlwaysVerified` differ. The frozen surface file is regenerated with `go test ./internal/formats -run TestR_ARCH_025 -update-contract`.

**Consequences.** Two flags that must agree; the check at registration keeps them from drifting. A format that addresses artifacts by digest sets both.

**Alternatives considered.** Moving `VerifyAnnouncedDigests` into `Facts` (a removal from `Descriptor`: raises `ContractVersion` and moves every format); the validation asking the registered format for its descriptor (the repository package does not import the formats package).

**Revisit condition:** a second format that always verifies, or a contract version that is raised anyway and can merge the two flags.

**Spec:** [spec/formats/npm.md](spec/formats/npm.md) R-NPM-025, Q-NPM-79; [spec/repositories-and-proxy.md](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-041.

### ADR-161 · The format contract gains the registry root, the upstream handshake, HEAD revalidation and upload sessions

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** The OCI registry ([formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md), T-16) needs things the frozen format contract (ADR-141,
R-ARCH-025) does not say: a client address at the root of a host (`/v2/<project>/<key>/`, [Q-OCI-4](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-4--the-registry-root-is-mounted-through-the-format-contract-its-repository-less-routes-are-the-cores)),
a token handshake with the upstream, a revalidation by `HEAD` and a manifest entered under its digest
([Q-OCI-13](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-13--remotes-the-handshakes-io-in-the-core-revalidation-by-head-a-namespace-prefix-in-the-url),
[Q-OCI-25](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-25--a-remote-manifest-keeps-its-media-type-in-the-cache-entry-and-is-entered-under-its-digest-in-the-fill-transaction)),
uploads over several requests and replicas and the commit of an item for a blob that is stored already
([Q-OCI-12](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-12--uploads-use-the-sessions-of-r-stor-011-mounts-name-their-source-no-automatic-mount),
[Q-OCI-26](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-26--upload-session-calls-repeat-a-session-reference-the-host-decides-and-a-416-carries-the-received-count-as-a-value),
[Q-OCI-27](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-27--a-link-names-the-source-item-and-the-host-checks-it)), a removal that cascades without a request
([Q-OCI-24](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-24--a-storage-hook-cascades-through-the-host-and-a-removal-without-a-request-has-a-system-actor)), the package of a route
([Q-OCI-29](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-29--a-route-declares-its-package-parameter-and-the-link-builder-knows-a-bound-host)), and a plan of a mirror that reads a child manifest
through the engine ([Q-OCI-16](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-16--what-a-mirror-of-a-registry-discovers-and-keeps)).

**Decision.** Additions only, so `ContractVersion` stays 2 and no format changes:

- `catalog.Facts` gains `RegistryRoot` (the one format whose `ProtocolBasePath` is `catalog.RegistryRootBasePath`,
  `/v2/{project}/{key}/`; the catalog refuses a second one and a base path that differs) and `DefaultCredentialHosts` (the entries of
  `DefaultExtraHosts` proposed with `sendCredentials: true`; each must be one of them). `formats.Validate` takes the registry's base
  path for the format that declares the root and `/api/<id>/{project}/{key}/` for every other.
- `Refusal` gains no field: `Refusal.Registry()` reads the protocol base path from the catalog by `Format`, and the host's link
  builder takes it from the descriptor. `SetupData` gains `ImagePrefix` (`<host>/<projectKey>/<repoKey>` for the registry-root format,
  empty for every other). `LinkBuilder` gains `ClientName` (the package name as the client of the request's host spells it) and renders
  the registry without project and key on a host whose root is bound to the repository (`EndpointFacts.Bound`, set by the dispatcher).
  `Route` gains `PackageParam`, the placeholder that holds the route's package, so that the core knows the image name format-neutrally.
- `RemoteAdapter` gains the optional interfaces `Authenticator` (its `TokenRequest` receives the upstream request that was answered
  401) and `Revalidator`, found by `CapabilitiesOf` into `RemoteCaps.Auth` and `RemoteCaps.Revalidate`; the engine reads a revalidation
  answer that is not 2xx itself. `RemoteDocument` carries `MediaType` next to the digest it has, filled from the new column
  `remote_cache_entries.media_type`; `Prepared` gains `Aliases`, the paths the engine enters a fetched document under, as artifacts
  and items for the same blob, in the fill transaction.
- `ItemsEvent` gains `Cascade`, which removes in the transaction of the event and runs the hook again, as the actor of the removal or
  as the system actor `removal`.
- `Host` gains `Uploads() UploadSessions` (`UploadSessions`, `UploadSession`, `SessionRef`: the port of R-STOR-011; every call repeats
  the id and the binding, and the host decides principal, binding and `deploy` on the session's target), and `Ingestor` gains
  `Link(ctx, rq, from SourceRef, c Commit)`, the commit of an item with the content of a source item named by the qualified name of its
  repository and a path ([Q-OCI-32](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-32--a-link-names-its-source-by-repository-name-and-path-and-the-host-resolves-it)): the host resolves the repository by name (a virtual one
  through its members), and checks the item (live, untrashed, served, not blocked, readable by the caller), without a body.
- `servefacts` gains the kind `oci_local` (`formats.ServeOCILocal`) and `Facts.OCIManifest`: the item lookup of a download returns the
  manifest row and whether a tombstone withholds the item's digest in its one statement (R-ARCH-027,
  [Q-OCI-33](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-33--a-manifest-the-journal-replay-withheld-is-refused-by-the-serve-check-from-facts-read-with-the-item-and-an-administrator-reinstates-it)); the format's `ServeCheck` refuses a withheld manifest. The journal replay of
  `oci.manifest.deleted` withholds and never deletes (R-HA-054); `quader admin oci reinstate` is the way back.
- `discover.Upstream` gains `Artifact`, the fill of an artifact through the format's gate and the engine as a background request of
  the pass; an artifact above `max` answers `found` with no body.

The surface file is regenerated with `go test ./internal/formats -run TestR_ARCH_025 -update-contract`, and the blocks of R-ARCH-008
and R-ARCH-009 name the additions. The production host builds `Link` and `Cascade` with the work package of the contract (item store
`CommitLinked` and `LinkIn`, blob store `LinkExisting`); `Host.Uploads` and `discover.Upstream.Artifact` answer `not_implemented` until
their work packages land. The in-memory host of the conformance kit implements `Link` and takes an `UploadSessions` in its options.
The audit event `oci.manifest.deleted` carries the revocation journal flag, and its replay (which withholds), the reinstate command and the
push refusal for a withheld digest are the work package of the deletion
([Q-OCI-30](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-30--the-deletion-of-a-manifest-is-journaled-so-a-restore-does-not-serve-a-deleted-image-again)).
An upstream 429 has the error code `upstream_rate_limited` (kind unavailable), so that a format can tell it from an overload of Quader.

**Consequences.** The facts `RegistryRoot` and `DefaultCredentialHosts` are checked at registration, so a second format cannot take
`/v2/`. The dispatcher mounts the prefix `/api/<id>/` of the formats that do not declare the root and none for the one that does; the
mount of `/v2/` is the work package of the registry root, and until it exists the format `oci` registers with the class `local`, its
routes are served nowhere and answer 501 in the conformance kit. Migration 00056 tightens the key grammar of every format
([Q-OCI-31](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-31--the-key-grammar-migration-adds-its-checks-directly-and-folds-the-composite-names)) as a contract step.

**Alternatives considered.** A rewrite at the edge from `/v2/` to `/api/oci/` (R-HA-041 forbids edge rewrites); a second dispatcher for
`/v2/` (every check of the dispatcher twice); an upload port owned by the format (the sessions and their claims would be written once per
format); a field `Refusal.Base` (a new member for a fact the catalog holds); a bare digest for `Link` (a caller could link any blob).

**Revisit condition:** a second format needs the root of a host, or an upload session needs more than one blob per session.

**Spec:** [spec/formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md) Q-OCI-3, Q-OCI-4, Q-OCI-12, Q-OCI-13, Q-OCI-16, Q-OCI-24 to Q-OCI-34; [spec/architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-008, R-ARCH-009; [spec/storage.md](spec/storage.md) R-STOR-011.

### ADR-162 · The upload session service is a domain package under the host, and a staged blob commits through the commit protocol with a server-side copy

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** R-STOR-011 (unbuilt until T-16 work package 1) keeps a blob that a client sends over several requests and replicas in PostgreSQL and
one S3 multipart upload, and finalizes it by a server-side copy to the content address under the commit protocol of R-STOR-005. The
port of the format contract (`Host.Uploads`, ADR-161) is the host's; the claims, parts, tails and states are not a format's business, and the
commit protocol takes a spooled body, which a blob that is in the bucket already is not.

**Decision.**

- `internal/uploads` is a domain package (layer table, R-ARCH-003): the service decides nothing about who may do what, takes a scope the host
  built (the addressed repository, the binding, the principal) and answers a session of another scope as one that does not exist. The host
  (`internal/formathost/uploads.go`) decides principal, binding and `deploy` on the session's target before every call and implements
  `formats.UploadSessions` over it; a host without the service answers `not_implemented`.
- The state is the rows of migrations 00054 and 00057 (the tail as segments, the item of a finished session); the statements are `queries/uploads.sql`, and the lease of a claim and the age of a
  session are judged by the database's clock. The service reaches the rows through a seam (`rows`), so the unit tests run the state machine
  against a simulation and the integration tier runs the same code on PostgreSQL.
- `blob.ObjectStore` gains `Copy(srcKey, dstKey, size)` (CopyObject up to 5 GiB, UploadPartCopy above, with the encryption of every write; the
  guard counts it, the in-memory store implements it). A store may also implement `blob.MultipartPager` (the client, the guard and the in-memory store do), which the sweep of the staging area uses to list unfinished uploads a page at a time. `blob.Staged(digests, key)` is a `Spooled` whose object write in the commit protocol is that
  copy; a blob that is stored copies nothing, and the source being gone is `blob.ErrStagingGone`. `Spool.IngestSegment` reads at most one
  part of a request into the spool behind the recorded tail, feeding the session's hash functions.
- The finalize commits through `items.Store.Commit` with the staged blob; the end of the session is a step of the commit transaction
  ([Q-STOR-171](spec/storage.md#q-stor-171--a-session-ends-in-the-transaction-that-links-the-item)).
- The collection run gains a session step: expiry, the removal of what aborted and finished sessions staged, and, in the full sweep, of what no
  session stands for ([Q-STOR-170](spec/storage.md#q-stor-170--the-collection-run-aborts-a-live-session-for-its-idle-time-and-an-open-one-for-its-age),
  [Q-STOR-172](spec/storage.md#q-stor-172--the-full-collection-sweep-removes-what-no-session-stands-for-until-the-orphan-sweep-is-a-task-of-its-own)).
- The service has a fault hook (`Service.Fault`, named points of a request) in the form of the collector's: a returned error ends the request as if
  the process had been killed there, with no release of the claim and no clean-up, and a hook may block to hold a request at a point. It is a field
  of the object, not a build tag.

The contract of `UploadSessions` and `UploadSession` is as work package 0 wrote it; nothing in `internal/formats` changed.

**Consequences.** Every replica that takes uploads builds the service with its blob store (`a.uploads`, `wireBlob`); no Valkey is involved at any
step (R-OCI-032). A format's handlers get the minimum chunk length from `UploadSession.PartSize`. The orphan sweep of R-STOR-026 has its
`_uploads/` pass already, inside `gc-full`.

**Alternatives considered.** Keeping the session logic inside `internal/formathost` (edge: no layer below it could be tested without a request, and
the collection run could not share the key layout); a heartbeat-driven lease (the database's `now()` and a renewed `writer_until` per part
are the same fence with no extra moving part); spooling the whole blob on the finalizing replica and committing it as a body (a replica that is
drained or replaced loses it, and the bytes pass the replica twice); a build tag for fault injection (the collector's hook is a field, and tests
of other packages use the service without a tag).

**Revisit condition:** a second consumer of upload sessions with a different finalize (a generic resumable upload that is not content addressed),
or a session that must stage more than one blob.

**Spec:** [spec/storage.md](spec/storage.md) R-STOR-011, Q-STOR-170 to Q-STOR-176; [spec/architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-003;
[spec/formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md) R-OCI-011, R-OCI-032.

### ADR-163 · Registry tokens are bound to their Quader token by the hash of its secret and verified through the token cache

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** The OCI registry uses the token flow of the distribution specification (Q-OCI-5): a client exchanges its Quader token at
`/v2/_token` for a short-lived registry token and presents that on every request below `/v2/`. R-OCI-005 requires the registry token to
be self-contained, verified without the database on its own, and stopped by a revocation of the Quader token within the bound of
R-AUTH-023. Quader's tokens so far are reference tokens only (R-AUTH-022), resolved through a cache keyed by the SHA-256 of the secret.

**Decision.** A registry token is `qdr_rgt_` + base64url(`1:<key id>:<claims as JSON>`) + `.` + base64url(HMAC-SHA-256), with the MAC
key derived by HKDF-SHA-256 from each key of the stored-secret key ring with info `quader registry token v1`; the key ID precedes the
claims so the MAC is checked before anything is parsed (Q-OCI-54). The claims name the Quader token that requested it by its ID, its
type and the SHA-256 of its secret (Q-OCI-50). The authentication stage verifies the MAC, the expiry and the endpoint without any
lookup and then asks the token cache of R-AUTH-023 with the hash (`token.Service.CheckSecretHash`), with the endpoint's token types and
bindings as for the Quader token itself. The token service at `/v2/_token` is not authenticated by the chain; it hands the one presented
credential to the stage (`auth.Stage.AuthenticateTokenRequest`, Q-OCI-51) and grants per scope entry by the coarse check, asked as a
question without an audit event (Q-OCI-55). Claims that span more than `oci.token_lifetime` or are issued more than a minute ahead
are refused. One enforcement point (`registry.Enforcer`) is the only way to mount a handler below `/v2/` - `Mount` registers the
routes and wraps the handler in one call, and the route table admits only its patterns - and checks the grant on the route the
dispatcher's own match names, refusing a registry token on any other (Q-OCI-56). The key ring gains `Derive(info, size)`, which returns the derived keys of every key of the
ring and never the key files themselves.

**Consequences.** The registry token's revocation bound, freshness gate, throttle and rejection events are the Quader token's by
construction, and a client that logs in with its Quader token fills the cache entry its registry tokens use. The hash of the Quader token
travels in every registry token; it allows no guess of the secret, and it makes a holder of the key ring need that hash as well as the
ring to forge (H-579). A registry token is a bearer credential within its lifetime and grant (H-595). The chain's request log of a token
request records the anonymous principal unless the composition root records the caller the token service authenticated.

**Alternatives considered.** An ID in the claims with a second cache keyed by ID (a fifth auth cache, a query per replica that the
Quader token's own lookup already paid, and a forgery that needs only an ID every listing shows); reference registry tokens stored per
issue (a database write on the hottest route, Q-OCI-5 (d)); a JWT (header-driven algorithms for a token only Quader reads).

**Revisit condition:** the hash must be kept from the clients that hold registry tokens, or another party must verify registry tokens.

**Spec:** [spec/formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md) R-OCI-004, R-OCI-005, R-OCI-006, R-OCI-034, Q-OCI-50 to Q-OCI-57;
[spec/identity-and-authentication.md](spec/identity-and-authentication.md) R-AUTH-001, R-AUTH-002, R-AUTH-022, R-AUTH-023, R-AUTH-041;
[spec/authorization.md](spec/authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-007; [spec/architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-021.

### ADR-164 · The OCI push path is one transaction with its reference check under row locks, and the format's data port reads items

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** A push of an OCI manifest ([formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md) R-OCI-013) writes the manifest item, a tag item, the package
and version rows, the manifest and reference rows of the format, and must refuse a manifest that names what the repository does not hold,
without a gap in which a concurrent removal takes a named blob away. The data port of WP0 (ADR-161) had the rows of the format and no way
to ask which items exist, which a version points at which manifest, or what the screens list.

**Decision.**

- The tag item is the lead of a push by tag and the manifest item its companion (a companion goes with a lead that changed); a tag whose
  manifest is stored already is linked with `Ingestor.Link`, a push by digest has the manifest as the lead
  ([Q-OCI-61](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-61--a-push-is-checked-before-it-is-stored-and-again-in-the-commit-transaction-on-rows-held-against-a-removal)).
  `OnCommit` of the format creates the package row under its lock, claims the name, creates the version of a new tag or leaves the
  version of a moved tag where it is, checks the references again on rows held with `FOR SHARE`, records the manifest and its edges, and
  raises the revision; a manifest or tag item without the payload of a push is refused (409), a blob item is let through for the upload
  work package.
- The data port `Store` gains `ExistingItems` (live files among canonical paths, locked inside a transaction), `WithheldAmong`,
  `TagViews`, `StoredTags` and `WithheldVersions`; the port reads the generic `items`, `packages` and `package_versions` tables for
  these, because the format's rows alone cannot say whether an item exists or which manifest a tag holds. The implementation and its
  statements are `internal/formatdata/oci/store_manifests.go` and `internal/meta/postgres/queries/oci_manifests.sql`.
- The manifest is read by `internal/formats/oci/manifest` (a strict reader, [Q-OCI-60](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-60--a-manifest-is-read-by-a-strict-reader-that-refuses-what-two-readers-could-interpret-differently)); the tag
  order of `internal/formats/oci/tagorder` ([Q-OCI-64](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-64--the-tag-order-ranks-a-release-above-its-variants-above-its-pre-releases)) is the order of the package view.
- A refusal of the registry itself that is a conflict (the push of a withheld digest, and the deletion that would leave a dangling
  reference) is `409 DENIED`: the error kind `conflict` maps to the code `DENIED` in `WriteError`.
- The response `ETag` of a manifest or blob is `"sha256:<hex>"` and the request's validators are translated for the item store
  ([Q-OCI-62](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-62--the-etag-of-a-manifest-or-a-blob-is-the-digest-in-quotes-the-item-store-compares-the-hex)).

**Consequences.** A push is two queries over the named paths (before the commit and in it), the second on rows held `FOR SHARE`, in the
commit transaction and on its connection. The locks of a push are not in one order: the item of its path first (the item store), then
the package row (the hook), then the companion manifest item and the items the manifest names. A removal takes the package row first and
must read the references again once it has it; it inverts the order against a push of the same tag, and a tag push inverts it against a
digest push of the same new manifest. The database breaks the cycle (40P01) and the transaction runner retries the loser; this is
a constraint on the deletion work package (the tag delete, the sweep) and recorded as
[H-608](spec/formats/oci.md#h-608--pushes-and-removals-take-their-locks-in-different-orders-and-rely-on-the-retry).

**Alternatives considered.** A check before the commit only (a removal in the gap leaves a manifest over a missing blob); a check in
the hook only (the body is spooled and written before the client hears of a missing layer); the standard decoder for the manifest
(duplicate and case-folded keys are read two ways); a `package.published` event of the format (a tag is a pointer, not an immutable
version).

**Revisit condition:** the second query shows in the latency of pushes of large indexes, or the deletion work package needs a lock order
other than the package row first.

**Spec:** [spec/formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md) R-OCI-006, R-OCI-008, R-OCI-009, R-OCI-010, R-OCI-013, R-OCI-014, R-OCI-020, R-OCI-031, Q-OCI-60 to Q-OCI-65.

### ADR-165 · The remote engine carries out the format's token handshake and HEAD revalidation

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** ADR-161 gave the remote adapter the optional interfaces `Authenticator` and `Revalidator` and left the engine not calling them. A
container registry answers a request without a token with `401` and a challenge naming a token service (R-OCI-021), expects its quota to
be spent on a `HEAD` and not a `GET` (R-OCI-022), and sends `RateLimit-Remaining: 0;w=21600` (R-OCI-025). The upstream chooses the token
service's host, so the engine must apply the host and credential rules of R-REPO-033 to an address that comes from the upstream.

**Decision.** The engine owns the I/O, the format the protocol:

- `proxy.Authenticator` and `proxy.Revalidator` are the engine's views of the format's interfaces; `internal/formathost` adapts
  `formats.RemoteCaps.Auth` and `.Revalidate` to them (a format without them answers `ok` false, so a `401` or an expired document is
  handled as before). `proxy.QueryRequest.Auth` and `proxy.Get.Auth` give the handshake to a pass-through query and to a mirror's
  discovery request, which have no repository path.
- On a `401` the engine asks the format for the token request, refuses an address that is not the upstream origin or an `extraHosts`
  entry, sends it through the repository's client (the credential goes where R-REPO-033 allows), reads at most 64 KiB, hands the answer to
  the format and retries the original request once with the value the format returns. The value goes to the upstream origin only
  (`outbound.WithAuthorization`, [Q-REPO-255](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-255--a-handshake-token-goes-to-the-upstream-origin-only-and-the-realm-is-asked-under-the-credential-rule)).
- The token is kept in the registered cache `proxy_upstream_tokens`, per repository, configuration version and the format's key, and
  looked up before a request with the last challenge of the repository ([Q-OCI-82](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-82--the-engine-asks-the-format-before-a-request-with-the-last-challenge-so-only-the-first-request-of-a-replica-is-challenged), superseding Q-OCI-80;
  [Q-ARCH-350](spec/architecture.md#q-arch-350--the-tokens-of-upstream-handshakes-are-a-registered-per-replica-cache-never-stored)); concurrent
  handshakes of a key share one request.
- An expired stored document is revalidated with the format's request when it gives one; the 2xx answer that the format calls unchanged
  renews the freshness without a body ([Q-OCI-81](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-81--a-head-that-is-not-a-2xx-is-the-engines-answer-and-a-2xx-that-is-not-unchanged-is-a-get)).
- The repository validation proposes the extra hosts of a well-known upstream with `sendCredentials: true` for the hosts the catalog
  names in `DefaultCredentialHosts`.
- `RateLimit-Remaining` is read by its integer before the first `;` ([Q-REPO-256](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-256--the-quota-header-is-read-by-its-integer-before-the-first-semicolon)).

**Consequences.** `ContractVersion` stays 2 and no format changes. Only the first request of a replica and configuration version to a registry
is challenged; the format takes the scope from the request and only the realm and the service from the challenge. The handshake's failures are the request's answer and do not count toward the circuit.

**Alternatives considered.** The format doing the I/O (it would need the repository's client and the credential rules); a token set as a
request header by the adapter (the hop policy removes it); a token guessed from the last key (the scope belongs to the request); the cache in Valkey
(a token is a credential).

**Revisit condition:** a registry that counts unauthenticated requests, or a format whose upstream needs the token at a second host.

**Spec:** [spec/repositories-and-proxy.md](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-033, R-REPO-054, Q-REPO-255, Q-REPO-256;
[spec/formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md) R-OCI-021, R-OCI-022, R-OCI-025, Q-OCI-80 to Q-OCI-82; [spec/architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-032, Q-ARCH-350.

### ADR-167 · The pinned tools of a CI job come from a verified cache, not from a live release download

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** On 2026-11-08 the GitHub release host answered 504 for the buildx archive of the nightly run 42465102401, and the buildx action's own binary cache held an entry that a runner with another workspace depth could not extract: the cache writer stores paths relative to the workspace, and that entry was saved from `/runner/_work/quader/quader`, four levels deep, and restored into `/home/runner/_work/quader/quader`, five levels deep. Each job of Test and Release and of the nightly downloads its tools again, and a release-host outage of a minute fails the leg.

**Decision.** A tool pinned in `tools/versions.env` reaches a job as a verified archive: a composite action (`.github/actions/install-buildx`) first uses the runner's copy when that file is the pinned release binary (the same SHA-256; another build of the pinned version goes through the cache), otherwise a copy cached under the workspace path `.bin/`, otherwise a download with a bounded retry; the archive is used only when its SHA-256 equals the pinned digest. The action's own binary download is avoided. Applied to Docker Buildx in all 23 jobs, and to the chart pulls of `make dev-up` as a retry (`chart_tgz`). Still open: the Go toolchain and the cache of the chart archives. The two GitHub-release chart archives are pinned by digest, and every release-asset download is authenticated with the job's token (Q-ARCH-356).

**Consequences.** One pin and its digests per tool, read by the workflows and by `make versions-check`. A version bump edits the version and its digests together. The Go toolchain keeps its exposure until it is moved.

**Alternatives considered.** Only fixing the cache key (the download stays exposed); longer retries inside the actions (not configurable); baking the pins into the runner image (outside the repository, and a bump waits for an image rebuild).

**Revisit condition:** the runner image carries the pins (the cache steps then do nothing), or a cold-cache run fails on the release host within the retry window again.

**Spec:** [spec/architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) Q-ARCH-355; [developer/releasing.md](developer/releasing.md#pinned-tools-in-the-jobs).
