### ADR-168 · The OCI data port reads and removes for the deletion, the sweep and the replay

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough. **Superseded in part by
[Q-STOR-190](spec/storage.md#q-stor-190--the-delete-job-decides-every-batch-again-on-what-the-subject-that-asked-holds-then) and
[Q-AUTHZ-260](spec/authorization.md#q-authz-260--a-job-carries-who-asked-and-reads-what-that-subject-holds-for-every-batch)**: the delete
job no longer carries the encoded subject of the request; it carries who asked (`authz.JobSubject`), reads what that subject holds for
every batch, and decides on it the batch's own items, the ownership of its files and the cascade, with a 403 that names the path the
request named.

**Context.** ADR-161 gave the OCI format the cascade of a removal (`ItemsEvent.Cascade`), the audit event `oci.manifest.deleted` with
its journal flag and the table of withheld manifests, and left the behaviour behind them to the work package of the deletion. That
package needs reads inside the transaction of a removal, the lists of the registry API, a job that removes unreferenced blobs, a
replay handler and an administrator's command, and none of them may open a second road to the items or the audit trail.

**Decision.**

- The data port `Store` of the format gains the reads of the removal hook, which see the effects of the transaction that removed the
  items (`TagsPointingAt`, `SubjectManifests`, `Children`), `RecordManifestDeleted`, `Holds` (the 404 of a tags list) and
  `CatalogNames` (the page of one repository for the catalog of the registry root). `internal/formatdata/oci` records its events
  itself, through the audit recorder, the source and the actor it is given, as the npm and NuGet ports do; `oci.manifest.deleted`
  carries the journal entry `{repository, name, digest, actorId}` and a removal without a principal is written by the system
  actor `removal` ([Q-OCI-24](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-24--a-storage-hook-cascades-through-the-host-and-a-removal-without-a-request-has-a-system-actor)).
- The contract gains, additively, the listing-form decision `Host.PathsAllowed(ctx, rq, action, paths) []bool` (the evaluation of
  `authz.PathsAllowedOn` with the coordinate of each path completed by the format's `Classify`, the repository's include and exclude patterns and the remote-claim refusal applied as `Authorize` applies them, no audit event): the filtering of lists and the
  check of a cascade use it, while the request's own target stays an audited `Authorize`. The host guards the cascade of a removal a request
  makes: `items.WithCascadeGuard` carries a function in the context, set by the writer of `Host.Write` and by the files service, and the
  cascade of a storage hook decides every path it is about to remove with it and refuses the whole removal at the first refusal; the delete job carries the encoded subject of the request (`DeleteArgs.Subject`) and re-decides the cascade of every batch for it on the index of that moment (`items.JobGuard`), failing the job permanently with the 403 of the path
  ([Q-OCI-76](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-76--a-delete-is-decided-by-the-path-of-every-item-it-removes-and-a-delete-by-digest-is-refused-when-its-cascade-would-take-an-item-the-caller-may-not-delete)).
  Also additively, `ItemsEvent.InScope` (whether the live file at a path belongs to the same removal as the event: the delete of
  a subtree reaches a hook in events of at most 5,000 files, or in the batches of a job) and the optional `formats.RemovalLocker`
  (`LockRemoval`, found by `CapabilitiesOf`: the locks a format's writers take first, taken before the item store deletes the rows of the
  files of a removal; the conformance host calls it). Both are in the blocks of R-ARCH-008/009 and in the surface file.
- The hook `OnItemsRemoved` holds the rules of every removal ([Q-OCI-73](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-73--every-removal-path-refuses-what-would-leave-a-dangling-reference-and-the-refusal-is-409-denied)); the
  routes of the deletion check authorization (by path, with the cascade of a delete by digest, [Q-OCI-76](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-76--a-delete-is-decided-by-the-path-of-every-item-it-removes-and-a-delete-by-digest-is-refused-when-its-cascade-would-take-an-item-the-caller-may-not-delete)) and ownership and let the hook decide. The registry error shape maps a conflict to `409`
  `DENIED`.
- The job `oci-sweep` lives in `internal/formatdata/oci` and removes through the item store, which the composition root hands it
  late, as it does the job that deletes a subtree
  ([Q-OCI-71](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-71--the-sweep-removes-one-blob-item-per-transaction-under-the-lock-of-the-names-package-and-reads-the-references-again)). The task is scheduled hourly in
  `maintenance.tasks` and counted by `quader_oci_sweep_blobs_removed_total`.
- The replay handler of `oci.manifest.deleted` withholds and never deletes
  ([Q-OCI-30](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-30--the-deletion-of-a-manifest-is-journaled-so-a-restore-does-not-serve-a-deleted-image-again),
  [Q-OCI-33](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-33--a-manifest-the-journal-replay-withheld-is-refused-by-the-serve-check-from-facts-read-with-the-item-and-an-administrator-reinstates-it));
  `quader admin oci reinstate <projectKey>/<repoKey> <name>@<digest>` removes the mark while the manifest row and its item are stored
  with the digest, raises the revision and writes `oci.reinstate`, which is not journaled.

**Consequences.** Every road of removal (the protocol, `/files/`, the items API, a retention run, the sweep, the cascade itself)
keeps the graph of manifests whole and writes the journal entry a restore withholds the image by. The sweep takes the lock every
writer of the image name takes, and the manifest push holds its layers' rows until its own rows are written, so a push and the sweep
of one blob end with the blob either swept before the push checks or kept by the manifest. The item store passes the scope of a whole delete to the hook (`ItemsEvent.InScope`, an addition to the contract), so a delete of an image name beyond one event or one job batch is one removal, and offers an optional `LockRemoval` before it deletes item rows, which the format uses to take its package rows first.

**Alternatives considered.** Refusals in the routes only (a raw delete would leave a dangling reference); a statement that deletes every
unreferenced blob (no lock, no hook, no audit); a second journal for OCI (R-HA-054 has one).

**Revisit condition:** the trash can exists (R-STOR-022) and a deletion must follow its reason in more than the rows, or a format
other than OCI needs a cascade that depends on the order of removal.

**Spec:** [spec/formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md) R-OCI-015 to R-OCI-019, R-OCI-033, Q-OCI-70, Q-OCI-71, Q-OCI-73 to Q-OCI-76; [spec/ha-and-helm.md](spec/ha-and-helm.md) R-HA-054.

### ADR-169 · The catalog carries the package-document path, and the conformance kit holds every format to the paths it authorizes

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** Finding F-82 (2026-11-08): the npm and NuGet handlers authorized a package without a path, and the decision
point let a coordinate without a path pass a path set without an include list, so a grant or a token scope that excluded a
package's paths read, listed and pushed that package through the protocol while `/files/` refused the same file; an
include refused every package. The decision point also asks questions about a package as a whole of its own (a listing row,
the ownership of a name, a check of the caller) and had no path to decide them on. The format contract is frozen at version
2 (ADR-141, R-ARCH-025): every change of it is an ADR.

**Decision.** A target that names a package names the canonical path of the document or file the operation serves or
writes, and a non-repository coordinate without a path does not match a path set with any pattern
([Q-AUTHZ-250](spec/authorization.md#q-authz-250--a-protocol-request-is-decided-on-the-canonical-path-of-what-it-serves-or-writes-and-a-package-without-a-path-fails-a-path-set)).
`catalog.Entry` gains `DocumentPath`, which `formats.CatalogEntry` derives from a format's `PackageDocumentPath` for a format
with package names; the decision point completes its own package-level coordinates with it. It is an addition: the zero
value leaves such a question without a path, which fails closed, and `ContractVersion` stays 2. `catalog.Facts` gains
`LowerCasePaths`, true for NuGet: the path dimension of such a repository is compared in lower case, pattern and path alike
([Q-AUTHZ-254](spec/authorization.md#q-authz-254--the-path-dimension-of-a-format-with-lower-case-paths-is-compared-in-lower-case-pattern-and-path-alike)),
and a path pattern with an upper-case letter over such a repository is refused where it
is written ([Q-AUTHZ-253](spec/authorization.md#q-authz-253--path-patterns-over-a-format-with-lower-case-paths-are-lower-case-and-every-path-pattern-on-a-package-format-is-warned-about));
the zero value folds and refuses nothing. The conformance kit gains
check 13 (R-ARCH-010): every target a handler hands `Authorize`, `CheckOwnership` or `Claim` names a canonical path that
`Classify` places in the target's package, every served file was authorized at its path, and a package's request is not
authorized at the repository level. The vulnerability corpus of the spec's list moves from item 13 to item 14; the kit did
not number it. The frozen surface file is regenerated with `go test ./internal/formats -run TestR_ARCH_025 -update-contract`.

**Consequences.** A format states a path for every target, and a format that forgets one refuses every caller with path
patterns and fails the kit before a release; the OCI format of its feature branch is held to the same check when it lands.
A path pattern on a package format has to cover the package document and the files. Listings and the protocol decide a
package on the same path.

**Alternatives considered.** The host deriving the path from the request (a write's path is known only after the body; a
protocol path is not a canonical one; a required method would raise `ContractVersion`, an optional one would leave a format without it deciding without a path); refusing path patterns on package
formats (a selector covers repositories that do not exist yet); failing closed without the format changes (path patterns
would refuse every package).

**Revisit condition:** a format serves a document that spans packages under one path, or an operation that removes several
files has to be decided per file (H-586).

**Spec:** [spec/authorization.md](spec/authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-005, R-AUTHZ-007, Q-AUTHZ-250;
[spec/architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-010; [spec/formats/npm.md](spec/formats/npm.md) Q-NPM-80;
[spec/formats/nuget.md](spec/formats/nuget.md) Q-NUGET-113.

### ADR-170 · APT indexes are built by a job and published through the item store's publication port as generated items, also in virtual repositories

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** An APT client reads `Release`, `InRelease`, `Release.gpg` and a `Packages` index per suite, component and architecture, signed by
a key it trusts, and fetches index files by hash (`by-hash`) so that a client that read a release can still fetch the files it names
while a newer generation is published. Indexes of a repository of ten thousand packages are tens of megabytes compressed, are signed, and
must be the same bytes on every replica (R-DEB-010). ADR-089 and R-ARCH-012 render derived metadata per request; a job-built index is the
justified exception item 2 of R-ARCH-012 allows.

**Decision.**

- The indexes of a local and of a virtual Debian repository are built by the job `deb-index` (queue `index`, coalescing per repository) from
  the rows of one `REPEATABLE READ` snapshot, rendered, compressed and signed outside any transaction, and published as **generated items**
  (package-less items) through the publication port `items.Publisher` ([Q-STOR-182](spec/storage.md#q-stor-182--generated-items-are-published-through-one-port-blobs-first-then-one-transaction)):
  blobs first, then one transaction that upserts every file of the generation, removes what retention gives up and writes the build's own rows.
- A virtual repository holds the generated items of its merged indexes in its own `items`
  ([Q-STOR-180](spec/storage.md#q-stor-180--a-virtual-repository-of-a-format-with-a-job-built-index-holds-the-generated-items-of-its-indexes)); it accepts generated
  items from this port and from nothing else.
- An upload never waits for an index (R-ARCH-012 rule 3); the delay bound is `deb.index_delay` plus 5 s, and an index state read can wait
  (`deb.index_wait_max`).

**Consequences.** Every replica serves the same signed bytes; `If-Modified-Since` works because every item of a generation carries the
`Release` date as `modified_at`; a reader sees a suite's previous generation or its new one. The port is declared by the contract work and
built by the index builder; until then the format's routes answer 501.

**Alternatives considered.** Rendering and signing per request (a signature per request on a key that must not be opened by a handler, and bytes
that differ between replicas); a per-replica cache of merged indexes (replicas would serve different signatures).

**Revisit condition:** a second format builds its index by a job, or the delay bound cannot be held at the reference sizes.

**Spec:** [spec/formats/debian.md](spec/formats/debian.md) R-DEB-010 to R-DEB-014, Q-DEB-6, Q-DEB-33; [spec/storage.md](spec/storage.md) R-STOR-003, Q-STOR-180, Q-STOR-182.

### ADR-171 · Every Debian local and virtual repository has its own EdDSALegacy signing key, generated by Quader and sealed with the stored-secret key ring; rotation by a co-signing next key; the journal withholds keys and never erases them

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** A client trusts a key, not a host (`Signed-By`). A key shared by repositories would make trust in one repository trust all
of them; a key outside Quader would need a signing service. The verifiers of Debian 12 and 13 and Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 (`gpgv` 2.2 and 2.4,
`sqv`) read the signatures of algorithm 22 (EdDSALegacy) and not those of algorithm 27, which the OpenPGP module writes by default.

**Decision.**

- Every local and virtual Debian repository has a primary key from the transaction that creates it (the creation hook,
  [Q-REPO-273](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-273--a-formats-data-port-adds-rows-in-the-transaction-that-creates-its-repository)); a key belongs to one repository.
- The key is EdDSALegacy over Ed25519, version 4, created an hour before the creating transaction (so no signature precedes its key), with
  a binding self-signature at the same time; the private key is sealed with the stored-secret key ring in `deb_signing_keys.private_key`, a
  registered sealed column, and is opened only for one signing call.
- Rotation is a next key that co-signs, then a promotion that retires the old key (its private key is erased) and journals the event. A
  restore's replay of `deb.signing_key.promoted` and `deb.signing_key.retired` withholds a key (state `withheld`, the sealed key kept) and never
  erases one; an administrator confirms the retirement or reinstates the key.

**Consequences.** A forged journal entry costs availability until an administrator acts, never a key. A holder of the key ring and a
database copy can sign for every repository ([H-620](spec/formats/debian.md#h-620--a-holder-of-the-stored-secret-key-ring-and-a-database-copy-can-sign-for-every-debian-repository)).
`secrets-reencrypt` walks the column, so a key-ring rotation covers the keys.

**Alternatives considered.** One instance-wide key; keys in an external service (deferred, FULL.md); RSA only (larger signatures and slower
builds, accepted only on import).

**Revisit condition:** a key management service or an HSM is wanted, or a verifier of a supported client stops reading algorithm 22.

**Spec:** [spec/formats/debian.md](spec/formats/debian.md) R-DEB-015 to R-DEB-018, R-DEB-032, Q-DEB-9 to Q-DEB-11, Q-DEB-30, Q-DEB-31.

### ADR-172 · The format contract gains the remote name index and the serve-facts kinds `deb_local` and `deb_remote`

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** The shadowing check (R-REPO-048) asks a remote member whether it serves a package name by its package document; an APT archive
has none. The serve check of a local Debian repository and the artifact gate of a remote one decide on rows besides the item, which a
download reads in the one statement R-ARCH-027 allows.

**Decision.**

- The contract gains the optional interface `NameServer` on a remote adapter, with `NameQuery` and `RemoteCaps.Names`
  ([Q-REPO-270](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-270--a-format-without-a-package-document-answers-the-shadowing-check-from-its-index-rows-in-the-scope-of-the-virtual-repository));
  the shadowing check takes it when `PackageDocumentPath` reports no document, once per pair of a virtual repository and a remote member.
- The serve-facts kinds `deb_local` (the withheld mark of a package file) and `deb_remote` (the SHA-256 and size the newest parsed index lists
  for a path, `ServeDebRemoteFacts`) are read in the item lookup ([Q-ARCH-381](spec/architecture.md#q-arch-381--the-item-lookup-reads-the-withheld-mark-of-a-debian-package-file-and-the-digest-a-debian-remotes-parsed-index-announces)).
- `ContractVersion` stays 3 (R-ARCH-025: an addition); the surface file `internal/formats/testdata/contract.txt` changes in the same change.

**Consequences.** No existing format changes. The Debian format is the first to have no package document, so the conformance kit gains
`Fixture.NoDocument` and its authorization check no longer requires a document path for a package.

**Alternatives considered.** A `PackageDocumentPath` that names an index (a megabyte document that says nothing about the scope); a per-request
statement in `ServeCheck` and the gate (a second statement on the hottest route).

**Revisit condition:** a second format has no package document.

**Spec:** [spec/architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-008, R-ARCH-027, Q-ARCH-381; [spec/formats/debian.md](spec/formats/debian.md) R-DEB-022, R-DEB-023, Q-DEB-37.

### ADR-173 · The registry root is one pattern, one handler and one match

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** The enforcement point of the registry tokens' grants (ADR-163, Q-OCI-56) decides a request on the dispatcher's match and
promises that nothing below `/v2/` is served around it. `http.ServeMux` unescapes the literal segments of a pattern, so a pattern
`/v2/_catalog` also serves `/v2/%5Fcatalog`, which the match reads as no core route; a router also serves paths through its
`HandleUncleaned` prefixes and its fallback, which the route table did not list; and a host bound to a repository (R-EP-006) changes
what a path means without any lookup that the token service and the match share.

**Decision.** Everything below `/v2/` is served on one handler below the patterns `/v2` and `/v2/{rest...}`, mounted through the enforcement point
(`registry.Register`). The dispatcher's handler for it (`Dispatcher.RegistryHandler`) matches the request with `registryMatch`, the
function `RegistryTarget` also reduces to the enforcement point's target, and serves the route that match names: the version check,
the catalog and the token service through their handlers, every repository route through the code path of `/api/<format>/`
(`serveRoute`). The route table checks, besides the text of the patterns, a probe of each pattern in a scratch mux, the uncleaned
prefixes (`HandleUncleaned` panics at or below `/v2`, the enforcement point registers its own prefix with
`HandleRegistryUncleaned`) and the fallback (Q-ARCH-390). A binding of a host root counts for a repository of the format only,
read per request by `Dispatcher.BoundRepository`, which the match, the token service and the catalog all call (Q-EP-80).
`registrytest.Walk` keeps its own expectation (the format's `Match` of each example) and compares it with the route that served the
request, through the endpoint's real handler.

**Consequences.** A path reaches the route its match names and no other, by construction. The 405 of a method a route does not offer is
written by the handler (`Allow` in the registry's shape), not by the router. A bare `/v2` is the version check too (a second pattern on the same handler). The request is matched once: the enforcement point puts
a memo of the match into the request's context and the handler reuses it, so a binding that changes in between cannot make the grant be
checked on one repository and the request served on another (W3-2). A failed lookup of the bound repository refuses a registry token and answers the request with the error.

**Alternatives considered.** A pattern per core route besides a subtree for the repositories (two matchers, the escaped spelling); the
core handlers checking their own path (a third copy of the match); extending the text rules to decode escapes and parse hosts (a
second matcher that tracks ServeMux).

**Revisit condition:** a route below `/v2/` needs the router's method handling, or a second prefix needs the same protection.

**Spec:** [spec/formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md) R-OCI-001, R-OCI-003, R-OCI-017, R-OCI-029, Q-OCI-100, Q-OCI-101;
[spec/architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-005, Q-ARCH-390; [spec/endpoints.md](spec/endpoints.md) R-EP-006, R-EP-007, Q-EP-80.

### ADR-192 · Visibility levels replace the anonymous switch and the principal `authenticated`

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough. The levels private, internal and public, the
per-repository wiki level and the user flag `external` set by an administrator are the owner's (task T-18, 2026-11-11).

**Context.** Three mechanisms opened content before T-18: the runtime switch `anonymousAccess` under its YAML ceiling
`auth.anonymous.allowed` together with policy entries for the principal `anonymous`; the built-in principal `authenticated` in
policy entries (Q-AUTHZ-3); and the repository field `requireAuthentication`, which closed again what the first opened. The owner
asked for GitLab's visibility levels as one mechanism, with a default per installation, a level per project and per repository, a
wiki level apart from the artifacts, and a user flag `external`.

**Decision.**

- A level (`private`, `internal`, `public`) is stored on each project and, twice, on each repository (artifacts and wiki); the
  installation's default is copied when a project or a repository is created. A repository is never more open than its project,
  its wiki never more open than its artifacts; lowering a project lowers its repositories in the same transaction; raising lowers
  nothing back. An administrator sets a project's level, its Owner its repositories' levels within it
  ([spec/authorization.md](spec/authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-033, Q-AUTHZ-263 to Q-AUTHZ-267).
- A level is a source of `read` beside grants and roles: `public` for every request, `internal` for every internal subject,
  narrowed by the token scope; nothing but the endpoint's exposure narrows `public` (R-AUTHZ-030, R-AUTHZ-035, Q-AUTHZ-268,
  Q-AUTHZ-269). Amended by the owner on 2026-11-20: an internal subject is every authenticated subject - users, service accounts'
  technical tokens, CI tokens - except a user flagged external and that user's tokens, through every door, a Bastion included; the
  rule built until then (a user through a session or a personal token, not flagged external, not through a Bastion) is gone.
- The wiki is the documentation Quader serves or shows apart from the files; one coordinate part decides it, asked through
  `formats.Route.Wiki`, `Host.WikiReadable`, `x-quader-part: wiki` and `authz.ReadScope.MayReadWiki`; a caller who reads the
  artifacts but not the wiki gets the refusal of a read on a wiki route and documents without the wiki members (R-AUTHZ-034,
  Q-AUTHZ-270 to Q-AUTHZ-272).
- The switch, its ceiling, `requireAuthentication` and the principal `authenticated` are removed; no policy entry, binding,
  membership or owner record names `anonymous` or `authenticated` (422 `principal_not_allowed`, SQLSTATE `AI009`); the default
  endpoint's `auth.anonymous` is the operator's ceiling of `public` ([spec/identity-and-authentication.md](spec/identity-and-authentication.md)
  R-AUTH-037, R-AUTH-044, Q-AUTH-230 to Q-AUTH-233; Q-AUTHZ-279).
- The levels are columns (`project.visibility`, `repositories.visibility_artifacts`, `repositories.visibility_wiki`) with the
  container rule in the database (`AI008`); migrations `00073_visibility.sql`, `00074_external_users.sql`,
  `00075_principal_builtins.sql` (Q-AUTHZ-276).

**Consequences.** The grant index reads the levels in its snapshot, the stage resolves the flag with the user's status and groups,
and both reach every replica within the existing bounds (R-AUTHZ-036). The Bastion's interface rises to version 2: its handshake
reports `anonymousReads`, its feed carries the level changes, and a request through it is decided as the same request at the main
installation's door (owner, 2026-11-20; [spec/bastion.md](spec/bastion.md) Q-BAS-148 to Q-BAS-150). Every test and fixture that switched anonymous access on or set
`requireAuthentication` changes. The wiki
level cannot hide documentation shipped inside an artifact (H-880 in [security/visibility.md](security/visibility.md)).

**Alternatives considered.** Levels compiled into policy entries for `anonymous` and `authenticated` (two places that can disagree);
levels beside the switch (the second mechanism the owner ruled out); live inheritance of the project's level (a raise of a project
opens repositories nobody chose to open); groups marked external (not the owner's flag).

**Revisit condition:** the owner wants per-principal anonymous exceptions, Owners who open their own projects, or public
documentation of internal packages.

**Spec:** [spec/authorization.md](spec/authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-003, R-AUTHZ-030, R-AUTHZ-033 to R-AUTHZ-036, Q-AUTHZ-263 to
Q-AUTHZ-279; [spec/identity-and-authentication.md](spec/identity-and-authentication.md) R-AUTH-037, R-AUTH-040, R-AUTH-044,
Q-AUTH-230 to Q-AUTH-233; [spec/api-and-ui.md](spec/api-and-ui.md) R-API-056 to R-API-058, R-UI-053 to R-UI-057.

### ADR-198 · The format catalog names a format's upstream presets, and the contract is at version 4

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough. The four OCI registries are the owner's (task T-21,
2026-11-12: "for Docker: Quay, ghcr, Docker Hub, GitLab").

**Context.** A format declared one well-known upstream as three catalog facts: `DefaultUpstreamURL`, the `DefaultExtraHosts` a repository
of it takes, and the `DefaultCredentialHosts` among them that receive the credential. The owner asked for the well-known public
registries of a format as one-click choices, so a format has several upstreams, each with hosts of its own (GitLab's token service is
on `gitlab.com`, Docker Hub's on `auth.docker.io`, Quay's and ghcr.io's on the registry itself). Which host receives a credential is a
security fact of the registry, which belongs where the handshake is checked and not in the web client
([Q-REPO-320](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-320--the-presets-are-a-fact-of-the-format-and-the-api-serves-them)).

**Decision.** `catalog.Facts` gains `UpstreamPresets []UpstreamPreset` (`ID`, `DisplayName`, `URL`, `ExtraHosts []PresetHost` with
`Pattern` and `SendCredentials`, `Default`) and the methods `DefaultPreset` and `PresetFor`; `DefaultUpstreamURL`,
`DefaultExtraHosts` and `DefaultCredentialHosts` leave. The catalog refuses presets on a format without the class remote, no default
or two, an ID or a URL twice and a host pattern twice in one preset; `formats.Validate` refuses a preset URL that is not in the form
R-REPO-024 stores. Fields leave the contract, so `ContractVersion` rises to 4 and every format moves in the same change: OCI
(Docker Hub, Quay, GitHub (ghcr.io), GitLab), npm (the public registry), NuGet (nuget.org), Debian (Debian, Debian security updates,
Ubuntu, Ubuntu security updates, Ubuntu ports) and Ansible Galaxy (the public Galaxy), each with the hosts it had or needs. `GET
/api/v1/formats` serves `upstreamPresets` in place of `defaultUpstreamUrl`, `defaultExtraHosts` and `defaultCredentialHosts`
([R-REPO-062](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md#r-repo-062--upstream-presets-of-a-format),
[Q-REPO-327](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-327--the-format-lists-default-upstream-members-are-replaced-by-the-presets)).

**Consequences.** A preset says per host whether it receives the credential, so the old rule "a credential host is one of the extra
hosts" holds by construction. The default preset is the default upstream of R-REPO-024; a create that names another preset's URL
takes that preset's hosts (Q-REPO-322), and every preset's URL needs a mirror bound (Q-REPO-323). A preset's hosts are copied into the
repository at create, so a later correction of a preset does not reach existing repositories
([H-970](security/remote-repositories.md#h-970--a-presets-credential-host-is-fixed-in-the-repository-when-it-is-created)).

**Alternatives considered.** The presets as a list in the web client (a second list per format, and an API client would create a
GitLab remote without its token host); keeping the three fields beside the presets (two shapes of one fact, before the first stable
release); an additive field with the old three kept (no version rise, but a format could declare both and disagree).

**Revisit condition:** the owner wants installation-specific presets (the open question of T-21), which would merge a settings list into
`upstreamPresets` at the API and leave the contract as it is.

**Spec:** [spec/repositories-and-proxy.md](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-003, R-REPO-024, R-REPO-052, R-REPO-062, Q-REPO-320 to
Q-REPO-323, Q-REPO-327; [spec/architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-008, R-ARCH-025; the format pages
[oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md) R-OCI-001, R-OCI-021, [npm.md](spec/formats/npm.md) R-NPM-023, [nuget.md](spec/formats/nuget.md)
R-NUGET-001, [debian.md](spec/formats/debian.md) R-DEB-001, [ansible.md](spec/formats/ansible.md) R-ANS-001.

### ADR-197 · A format's documentation is gated by one call, the wiki check, and never by the artifact check

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** Task T-18 gives a repository a wiki part whose visibility is set apart from its artifacts (R-AUTHZ-034). The documentation of an Ansible collection (T-19)
is wiki content, and so will be the documentation other formats grow. A route that answers the artifact `read` for such content would show it to a caller who may
install but not read.

**Decision.** A format lists exactly which of its routes, documents and fields are wiki content, and every one of them is served only after one call of the format
package, `wikiReadable`, which calls the wiki check of R-AUTHZ-034; the format neither decides the levels nor imports the authorization package. The surfaces are registered
in a registry that a test walks, so a surface added later cannot skip the call. A route that serves only wiki content passes the check's refusal on unchanged; a
document that embeds a wiki field leaves the field out. The Ansible list is [R-ANS-037](spec/formats/ansible.md#r-ans-037--the-documentation-is-wiki-content-which-routes-documents-and-fields-the-wiki-check-gates).

**Consequences.** Each format that adds documentation adds its list and a registry; the version document of a protocol stays an artifact document, so a client's
install never depends on the wiki level. The registry proves the surfaces it lists, not that it lists all (H-894).

**Alternatives considered.** The artifact `read` for documentation: leaks the wiki. A check at the dispatcher only: cannot gate a field inside a document. The format deciding levels: a second model beside T-18's.

**Revisit condition:** R-AUTHZ-034 changes what it asks of a format.

**Spec:** [spec/formats/ansible.md](spec/formats/ansible.md) R-ANS-037, Q-ANS-68, Q-ANS-69; [spec/authorization.md](spec/authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-034.

### ADR-196 · The Host gains a Markup capability for the rendering and sanitizing of a format's documentation

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** A format package may import neither the README renderer nor an HTML library (R-ARCH-008), yet the Galaxy's `docs-blob/` document, which the format serves, holds
HTML members, and an upstream's HTML is untrusted.

**Decision.** The contract's Host gains `Markup() Markup` with `Markdown(src) (html, truncated)` and `SanitizeHTML(html) string`. The composition root implements it over
`internal/packages/readme`, which gains `Renderer.SanitizeHTML`; the conformance kit's Host has a deterministic stand-in; a Host without a renderer returns a
`NoMarkup` whose calls return the empty string (and `Markdown` reports truncated), never the input; the two methods return no error, so the refusal
is an empty result and not an error value. The contract stays at its version and gains an addition only.

**Consequences.** One allowlist serves every surface; no format carries an HTML parser. A test that uses the stand-in proves wiring, not the policy (H-898).

**Alternatives considered.** A sanitizer inside the format: two policies. Serving Markdown only: not the Galaxy's shape. Widening `formatAllowed`: opens the rule for one package and pulls goldmark and bluemonday into every format.

**Revisit condition:** a second format needs more than Markdown and HTML sanitizing.

**Spec:** [spec/formats/ansible.md](spec/formats/ansible.md) R-ANS-039, Q-ANS-66; [spec/architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-008.

### ADR-191 · The format contract gains the route flag for the Galaxy `Token` scheme, and the hub token exchange is an optional interface of the remote adapter

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** `ansible-galaxy` sends a configured token as `Authorization: Token <token>` (verified in ansible-core 2.17.14 and 2.21.6), a scheme the authentication stage does not read; and a Galaxy-compatible hub behind single sign-on needs an offline token exchanged in a form body, which the remote adapter's token handshake (it receives the challenge, not the credential) cannot carry. Roles of the public Galaxy are GitHub archives that Galaxy does not store, so they are served by translation of a remote and never published.

**Decision.** The contract stays at version 3 and gains additions only: the route field `Route.TokenScheme` (with `auth.EndpointRules.TokenSchemeRoute` and the method label `galaxy_token`, wired like the NuGet API-key header: the scheme is read only on a route that declares it); and an optional interface of the remote adapter that receives the stored credential for one exchange, whose shape the package that builds the hub exchange decides and records. Collections are the format's stored artifact; roles exist on remote and virtual repositories only ([Q-ANS-4](spec/formats/ansible.md#q-ans-4--the-authorization-scheme-token-is-accepted-on-the-routes-that-declare-it), [Q-ANS-6](spec/formats/ansible.md#q-ans-6--roles-are-served-by-translation-from-a-remote-only-collections-are-the-stored-artifact), [Q-ANS-17](spec/formats/ansible.md#q-ans-17--the-hub-token-exchange-is-a-separate-optional-interface-built-after-the-core-class)).

**Consequences.** No existing format changes. The Galaxy format is written against the unchanged contract otherwise (`Discoverer`, `FillInspector`, `FactsGate`, `MirrorLister`, `VersionPather`, the importer's `Format`). The optional interface is `formats.CredentialExchanger` (`RemoteCaps.Exchange`, [Q-ANS-51](spec/formats/ansible.md#q-ans-51--the-hub-exchange-is-the-optional-interface-credentialexchanger-and-the-engine-sends-the-exchanged-token-and-never-the-credential)): `ExchangeRequest` receives the credential for the request to the realm, the engine (`internal/proxy/credential_exchange.go`) sends it under the host rule of R-REPO-033, caches the token and sends the upstream request with it in place of the credential.

### ADR-190 · The format contract gains the optional interface `ImageScanned` and a port of the Host for the block of an image pull

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** Images are the first content the scanning reads rather than matches by name (R-VULN-033). A format has no way to say that it takes part in the scanning without implementing the adapter that every OSV path reads, and a manifest pull is refused from the format's own handlers, where the digest is known.

**Decision.** The contract stays at version 3 and gains additions only: the optional interface `formats.ImageScanned` (`CapabilitiesOf` records it in `Capabilities.ImageScanned`), its catalog fact `Entry.ImageEcosystem`, the member `RefuseImage` of `formats.VulnerabilityData` (a service of the Host), and the value `advisory.EcosystemOCI` in the leaf the contract speaks in. See [Q-VULN-138](spec/vulnerability-scanning.md#q-vuln-138--the-pull-is-gated-in-the-registrys-handlers-by-the-digest-that-is-about-to-be-served) and [Q-VULN-141](spec/vulnerability-scanning.md#q-vuln-141--the-format-takes-part-through-an-optional-interface-of-its-own-not-the-adapter).

**Consequences.** No format changes; OCI implements the interface and calls the port.

### ADR-189 · The OCI conformance suite and the protocol criteria run against replicas of the whole application

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** R-OCI-035 asks for the specification's own conformance suite in all four categories, through a local and a virtual address, and for every protocol criterion of the format over HTTP. The suite
is an external test binary that speaks to an address; the criteria need several replicas with a request pinned to each. Finding F-88 asked that a test name carry an ID only for a criterion it proves.

**Decision.**

- `make oci-conformance` pins the tag once (`OCI_CONFORMANCE_TAG`), resolves it to the commit it points at because the conformance module has no tags of its own
  ([Q-OCI-210](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-210--the-conformance-suite-is-fetched-at-the-commit-its-tag-points-at)), downloads the module into `.out/oci-conformance/mod`, compiles it with the repository's Go
  (`GOTOOLCHAIN=local`) and runs `TestOCIConformance` (build tag `ociconformance`, so no integration run needs the binary and none has to skip). The test starts one replica on a fixed loopback address,
  runs the binary once through the local address and once through the virtual one, reads the JUnit reports, and fails on a failed or an undocumented skipped specification
  ([Q-OCI-211](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-211--the-conformance-suite-runs-all-four-categories-through-the-local-address-and-pull-push-and-discovery-through-the-virtual-address)).
- The suite found one defect, fixed on its own: the challenge of a mount named the target's `push` only, so a client that takes its scope from the challenge never got a token that could mount
  ([Q-OCI-212](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-212--the-challenge-of-a-mount-names-the-sources-pull-as-well-as-the-targets-push)).
- The protocol criteria run in `test/integration/oci` as subtests of one installation with three replicas ([Q-OCI-214](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-214--the-protocol-criteria-run-in-testintegrationoci-against-replicas-of-the-whole-application)),
  `TestR_AUTHZ_007_OCIActionMap` has a subtest per row of the OCI table, and a separate test runs the registry with Valkey unreachable.
- A test name carries a requirement ID when it proves a whole criterion of it ([Q-OCI-213](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-213--a-test-name-carries-the-id-of-a-requirement-when-it-proves-a-whole-acceptance-criterion-of-it)).

**Consequences.** CI runs the conformance suite in shard c of the integration job and uploads its reports. The coverage evidence record loses the two OCI requirements whose criteria only real clients prove (R-OCI-014, R-OCI-030) until
the e2e rows name them. The deletion path of a virtual repository is covered by its 405 test only (H-755).

**Alternatives considered.** Running the suite from a container image (a second Go toolchain); a delete through a virtual repository so that the category passes everywhere (reverses ADR-180); one area per criterion family.

**Revisit condition:** the project publishes `conformance/v*` tags; the owner wants a delete through a virtual repository; the e2e rows name R-OCI-014 and R-OCI-030.

**Spec:** [spec/formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md) R-OCI-035, Q-OCI-210 to Q-OCI-214.

### ADR-188 · The OCI e2e clients run privileged in a namespace of their own, and the kubelet row is served by a forwarder on the node

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** The e2e tier of R-OCI-035 needs the real Docker Engine with Buildx and Podman against the chart on kind. dockerd needs a privileged container; the namespace `quader` enforces Pod Security `restricted`. The row that starts a Kubernetes pod from a Quader repository is pulled by the node's containerd, which resolves neither the pod's forwarder nor the host port of the edge.

**Decision.** The client pods (`quader-e2e-oci-<i>`, one container `docker` with the pinned dind image and one `podman`) live in the namespace `quader-e2e-clients` with Pod Security `privileged` and nothing else in it. Their forwarder (the tool of the npm and NuGet client pods) makes `localhost:<edge port>` the registry host, as the setup snippets print it. For the kubelet row the harness puts a forwarder and the dev CA with a `hosts.toml` on the control-plane node, and `deploy/dev/kind.yaml` sets `config_path` of the node's containerd. The Docker Engine mirror row uses the further endpoint `ocimirror` of the dev profile (a bound host, anonymous requests, cache fill).

**Consequences.** A cluster created before this change has to be created again (`config_path`). The pods are a privilege footprint of the dev and CI clusters ([H-750](security/oci-registry.md#h-750--the-oci-client-pods-of-the-e2e-tier-are-privileged-and-the-dev-ca-is-added-to-a-nodes-containerd)). Both clients are pinned by digest in `tools/versions.env` and compared by the tests with the versions they run.

**Alternatives considered.** The runner's Docker daemon (Q-OCI-21 (b): shared with kind, certificates in the host's `/etc/docker`); an image host the node resolves (Q-OCI-200 (b)); the bound host as a host of the default endpoint (Q-OCI-201 (b): the host check would answer `421` to the other suites).

**Revisit condition:** the dev cluster's admission refuses the level `privileged`, or the dev cluster gets a registry host every node resolves.

**Spec:** [spec/formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md) R-OCI-035, Q-OCI-21, Q-OCI-200, Q-OCI-201; [developer/e2e.md](developer/e2e.md#the-oci-clients).

### ADR-182 · The OCI mirror stores through the host's artifact fill, and the engine counts versions

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** The OCI remote adapter can mirror (R-OCI-026, T-16 WP10). Its plan has to read the manifests an index names before it can name their blobs, an image is
many items per tag, and a tag costs a manifest request that Docker Hub counts against an allowance. `discover.Upstream.Artifact` was a stub (not_implemented),
`SelectItems` counted items, and the plan could not know the bounds the engine would apply afterwards.

**Decision.** `Artifact` is built in the format-neutral host (`MirrorHost.fillPath`, shared with `Fill`): the artifact goes through the format's gate and the remote engine as a
background request of the pass, a stored one costs no request, an upstream 404 is found=false, and what the call stored is reported to the package's tally through the plan's
context (`mirror.ReportStored`, Q-ARCH-415). The engine's `SelectItems` counts versions (an item's `Version` is its unit), the fill skips a path it has filled in the attempt
(Q-REPO-295). The Upstream the engine lends implements the optional `discover.Bounded`, which a plan reads with `discover.BoundsOf` (Q-OCI-182). The frozen contract gains
that one optional interface (the contract file is regenerated, `ContractVersion` stays 3); the APT builders reuse `Artifact` and `Bounded` for the Debian indexes. The settings
member `<format>.mirror` is kept from an Owner like the patterns (Q-OCI-22, Q-REPO-295).

**Consequences.** Every mirror test of npm and NuGet is unchanged (one item per version there). A format whose plan reads documents that are artifacts (an index, a Debian
`Packages` file) uses `Artifact` and is counted by the pass for what it stored.

**Alternatives considered.** A required method on `Upstream` and a callback on `Artifact` (every implementer and fake changes); a plan of tag-level items with a second round trip to the
format for the blobs (a new type and a second call between engine and format); planning every tag and dropping in the engine (a first pass reads every selected tag).

**Revisit condition:** a second format needs the engine to see a plan's per-version items before the format reads them.

**Spec:** [spec/formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md) Mirror discovery, Q-OCI-180, Q-OCI-182; [spec/architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-008, Q-ARCH-415;
[spec/repositories-and-proxy.md](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-050, R-REPO-051, Q-REPO-295.

### ADR-177 · The format contract gains the optional ViewSizer for the size of a version that is not the sum of its files

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** Finding F-86 (2026-11-08): the package view computes a version's `sizeBytes` as the sum of its linked file items. An OCI
tag links its lead item only, the manifest document, so the list of versions showed a few hundred bytes for an image of tens of MiB.
The format knows the size (the rows of R-OCI-007); the core cannot. The format contract is frozen at version 2 (ADR-141, R-ARCH-025):
every change is an ADR, and a new behaviour is an optional interface, never a new case of an existing method.

**Decision.** `formats.ViewSizer` is an optional interface of a `Format`: `ViewSizes(ctx, ports, []ViewVersion)` returns the size the
screens show as the version's `sizeBytes`, by version id, in one call for a page. `CapabilitiesOf` finds it and `Capabilities.ViewSizer`
records it; the package view asks a format only when it has it (`view.Sizer`, which only the bridge of such a format implements), once
for a page of the version list after the cut and once for the version details. `ViewData`, `ViewFields` and the view adapters of
npm and NuGet are unchanged, and `ContractVersion` stays 3 (the upload sessions' Finalize raised it, ADR-178). The conformance kit gains a check: a `ViewSizer` answers only for the ids
it was asked for, with sizes not below zero, in one call. OCI implements it (Q-OCI-130).

**Consequences.** A format whose versions are not their files adds the one method; a format without it is never called. The version
rows and the sizes are read in separate transactions, so a tag deleted between the two reads, or re-pushed so that its version row is replaced,
shows the sum of its files in that one answer.

**Alternatives considered.** A new `ViewFields` case and a `ViewData.SizeBytes` member: an existing method would gain a case that
every adapter has to know, and the unchanged adapters would be called for it. A size stored on the version row: a second copy of what
the manifest rows hold (Q-OCI-130).

**Revisit condition:** a second format reports a size that needs more than the version's id and name.

**Spec:** [spec/architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-008, R-ARCH-025; [spec/formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md) R-OCI-031, Q-OCI-130.

### ADR-175 · The upload and mount handlers hold the protocol, and the host holds the session and the link

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** The host's upload-session port (ADR-162) and `Ingestor.Link` by source name (Q-OCI-27) left the OCI routes to build: the blob upload protocol of
the distribution specification and the cross-repository mount. Both are security-relevant: a session id continues an upload, and a mount reaches bytes in
a repository by naming it.

**Decision.**

- The handlers (`handlers_upload.go`, `handlers_mount.go`) hold the protocol and no state. Every session call passes the image name of the path as the
  binding; the host answers `404 BLOB_UPLOAD_UNKNOWN` for a session of another principal, repository or name, and the handlers read no session by its id
  alone. An id that is no UUID names no session. A monolithic `POST` is the upload pipeline's spool and commit; the finalize of a session is the port's.
- A mount is `Ingestor.Link` from `<source name>/_blobs/<digest>` of the repository `oci.MountSource` names, after `deploy` on the target. Whatever the link
  answers `NotFound`, and whatever `from` does not name an image, is the answer of a request without `from`: a session and 202
  ([Q-OCI-110](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-110--a-mount-that-cannot-be-served-opens-a-session-and-says-nothing-more-and-one-function-parses-its-source)).
- The 416 of an offset mismatch is rendered from the port's typed received count ([Q-OCI-111](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-111--a-chunks-content-range-is-read-strictly-and-a-416-carries-the-range-the-session-holds)); a monolithic digest mismatch is `DIGEST_INVALID`
  ([Q-OCI-112](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-112--a-monolithic-upload-compares-the-digest-after-the-spool-and-answers-400-digest_invalid)).
- The link refuses a source of another format and decides the read of its source as a read is decided (patterns, the refusal of a claimed name, the routing and the per-member check of a virtual
  source); `Finalize` takes the offset of the last bytes and checks it under the session's claim; a blob upload, a monolithic upload and a mount ask the ownership rule without a publish
  ([Q-OCI-115](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-115--blob-uploads-and-mounts-ask-the-ownership-rule-without-a-publish-before-a-body-is-read)); a session is decided on the package's document path ([Q-OCI-116](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-116--a-session-is-decided-on-the-packages-document-path)).
- The frozen contract changes in one place, [ADR-178](#adr-178--the-upload-sessions-finalize-takes-an-offset-and-reports-the-received-count-and-the-contract-is-at-version-3).
- The commit hook of the format refuses a blob item whose content is not the digest in its path
  ([Q-OCI-113](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-113--a-blob-item-must-hold-the-content-its-digest-names-checked-by-the-commit-hook)): a mount links the source's bytes unread, and the
  source may be any repository's path.
- The registry token's `pull` on the source is the registry root's check, with the repository and name that `oci.MountSource` returns
  ([Q-OCI-114](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-114--the-grant-on-the-source-of-a-mount-is-the-registry-roots-check-the-read-right-is-the-hosts-link)).

**Consequences.** The handlers work at `/api/oci/` in tests and at `/v2/` once the root is mounted, with no change. A mount through a registry token is limited by the token's `pull` scope on the source
by the root's enforcement point, which reads `from` with the same function and the same bound repository (`EndpointFacts.BoundRepo`, an addition to the contract). A mount
costs one transaction and no bytes.

**Alternatives considered.** A 404 for an unreadable source (a disclosure or a client error); the handler reading the registry grant (a layer violation); a blob check in the mount handler only
(a later road would repeat the gap).

**Revisit condition:** a supported client treats the 202 fallback of a mount as an error, or a second format needs a mount.

**Spec:** [spec/formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md) R-OCI-011, R-OCI-012, Q-OCI-110 to Q-OCI-115.

### ADR-178 · The upload sessions' Finalize takes an offset and reports the received count, and the contract is at version 3

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** The first build of the OCI upload handlers checked the `Content-Range` of a final `PUT` against a separate read of the session and then appended at the end of whatever the session held,
so a request between the two moved the end and ruined the upload. The check belongs where `Append`'s is: under the session's claim, in the statement that takes it. [ADR-141](#adr-141--the-format-contract-is-frozen-at-version-1) says
that a changed signature or an argument that gains a rule raises `ContractVersion` and is an ADR of its own.

**Decision.** `UploadSessions.Finalize` gains the argument `offset int64` (the received count the bytes of `last` start at; `-1` appends at the end, the behaviour of version 2), decided under the claim. A
finalize at another count is an error of kind `RangeNotSatisfiable` as for `Append`, and the received count comes back with it, in the new field `Committed.Received` (zero otherwise), so that the
format renders the `Range` of the 416 from a typed value ([Q-OCI-111](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-111--a-chunks-content-range-is-read-strictly-and-a-416-carries-the-range-the-session-holds)). `uploads.Service.Finalize` and `uploads.Result` carry the same.
`ContractVersion` is 3; the surface file and the contract blocks of R-ARCH-008/009 are regenerated.

`EndpointFacts` gains the field `BoundRepo qname.Repo` (an addition: the zero value is an unbound host, and `Bound` stays the bool it was). `Bound` says that a host is bound; it cannot say to which
repository, and on a host bound to a virtual repository the request's repository of a write is the deployment target, not the repository the client's names (the `from` of a mount) are relative to. The dispatcher
sets `BoundRepo` from the match in `serveRoute`, so the format's handler and the registry root's enforcement point read the same repository; `Bound` is derived from it.

**What breaks.** (`BoundRepo` breaks nothing.) Every implementation of `formats.UploadSessions` and every caller of `Finalize`: the host (`internal/formathost`), the conformance kit's host (`formattest`) and the OCI handlers, which are all in this
repository. No other format has upload sessions, so no format changes its `ContractVersion` literal (they use the constant).

**Consequences.** A final chunk is held to the same offset rule as every other chunk, on every replica, without a second read. The 416 of a finalize needs no later read of the session.

**Alternatives considered.** Keeping version 2 and reading the session after the refusal (the first build: the count is a later fact and the check is racy); a new method `FinalizeAt` next to `Finalize` (two ways to finish, one of which is wrong).

**Revisit condition:** a second format with upload sessions needs a different shape of the final chunk.

**Spec:** [spec/formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md) R-OCI-011, Q-OCI-111; [spec/architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-008, R-ARCH-009, R-ARCH-025.
### ADR-174 · The format contract names the file of a version, decides many paths at once and gives formats the versions a caller may read

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** Finding F-83 (2026-11-08, the penetration test of the F-82 fix): a path pattern finer than a package's folder hid
a version's file and left what the file holds in the package's documents, the search and the package screens, and a write was
decided on one path while it wrote or removed several files (H-647, H-646, H-586). The decision point decided every question
about a package on the package document's path and had no path for a version's file; a format could not ask which versions a
caller may read without a listing scope, and could decide many paths only one `Authorize` at a time, each recorded and audited.
The format contract is frozen, at version 3 (ADR-141, ADR-178, R-ARCH-025): every change of it is an ADR.

**Decision.** Additions, so `ContractVersion` stays 3:

- `formats.VersionPather`, an optional interface `CapabilitiesOf` finds (`Capabilities.VersionPath`): the canonical path of
  the file that holds a version's content. npm answers the tarball, NuGet the `.nupkg`. `formats.CatalogEntry` carries it as
  `catalog.Entry.VersionPath`, and the decision point decides a version on that path as well as on the package document's
  ([Q-AUTHZ-255](spec/authorization.md#q-authz-255--a-version-is-decided-on-its-files-path-as-well-as-on-the-package-documents-and-every-place-that-shows-a-package-shows-only-the-versions-the-caller-may-read)).
- `formats.ReadScope.VersionsByPath`: whether the caller's own grants decide a package's versions one by one (a grant, the
  token scope or a CI contribution with a path pattern). The host implements it from `authz.ReadScope.VersionsByPath`.
- `formats.CallerVersions`, `formats.VersionView` (`Version`, `Hidden`), `formats.LiveVersions` and
  `formats.HiddenFingerprint`: the contract's service over the read scope that a format filters a document with. It is nil for
  a caller without path patterns; `LiveVersions` keeps a package's version list per revision in the rendition cache.
- The writes use `formats.Host.PathsAllowed`, the listing form of `Authorize` for many paths that ADR-168 added (Q-OCI-76), to
  decide the files of a removal without an audit event; this ADR adds nothing to it ([Q-AUTHZ-256](spec/authorization.md#q-authz-256--a-write-is-decided-on-every-file-it-writes-or-removes-whether-or-not-the-file-is-there-and-a-version-the-caller-may-not-read-is-not-the-callers-to-change)).
- Kit check 13 gains a fifth rule: a package document is served again on its seeded Host, with an unrelated path refused (the
  answer must not change) and with one version's file refused (the version must be gone from the answer), and `VersionPath`
  must classify to the package and the version; the test format gains `VersionPath` and the defects `lists-hidden-versions`,
  `filters-differently` (the control run) and `versions-outside-rows` (a fixture that judges no version).

The frozen surface file is regenerated with `go test ./internal/formats -run TestR_ARCH_025 -update-contract`.

**Consequences.** A format whose versions have a file implements `VersionPather` and filters its documents with
`CallerVersions`, or kit check 13 fails it; the rule is mandatory for every format whose fixture places a path in a version, and
OCI names its tag path (Q-AUTHZ-258). A format without `VersionPather` decides versions on the document's path, as before.
The kit's host answers `Resolver().ReadScope` from its `Allow` function (`formattest.Resolver`), so a test's resolver that does
not answer the read scope itself embeds it.

**Alternatives considered.** A required `Format` method for the version's path (raises `ContractVersion` and moves every
format); a host-level flag beside `PathsAllowed` instead of `ReadScope.VersionsByPath` (two questions where the read scope
already holds the classification); filtering in the core (the core does not know a document's structure).

**Revisit condition:** a format's version keeps content a document shows in more than one file, or the remote and virtual
documents get per-caller filtering (H-655).

**Spec:** [spec/authorization.md](spec/authorization.md) Q-AUTHZ-255, Q-AUTHZ-256; [spec/architecture.md](spec/architecture.md)
R-ARCH-008, R-ARCH-010, R-ARCH-027; [spec/formats/npm.md](spec/formats/npm.md) Q-NPM-82, Q-NPM-83;
[spec/formats/nuget.md](spec/formats/nuget.md) Q-NUGET-120, Q-NUGET-121; [spec/endpoints.md](spec/endpoints.md) Q-EP-85.

### ADR-180 · The OCI write routes serve the class virtual and the handler resolves the deployment target

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** The dispatcher answers a write to a virtual repository by replacing the request's repository with the deployment target (R-REPO-021): a route that does not
serve the class virtual is redirected, and the request then carries no addressed repository. For OCI that drops what R-OCI-011 asks the session to record (the repository the
client addressed) and makes the `Location` of a session and of a blob name the target's address, so a client that follows it talks to the target (H-663). A delete is a write
as well, so it would have been carried to the target, where the spec says 405 (R-OCI-028).

**Decision.**

- The write routes of the OCI format (manifest put, the five upload routes) and the two delete routes serve the classes local and virtual. The dispatcher no longer redirects them;
  the handler asks `Resolver().DeployTarget` ([writeRequest](../internal/formats/oci/virtual_write.go)) and decides and commits on a request made for the target
  (`Request.WriteTarget`), and calls the upload sessions with the request for the addressed repository, whose session records both. Every `Location` is built for the addressed
  repository.
- The delete handlers answer 405 `UNSUPPORTED` for the class virtual ([Q-OCI-165](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-165--a-delete-through-a-virtual-repository-is-refused-by-the-handler)).
- No change of the frozen contract, the dispatcher or the host: `uploadTarget` already accepted a virtual repository, and the descriptor lists the class.

**Consequences.** npm and NuGet keep the redirect. The format owns the resolution of the target for its write routes, so a new write route of the format must call `writeRequest`
(the checklist in [developer/oci.md](developer/oci.md)). The decision point still decides the write on the target before the handler runs
([Q-OCI-166](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-166--a-write-through-a-virtual-repository-without-a-deploy-target-is-refused-by-the-decision-point-before-the-handler)).

**Alternatives considered.** The dispatcher keeps the addressed repository on a redirect for every format (a field or a flag on the request; it changes how npm and NuGet writes are
decided, Q-AUTHZ-163); a route flag that asks the dispatcher to keep it (a change of the frozen route type for one format).

**Revisit condition:** a second format needs the addressed repository on a write through a virtual repository.

**Spec:** [spec/formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md) R-OCI-011, R-OCI-027, R-OCI-028, Q-OCI-160 to Q-OCI-166; [spec/repositories-and-proxy.md](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-021.

### ADR-184 · The Debian virtual build reuses the remote class's job code through a field of the indexer

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** A virtual build asks the remote engine for a member's release and index exactly as the remote class's jobs do: through the background upstream, with the verification
and the anti-rollback rules of R-DEB-019 and R-DEB-020, and the bounded reads of the parse.

**Decision.**

- `Indexer` has a field `Remote *RemoteJobs`, the value the composition root already builds for the remote class (ADR-187), and the virtual build calls its `repo`, `fetchRelease` and `fetchIndex` and reads its store.
- A replica that does not run the remote jobs has the field nil, and a virtual build there fails a remote member with `member_unavailable` instead of merging without it.
- The merge itself (`index.MergeMember`) is a leaf function; the virtual adapter's `Merge` of the contract uses the same function.

**Consequences.** One implementation of what a remote member's release is; a change of the verification reaches the virtual build with the remote class. The build of a virtual repository
depends on the remote class's package-private methods, which is allowed inside `internal/formatdata/deb`.

**Alternatives considered.** A copy of the release reader in the virtual build (two verifiers that drift); an interface in the format package (a seam with one implementation).

**Revisit condition:** a second class of the format needs the remote jobs.

**Spec:** R-DEB-025, R-DEB-026, Q-DEB-64.

### ADR-185 · The Debian format registers a repository hook that enqueues the builds a change of a repository calls for

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** R-DEB-026 asks for a build of a virtual repository when its members, pin rules or settings change, and when a member that a remote's keys or patterns concern changes, in the
transaction of the change. The repository service calls `repository.Hooks.OnUpdated` in that transaction, and an app-level hook list already exists (`authz.NewPolicyHook`, `ownershipHook`).

**Decision.**

- `debRepositoryHook` joins the list in `wire_repository.go`. For a Debian repository it enqueues `deb-index` (key `index:<id>`, no delay) for the virtual repository itself, or, for a local or remote repository, for every virtual repository that lists it.
- The creation hook of the format enqueues the first build of a virtual repository after its key exists.
- `OnDelete` does nothing: the rows go with the repository.

**Consequences.** No change of the repository service. A claims change has no hook (Q-DEB-65, H-725).

**Alternatives considered.** A hook seam for claims in the service (a change of the repository package for one format); polling the document (a window).

**Revisit condition:** a second format builds an index for a virtual repository by job.

**Spec:** R-DEB-026, Q-DEB-68.

### ADR-186 · A route that serves every class has one handler per class

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** The format's `Match` is blind to the class (Q-DEB-45), so `deb.dists.get`, `deb.dists.by_hash` and `deb.pool.get` serve the local, remote and virtual class. Three packages of one feature build the handlers of those routes in parallel.

**Decision.**

- `registerHandler(route, build)` registers the handler of the local and virtual classes, as before; `registerRemoteHandler(route, build)` the handler of the remote class.
- `handlerFor` composes them: a request addressed to a remote repository goes to the remote handler, every other to the shared one, and a route with neither answers 501.
- The routes of a flat repository are the remote class's alone and use `registerHandler`.

**Consequences.** No file of another package changes when the remote class lands, and the route table stays frozen (T-17's plan, 2.5).

**Alternatives considered.** One shared handler per route registered by two packages (a panic at start-up); a class switch inside the local handlers (edits another package's files).

**Revisit condition:** a second route table per class (Q-DEB-45 forbids it).

**Spec:** R-DEB-003, Q-DEB-45.

### ADR-187 · The jobs of the Debian remote class run on the worker roles and find their runtime at run time

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** The parse of an index, the re-verification and the housekeeping need the background upstream and the item store, which exist only in a process that runs jobs and are built after the job registry is frozen.

**Decision.**

- The handlers registered for `deb-remote-parse` and for the remote's `deb-index` are `late` values of the composition root, set where the format data ports are wired on a replica that claims jobs (`startDebRemote`).
- The remote part of the task `deb-index-refresh` is a refresh hook registered by the composition root.
- A job claimed before the value is set fails and is retried, as the other late handlers do.

**Consequences.** The same shape as the OCI sweep and the NuGet recomputation; nothing is claimed by a replica that cannot run it.

**Alternatives considered.** A package-level runtime (R-ARCH-032 forbids the state); running the parse in the web role (it holds a transaction for the length of a parse).

**Revisit condition:** a second job role.

**Spec:** R-DEB-021, R-DEB-023.

### ADR-176 · The OCI remote adapter works inside the contract and adds a catalog fact and an optional interface

**Status:** Decided by the development agent — owner review at the walkthrough.

**Context.** ADR-161 and ADR-165 gave the engine the token handshake and the revalidation by `HEAD`; the remote adapter of the OCI format
(R-OCI-021 to R-OCI-025) is what implements them. Its checks need the response headers where the hooks have the body and the body where the hooks have the
headers (the digest a tag announces, the cut of a tags list, the media type of a fetched manifest), and its upstream test meets an answer the generic probe
reads wrongly (a registry's `401` with a Bearer challenge).

**Decision.**

- The contract stays at version 2. The checks that need both read a body through a reader that `AcceptResponse` may put around it (it may wrap the body, and when
  the wrapper changes the length it drops the announced one, [Q-OCI-126](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-126--the-wrapper-that-records-the-cut-of-a-tags-list-drops-the-announced-length)), and a manifest is read as
  the type its own `mediaType` member names ([Q-OCI-120](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-120--the-digest-a-tag-announces-is-checked-by-a-reader-around-the-response-body),
  [Q-OCI-122](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-122--a-stored-tags-list-records-that-the-upstream-cut-it), [Q-OCI-121](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-121--the-rows-of-a-remotes-manifest-are-written-by-onfill-for-a-tag-and-by-oncommit-for-a-digest)).
- A stood `401` is read by the optional interface `StoodChallengeReader` of the `Authenticator`: `insufficient_scope` is a missing image ([Q-OCI-127](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-127--a-stood-401-with-insufficient_scope-is-a-missing-image-and-keeps-the-remembered-challenge)).
- The catalog gains one fact, `Facts.ProbeChallengeReachable`, an addition to the surface file of the contract, and `Register` checks it
  ([Q-REPO-280](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-280--the-upstream-test-reads-a-bearer-challenge-of-a-handshake-format-as-reachable)).
- The rows of a remote's manifests are written by `OnFill` and by `OnCommit` from the inspection; referrers and the windows of the tags list beyond the stored
  document are passed through, filtered for the caller ([Q-OCI-123](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-123--referrers-of-a-remote-are-filtered-here-for-the-caller-and-for-artifacttype)).
- The default extra hosts of Docker Hub are the realm; the CDN host that was seen is not listed, because `extraHosts` do not gate redirects ([Q-OCI-125](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-125--extrahosts-do-not-gate-redirects-so-the-docker-hub-defaults-list-the-realm-only)).
- A remote that cannot ask its upstream answers with what it stores ([Q-OCI-128](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-128--a-remote-that-cannot-ask-its-upstream-answers-with-what-it-stores)); the `library/` mapping is Docker Hub's itself ([Q-OCI-129](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-129--the-library-mapping-is-for-docker-hub-itself-and-a-read-is-decided-on-both-spellings-of-the-name)); the probe of the registry root is at the host ([Q-REPO-281](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md#q-repo-281--the-probe-of-the-registry-root-format-is-at-the-root-of-the-host)).
- A read of a Docker Hub remote is decided on both spellings of its name through the existing `PathsAllowed`, and the optional `SourceSpeller` gives a mount's source the other spelling
  ([Q-OCI-129](spec/formats/oci.md#q-oci-129--the-library-mapping-is-for-docker-hub-itself-and-a-read-is-decided-on-both-spellings-of-the-name)); `RemoteCaps` gains `Stood`, and `Register` refuses a `StoodChallengeReader` without an `Authenticator`.

**Consequences.** No format changes. The stored tags list of a remote carries one member of the format's own. A refused tag raises the engine's integrity event. A read of a Docker Hub remote is decided on both spellings of its name, and the contract gains the optional `SourceSpeller` for the source of a mount (`Capabilities.SourceSpeller`, Q-OCI-129); one request costs at most eight upstream pages of a tags list (Q-OCI-150).

**Alternatives considered.** An additive optional interface that gives the format the response headers (an addition keeps the contract version, Q-ARCH-284; open, taken
when a second format needs it); a handshake in the probe (a request to a second host in a test of one resource); a heuristic for a cut tags list; the engine reading
`insufficient_scope` itself (registry knowledge in the engine).

**Revisit condition:** a second format needs the headers in `PrepareFill`, or the probe is to judge the credential.

**Spec:** [spec/formats/oci.md](spec/formats/oci.md) R-OCI-020 to R-OCI-025, Q-OCI-120 to Q-OCI-129; [spec/repositories-and-proxy.md](spec/repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-024, Q-REPO-280, Q-REPO-281;
[spec/architecture.md](spec/architecture.md) R-ARCH-008.

## Decisions by the development agent

This index lists every decided question: one row for each block `### Q-<AREA>-<n> · <title>` on the
[specification pages](spec/README.md) and on [coverage/roadmap.md](coverage/roadmap.md#decisions). The block on its
page holds the options, the choice, the rationale and what the choice changed; the row repeats the block's title, the
value of its status line (who decided it, and when the owner did), what it chose and the entries of this log that the
block names or that name the question. Most were selected by the development agent from the options the block
documents, and the owner reviews them at the walkthrough; the status says where the owner, a planner or a builder
decided instead, and where a decision was superseded.

The index is generated from the blocks by `go run ./internal/tools/coverage` (also `make coverage`), ordered by area and
then by number, and `go run ./internal/tools/coverage -check` fails when a block has no row, a row has no block, or a
row no longer matches its block. A question is added, changed or revisited on its page only; the generator writes its
row. A conflict between two branches in the generated part is resolved by running the generator on the merged tree.

| [Q-STOR-254](spec/storage.md#q-stor-254--the-names-the-start-check-and-the-reads-give-their-findings) | The names the start check and the reads give their findings | Decided by the builder | (a) `capabilities.serverSideCopyFrom` maps the id of each other connection on the same endpoint to the result, with `checkedAt` beside the four flags of R-STOR-061; the reasons are `not_found`, `unavailable` (a transient error or an open circuit) and `size`; `check` exits `5` when a check that is not optional failed and `2` for a usage or configuration error, and a missing capability is reported `absent`, not failed | [ADR-239](#adr-239--several-object-store-connections-every-blob-on-every-connection-a-row-per-copy-one-reconciliation-and-a-scrub-per-copy) |

| [Q-STOR-257](spec/storage.md#q-stor-257--the-pass-queues-a-gap-only-where-another-connection-holds-the-blob-starts-hourly-or-at-once-while-a-connection-fills-and-keeps-its-position-in-a-row-of-its-own) | The pass queues a gap only where another connection holds the blob, starts hourly or at once while a connection fills, and keeps its position in a row of its own | Decided by the builder | (a) A gap is a live blob without a present copy on a connection with `drain: false` while another connection holds a present copy; a full pass starts when a target has never ended one, is filling with an empty queue (the last pass's gaps are copied), or the last ended an hour ago; the positions of the pass and of the drains are the row `storage_reconcile_state` of `system_state`, written after every batch | [ADR-239](#adr-239--several-object-store-connections-every-blob-on-every-connection-a-row-per-copy-one-reconciliation-and-a-scrub-per-copy) |
| [Q-STOR-258](spec/storage.md#q-stor-258--five-reasons-of-a-failure-a-queue-row-without-a-source-anywhere-is-deleted-and-a-target-whose-circuit-opened-during-the-run-spends-no-attempt) | Five reasons of a failure, a queue row without a source anywhere is deleted, and a target whose circuit opened during the run spends no attempt | Decided by the builder | (a) The reasons `no_source` (no other connection the worker reaches holds a present copy), `unavailable` (a transient error or an open circuit at the target or at every source, or the insert bound after every write), `source_damaged` (every source that answered was marked missing or corrupt), `refused` (the target's answer that retrying soon does not fix) and `claimed` (the target's row is claimed by an unfinished drain); a row whose blob has no present copy anywhere is deleted; a write that the target's breaker refused leaves its row as it is | [ADR-239](#adr-239--several-object-store-connections-every-blob-on-every-connection-a-row-per-copy-one-reconciliation-and-a-scrub-per-copy) |
| [Q-STOR-259](spec/storage.md#q-stor-259--the-drain-walks-every-copy-it-has-not-claimed-reads-the-survivors-again-under-the-blobs-lock-finishes-its-own-claims-and-a-draining-connection-is-no-longer-filled) | The drain walks every copy it has not claimed, reads the survivors again under the blob's lock, finishes its own claims, and a draining connection is no longer filled | Decided by the builder | (a) The walk takes every copy of D that is not `deleting`, by object name; the claim locks the blob as a mark does and checks again that every target holds a present copy and one is verified within its period; a claim on a live blob older than `handover_delay` is taken over by a compare-and-set of its time at the next run's start and finished; a walk that deleted or queued nothing is followed by the next after the pass interval; `drain: true` clears `filled_at`, a pass clears `drained_at` of its targets; the drained check runs at the end of each walk and at a run's start | [ADR-239](#adr-239--several-object-store-connections-every-blob-on-every-connection-a-row-per-copy-one-reconciliation-and-a-scrub-per-copy) |

| [Q-VULN-122](spec/vulnerability-scanning.md#q-vuln-122--a-rejection-is-counted-per-ecosystem-and-alerted-a-changed-limit-and-an-adapter-version-take-effect-without-a-new-archive-and-the-sources-api-keeps-the-last-full-syncs-count) | A rejection is counted per ecosystem and alerted, a changed limit and an adapter version take effect without a new archive, and the sources API keeps the last full sync's count | Decided by the development agent | (b), with these decisions: the series of every result the alerts read are created at 0 for every configured ecosystem when the service is built, because `increase()` does not see a counter that first appears with a value (the one miss left is a rejection within the first scrape interval after a process starts); the warning alert reads the bounds of one entry only (`rejected`), the critical one `MAL-` records of either cause (`rejected_malicious`: a `MAL-` record that fails validation keeps its stored row just as one above the bound does), and validation failures (`invalid`) alert only as a burst, `QuaderVulnerabilityRecordsInvalid`: at least ten in 24 hours and more than 1 % of the records processed in that time (`written`, `skipped`, `rejected`, `invalid`), so that a record now and then does not fire it; above 1 % of one archive the 1 % guard fails the full sync; the counts are written when the log of a run's rejections is finished, so every full and incremental path counts, also one that ends on an error; the sources API returns `fullRejected` beside `rejected`; the "unchanged" answers and the incremental run are skipped when the configured limit differs from `record_limit` and the last full sync rejected anything (`full_rejected > 0`), and a sync that rejected nothing is not repeated for a new limit (a record that only an incremental run rejected since the last full sync is not read again for a raised limit until the next full sync, because `limitChanged` reads `full_rejected`); a full sync logs, at `WARN` and capped like the rejection log, the rows of an older adapter that it kept, and counts none of them as written. | — |
